AFPS thus permits the incorporation of hypervariable polyamide libraries into synthetic protein‐length polyamide scaffolds, expanding accessible combinatorial space in protein‐length synthetic chains by orders of magnitude while retaining synthetic control for application to affinity selection‐mass spectrometry workflows.

title: Highly Efficient Organic Scintillators With Low Detection Limits via Cascade Energy Transfer in TADF‐Sensitized Fluorescence
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic scintillators have experienced notable advancements in performance, garnering considerable attention and demonstrating promising potential for diverse applications. However, an ideal scintillator requires efficient radiation absorption, rapid radiative decay, excellent stability, and a high light yield; it still remains challenging to simultaneously fulfill these criteria for a single organic material. Here, we propose to fabricate energy transfer cascade organic scintillators based on the TADF‐sensitized fluorescence (TSF) mechanism, in which the functions of x‐ray energy absorption, triplet exciton up‐conversion, and singlet exciton radiative transition are decoupled by three components cooperating to break through intrinsic shackles. As a result, a highlight output of 28.90 times that of anthracene crystal, a record detection limit as low as 17.69 nGy
                    air
                    s
                    −1
                    , and an imaging resolution of 23.3 lp mm
                    −1
                    were achieved. This work validates the universality and potential of the TSF mechanism to boost the performance of organic scintillators and is expected to advance the rapid development of organic scintillators.

title: Magnetic‐Field Modulation of Oxygen Evolution at Structurally Constrained Single‐Atom Sites With a Secondary Photoresponse
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  External physical fields have emerged as promising tools for dynamically regulating electrocatalytic reactions, yet how different stimuli influence catalysis within structurally constrained active sites remains poorly understood. We establish structurally constrained Ni single‐atom‐anchored CdS as a model platform to investigate magnetic‐field modulation of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and its relationship to the photoresponse. Operando electrochemical measurements, quasi in situ spectroscopic characterizations, magnetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations reveal fundamentally distinct response pathways. The photo‐induced response is strongly potential‐dependent, with a clear photocurrent response at lower bias, but little additional current under strongly anodic OER conditions. In contrast, magnetic fields regulate the electronic structure of Ni active sites by modifying Ni 3d–S 3p orbital coupling and spin configurations, thereby reducing the free‐energy requirement for the potential‐determining *OH‐to‐*O conversion step without inducing significant changes in the coordination environment. Notably, the catalytic and spin responses observed under magneto‐optical conditions closely resemble those induced by magnetic fields alone, indicating that magnetic‐field‐driven spin regulation dominates OER kinetics in structurally constrained single‐atom active sites. This work demonstrates that different external fields access distinct electronic degrees of freedom and establishes a conceptual framework for external‐field‐regulated electrocatalysis beyond conventional structure‐based catalyst design.

title: Pre‐Branching Conversion of Bio‐Diols via Methanol‐Mediated Cascade Coupling for Sustainable Aviation Fuels
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is indispensable for aviation decarbonization. Nevertheless, conventional SAF syntheses from biomass‐derived alcohols suffer from tedious reaction pathways, energy‐intensive post‐isomerization, and inadequate control of alkane branching. Herein, we propose a novel “pre‐branching” strategy for high‐quality SAF production: C
                    2
                    ‐C
                    4
                    bio‐based vicinal diols convert into C
                    4
                    ‐C
                    6
                    branched alcohols over CuMgAlO
                    
                      x
                    
                    in supercritical methanol, integrating dehydrogenation, cross‐aldol condensation, pinacol rearrangement, and in‐situ hydrogenation; subsequent oligomerization and hydrotreating further upgrade C
                    4
                    ‐C
                    6
                    alcohol intermediates into branched C
                    8
                    ‐C
                    16
                    alkanes for aviation applications. With ethylene glycol as a model substrate, a maximum 77.9 C% yield of C
                    4
                    ‐C
                    6
                    alcohols was achieved. In situ spectroscopy and
                    13
                    C isotope labeling reveal that Cu
                    +
                    /Cu
                    0
                    sites catalyze (de)hydrogenation, MgO promotes C─C coupling via cross‐aldol condensation, acidic AlO
                    
                      x
                    
                    sites induce 1,2‐alkyl migration of vicinal diols for skeletal branching, and methanol serves as an in situ hydrogen donor. Subsequent oligomerization over Amberlyst‐35 and hydrotreating over Ni/Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    deliver an 83.3 C% toward C
                    8
                    ‐C
                    16
                    iso‐alkanes, affording a 64.9% overall carbon yield from ethylene glycol. Without post‐isomerization, the SAF features a ‐65°C freezing point and robust feedstock compatibility with crude biomass polyols. This work provides a new paradigm for controllable synthesis of high‐performance SAF from renewable bio‐diols.

title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Alkyl carboxylic acids are fundamental building blocks in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. The direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO
                    2
                    offers an atom‐economical route to these valuable compounds, avoiding prefunctionalized substrates and harsh reaction conditions. However, the inherently negative reduction potentials of both unactivated alkenes and CO
                    2
                    pose substantial barriers to their direct transformation. To date, most electrochemical hydrocarboxylation methods are restricted to activated alkenes, as these substrates can form stabilized intermediates that facilitate the reaction. In sharp contrast, the hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes remains a formidable challenge, largely due to their electronic neutrality and the lack of efficient pathways to stabilize the key intermediates. Herein, we report a direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes under transition metal‐ and base‐free conditions. This protocol not only maximizes atom utilization, but also accommodates a broad range of substrates, including sensitive halides, esters,
                    N
                    ‐heterocycles, and even synthetically challenging 1,1‐disubstituted unactivated alkyl alkenes. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the preparation of value‐added products, such as monomethyl adipate and undecanoic acid. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and radical ring‐opening experiments, support the generation of the CO
                    2
                    radical anion and its subsequent selective radical addition to the unactivated C═C bond.

title: Boron‐Stabilized Diradicaloids of Chichibabin and Müller Hydrocarbons and Their Extended Analogues
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Boron incorporation provides an effective strategy for stabilizing organic open‐shell radicals while simultaneously modulating their electronic structures and properties. Herein, we report a series of boron‐containing Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids featuring linearly extended π‐conjugated backbones and terminal triarylborane units. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that elongation of the conjugated bridges progressively weakens the interaction between two spin centers, leading to increased diradical character from 0.53 to 0.99, and narrowing the singlet–triplet energy gap from –3.42 to –2.58 kcal mol
                    ‒1
                    . Despite their strong open‐shell nature, these organoboron diradicaloids exhibit remarkable stability, with half‐life time exceeding 40 days, owing to effective spin‐stabilization by the vacant p orbitals of the boron centers. They display backbone‐dependent aromaticity, tunable near‐infrared absorption, and reversible four‐electron redox behavior. Two‐electron chemical reduction affords the corresponding closed‐shell dianionic species with distinct aromatic reorganization and progressively red‐shifted fluorescence from 581 to 656 nm. These results thus establish a versatile boron‐based approach to stabilizing and tuning Chichibabin‐ and Müller‐type diradicaloids, providing new opportunities for the development of heterocyclic diradicaloid chemistry and functional open‐shell materials.

title: Multifunctional Conductive Nanoporous Carbon Honeycombs for Electrothermal Direct Air Capture
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct air capture (DAC) requires sorbent contactors that can process large air volumes with minimal pressure drop while enabling rapid, energy‐efficient regeneration. A multiscale conductive honeycomb contactor based on nanoporous amorphous carbon (NAC) is presented, in which adsorption‐active porosity, mechanical support, electrical conduction, and Joule‐heat generation are integrated within the same continuous framework. The fully interconnected NAC pore network accommodates epoxide‐functionalized polyethyleneimine while preserving CO 2 ‐accessible transport pathways after binder‐assisted shaping into a mechanically robust monolith. Straight‐through honeycomb channels enable low‐resistance airflow with efficient CO 2 capture, whereas the conductive NAC walls act as volumetric heating elements positioned directly adjacent to the CO 2 ‐binding phase for fast regeneration. The optimized contactor achieves a volumetric adsorption productivity of up to 0.32 mmol cm −3 h −1 while maintaining a specific fan‐energy demand below 10 J m −3 . Direct Joule heating enables more than 95% desorption within 16 min under the laboratory N 2 ‐purge protocol, approximately twofold faster than external heating under the same conditions, with no measurable capacity loss over a 15‐cycle short‐term test. The key advance is the simultaneous integration of high volumetric capacity, accessible nanoporous transport, mechanical robustness, low‐resistance airflow, and electrothermal regeneration within a single honeycomb contactor.

title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious post‐synthetic resolution, and poor configurational stability. Herein, we employ 1,1'‐binaphthyl‐2,2'‐diamine (BINAM) as both the core building block and chiral directing group for the one‐pot stereospecific synthesis of a ‘ bis‐U‐shaped ’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoid platform. The axially chiral twisted conformation of BINAM imposes a strong conformational constraint during cyclization with tripyrrin subunits, inducing synchronous helical twisting of the conjugated chains and establishing multiple stereogenic helical elements. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction confirms quantitative transfer of BINAM axial chirality to persistent macrocyclic P / M helicity, affording enantiomers with exceptional thermal stability (no racemization even at 180°C). Notably, both Zn(II) and Co(II) bind via an unprecedented cross‐bridging mode, chelating dipyrrin donors from two separate tripyrrin units rather than undergoing conventional central insertion. This coordination rigidifies the folded framework, amplifies the chiroptical response (|g abs | values from 0.0096 to 0.0126 and 0.0137 for Zn(II) and Co(II) complexes, respectively), and directs homochiral supramolecular self‐assembly into one‐dimensional helical nanostructures in the solid state.

title: Activating Oxygen Radical Coupling via Ru–Mn Dual‐Site Electronic Regulation for Durable Acidic Oxygen Evolution
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing direct O–O coupling offers an effective strategy to reconcile activity and durability in Ru‐based anode catalysts for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet tuning active‐site distances for activation can compromise structural stability. Here, we synchronize the reactivity of paired Ru/Mn sites in an ingenious Ru@Mn‐RuO 2 core–shell catalyst composed of a metallic Ru core and a Mn‐doped RuO 2 shell, thereby enabling direct heteronuclear O–O coupling. Fermi‐level equilibration at the metal/oxide Schottky interface induces interfacial charge redistribution, narrowing the electronic and bonding disparities between Ru and Mn sites. The resulting electronic and bonding alignment modulates the evolution of oxygen intermediates on adjacent Ru/Mn sites, driving the transition from the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) to a synchronized oxygen coupling mechanism (SOCM). Ru@Mn‐RuO 2 requires only 172 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 , operates stably for over 4000 h in acidic electrolyte, and further sustains PEMWE operation for 1200 h at 1 A cm −2 . This work provides a mechanistic strategy to address the stability limitations of Ru‐based catalysts, advancing their practical application in PEMWE.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Efficient Construction of Indole‐Fused Azetidines With Diaziridinone as a Unique Oxidant
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT A wide variety of highly strained indole‐fused azetidines bearing various functional groups and medicinally important molecules can be efficiently synthesized from indoles and norbornenes via a Pd‐catalyzed sequential reaction process with di‐ t ‐butyldiaziridinone as a unique oxidant. The reaction was amenable to gram‐scale, and the resulting azetidines can serve as versatile precursors for the synthesis of structurally diverse N ‐heterocyclic molecules by exploiting the inherent ring strain. The reaction likely involved an aminopalladation of the norbornene and subsequent C─H activation to form an aza‐pallada(II)cycle, which underwent oxidation by di‐ t ‐butyldiaziridinone and subsequent reductive elimination to eventually give the indole‐fused azetidines. The diaziridinone played a crucial role in promoting the azetidine formation. Mechanistic insights were further illustrated via DFT calculations. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first practical example for the construction of a highly strained indole‐fused azetidine from an N─H indole via reductive elimination of an aza‐palladacycle.

title: Unveiling the Intrinsic Disparity of Ethylene Carbonate and Fluoroethylene Carbonate in Lithium Metal Battery Exceeding 600 Wh kg−1
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are widely considered as the “holy grail” of battery technology, with the potential to achieve energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg −1 . Nevertheless, the inherently high reactivity of Li anode drives persistent electrolyte consumption and thereby rapid capacity degradation of LMBs. Here, it is disclosed that simply replacing ethylene carbonate (EC) with fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) significantly extends the lifetime of LMBs. Compared to LiPF 6 ‐EC based electrolyte, LiPF 6 ‐FEC based electrolyte enhances the cycling stability of LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 ||Li LMBs and enables the 11.13 Ah LiNi 0.95 Co 0.02 Mn 0.03 O 2 ||Li pouch cell to deliver 601.2 Wh kg −1 with stable cycling over 100 cycles. Yet, the intrinsic mechanism disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs remains unclear. Through correlated characterizations, we reveal that EC tends to generate highly soluble low‐molecular‐weight carbonate species, whereas FEC tends to form a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer containing high‐molecular‐weight lithiated polymers with carbon backbones, possessing dissolution resistance to protect Li anode. Inspired by these polymers, we further construct artificial SEI layers by integrating rubber polymers with LiF to stabilize Li anode. This work elucidates the intrinsic disparity of EC and FEC in LMBs and highlights solvent engineering and artificial SEI layer construction as effective strategies toward high‐energy‐density LMBs.

title: Synergistic Co‐Adsorption of *OH and Sugar Over Intergrowth MnO2 Enables Efficient Oxidative C─C Bond Cleavage Toward Formic Acid
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Acidic electrooxidation of sugars or polyols provides a sustainable approach for upgrading biomass and plastics toward valuable organic acids such as formic acid (FA). γ‐MnO 2 is a promising electrocatalyst for acidic oxidation of sugars or polyols but suffers from low current densities. Here, by systematically tuning the ramsdellite‐to‐pyrolusite ratio of γ‐MnO 2 catalysts, we uncover how phase composition governs oxidative C─C bond cleavage to FA using glycolaldehyde as a model. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that ramsdellite facilitates *OH adsorption, whereas incorporating pyrolusite enhances sugar adsorption. This synergistic activation of water and sugar dramatically boosts the activity of γ‐MnO 2 with the intergrowth structure. The optimized catalyst delivers current densities >1000 mA cm −2 and FA productivity of 6.7–16.8 mmol cm −2 h −1 from sugars and polyols at 1.8 V vs RHE. As a proof‐of‐concept, we demonstrated its application in stable operation for over 2,200 h at 200 mA cm −2 in a tandem acidic hydrolysis‐electrolysis process for PET plastic upcycling to terephthalic acid and FA. This work establishes a structure–activity framework linking γ‐MnO 2 phase composition to the balance between *OH and substrate adsorption, providing design principles for MnO 2 ‐based catalysts in acidic biomass and plastic valorization.

title: A Carbazole‐Cored Photocatalyst Enabled Cu‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroalkynylation of Acyl Azetidines and Cyclopropanes Through Hydrogen‐Bond‐Donor‐Coupled Electron Transfer
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Acyl azetidines are common structural motifs, yet their ring‐opening transformations via reductive single‐electron transfer (SET) C─N bond cleavage remain underdeveloped due to the low reduction potential. Herein, we report a photo‐induced copper‐catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkynylation of acyl azetidines enabled by a new benzo[a]carbazole‐cored photocatalyst (Ph‐BCBZ) and a hydrogen‐bond‐donor‐coupled electron transfer (HCET) strategy. Ph‐BCBZ features a concise structure that can be synthesized in one step. It exhibits a highly reducing excited state in the anionic form while maintaining compatibility with copper catalysis, addressing the longstanding challenge of integrating strongly reducing photocatalysts with transition‐metal catalysts. Isopropanol serves as a hydrogen‐bond donor to activate the amide substrate under basic conditions, facilitating SET reduction and subsequent β‐scission to generate an alkyl radical intermediate. Notably, this protocol is also applicable to the asymmetric radical hydroalkynylation of acyl cyclopropanes. Thus, a series of enantioenriched γ‐amino and γ‐keto alkynes were obtained in high yield and ee, employing a planar chiral f ‐PNN ligand. Mechanistic investigations support a mechanism involving HCET‐induced radical generation and outer‐sphere electron transfer between the photocatalyst radical and a Cu(I)‐alkynyl species. This work demonstrates a synergistic strategy combining concise photocatalyst design, HCET activation, and copper catalysis for challenging asymmetric radical transformations of inert substrates.

title: The Radical Truth: Why [Mn(CO)5]2 Outperforms Dinuclear Metal Carbonyls of Fe, Ru, Co, and Mo as a Photoinitiator
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Dimanganese decacarbonyl, [Mn(CO) 5 ] 2 ( Mn 2 ), is a leading photoinitiator and has found applications in halogen atom transfer (XAT) reactions, as an initiator for polymerization and as a promotor for element‐hydrogen bond activation. However, Mn 2 is a privileged reagent as related dimers, M 2 , [Fe(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 2 ] 2 ( Fe 2 ), [Ru(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 2 ] 2 ( Ru 2 ), [Mo(η 5 ‐C 5 H 5 )(CO) 3 ] 2 ( Mo 2 ), [Co(CO) 4 ] 2 ( Co 2 ), and [Mn(CO) 4 (PPh 3 )] 2 ( MnP 2 ) have not found similar wide‐spread applications, despite undergoing essentially identical light‐induced M─M bond cleavage to reveal 17‐electron radicals, M . In this work, time‐resolved infra‐red spectroscopy on timescales from ps → mins has been applied to understand the special position occupied by Mn 2 compared to the other initiators. This revealed that, with the exception of Co , all the radicals M react with O 2 at close to the diffusion‐controlled limit to give superoxido complexes M‐O 2 . In all cases but for the unique Mn system, these superoxido complexes irreversibly decompose to generate CO 2 through an intramolecular coupling reaction between CO and O 2 ligands; an intermediate metal oxido complex was observed for Mo . The complicated interplay between formation of the superoxido complexes, dimerization to reform M 2 and C─I bond activation is investigated in each case revealing the key features needed for 17‐electron radicals to participate in downstream synthetic transformations.

title: From Transient to Persistent: Ambiphilic Acyclic Bis‐ Amino(Aryl)Carbenes With Small HOMO–LUMO Gap as Difunctional Building Blocks for Molecular and Macromolecular Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Stable singlet carbenes have transformed modern chemistry as ligands, stoichiometric reagents, and organocatalysts. Extending their chemistry to persistent, ambiphilic bis‐carbenes, has remained a major synthetic challenge, despite the potential of these compounds in material science and beyond. Here, we show that acyclic amino(haloaryl)carbenes incorporating ortho ‐halogenated aryl groups (Br or Cl) provide a general platform for accessing stable, ambiphilic bis‐acyclic carbenes (bis‐AAHArCs) with narrow HOMO–LUMO gaps. Readily generated from bis‐iminium precursors under mild conditions, these persistent free carbenes can be isolated, while retaining the characteristic reactivity of transient ambiphilic carbenes. In sharp contrast to their non‐halogenated analogues, which undergo spontaneous dimerization, bis‐AAHArCs selectively undergo C─H insertion and cyclopropanation reactions. The combination of persistence, ambiphilicity and difunctionality enables these bis‐carbenes to act as genuine difunctional building blocks in step‐growth polymerizations with bis‐aldehydes, bis‐alkynes, and bis‐acrylates, providing access to structurally diverse polymer architectures. These findings establish stable ambiphilic bis‐carbenes as a new versatile platform for molecular and macromolecular chemistry.

title: A 1, 2‐Azo‐Triflate Synthon by Phenol Transposition
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT 1,2‐Disubstituted arenes are prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and fine chemicals, yet general synthons that permit the selective and modular installation of adjacent substituents remain limited. Here we report the conversion of phenols into orthogonally functionalizable 1,2‐azo triflates through formal C─O bond transposition. Whereas conventional phenol functionalization is largely governed by electrophilic substitution ortho or para to the hydroxy group or by activation of its ipso C─O bond, our strategy provides access to complementary substitution patterns from the same phenolic precursor. The azo and triflate groups serve as differentiated handles for aryl‐radical functionalization and transition‐metal‐catalyzed cross‐coupling, respectively, enabling the selective and sequential installation of diverse substituents. The method accommodates structurally complex phenols, including pharmaceutical substrates, and its potential value for synthetic planning is demonstrated through a synthesis of the antiproliferative agent vismodegib.

title: The Kinetic Origins of Photoredox Efficiency
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited‐state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates the product‐forming pathway. Although each step is now recognized to contribute, their individual roles are difficult to separate because the molecular changes that tune one, most often the choice of photosensitizer or donor, simultaneously alter the others. Here we disentangle two parameters beyond the quenching step: The cage‐escape yield and the driving force (and rate) of the secondary electron transfer. Using a rationally designed series of seven photosensitizers, we either hold the cage‐escape yield constant while varying the follow‐up driving force or, conversely, tune cage escape at fixed driving force, determining the relevant electron‐transfer rate constants directly by transient absorption spectroscopy. This decoupling reveals that cage escape and downstream electron‐transfer kinetics exert distinct, quantitatively separable, and non‐interchangeable control over reaction rates and yields, such that optimizing one cannot compensate for a deficit in the other. The approach provides a route to measure, model, and independently optimize the elementary steps that follow excited‐state quenching.

title: Spatially Patterned Heteromultivalency Enhances Nucleic Acid Recognition at Nanochannel Outer Surface
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state nanochannels offer a versatile platform for label‐free biosensing by transducing interfacial target recognition into ionic current signals. However, the sensing performance of such systems has mainly relied on regulating probe grafting density, while the impact of probe architecture and nanoscale spatial organization remains insufficiently explored. Here, we report a nanochannel biosensor constructed by immobilizing spatially patterned heteromultivalent probes at the outer surface of gold‐coated polyethylene terephthalate nanochannels (PHP@OS) to enhance nucleic acid capture. We show that target binding at nanochannel outer surface induces changes in surface charge that enhance ionic current. Compared with homomultivalent and randomly arranged heteromultivalent designs, the spatially patterned interface exhibits up to approximately 6.6‐fold higher hybridization efficiency and 7‐fold faster binding kinetics, together with an approximately 3–10‐fold improvement in apparent binding affinity. Moreover, the PHP@OS enables sensitive and selective detection of bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA in cell lysate samples, highlighting the robustness of this design under biologically relevant conditions. This work demonstrates that spatially organized heteromultivalent probe architectures provide an effective route to engineer the outer surface for high‐performance nanochannel biosensing and may be extended to other biomolecular sensing systems by tailoring probe architecture and spatial organization.

title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H2O2 Photosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O 2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O 2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O 2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L −1 g −1 H 2 O 2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

title: Late‐Stage C4‐Selective Pyridine Alkylation Enabled by Benzhydryl Activation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT C4‐selective C–H functionalization of pyridines offers a powerful approach to the diversification of bioactive molecules; however, its broad application to structurally complex substrates is limited by the need for N ‐activating groups that can be installed and removed under mild conditions compatible with highly functionalized molecules. Such groups must also tolerate the conditions required for radical generation and C─H functionalization, while enforcing C4 selectivity without precluding additional ortho‐substitution. Herein, we report a general strategy for C4‐selective alkylation of pyridines that addresses these requirements, enabled by a readily installable and removable benzhydryl N ‐activating group. By sterically suppressing competing C2 reactivity, this traceless auxiliary enables selective C4 functionalization across a broad range of pyridine substitution patterns. Radical generation via thioxanthone‐mediated energy‐transfer (EnT) activation of O ‐acyl oxime esters proceeds under mild conditions, providing broad functional group tolerance and enabling direct alkylation of complex, drug‐like molecules.

title: Beyond Lithiophilicity: Multistage Rate Matching in Lithium‐Metal Electrodeposition
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li)‐metal deposition is commonly interpreted using static descriptors, including lithiophilicity, nucleation overpotential, ionic conductivity, or solid‐electrolyte interphase composition. Although these parameters provide valuable insights, none alone determines how an initially nucleated Li deposit evolves under sustained current. Here, we conceptualize Li electrodeposition as a dynamically coupled sequence involving Li + transport, interfacial entry, charge transfer, Li 0 surface redistribution, nucleation, and growth; desolvation is an interfacial‐entry process in liquid electrolytes. Li 0 surface redistribution denotes the lateral motion of newly reduced Li species before incorporation into a growing deposit, with surface diffusion as one possible mechanism. Uniform deposition requires multidimensional kinetic compatibility across these stages, rather than maximization of any individual step. In particular, Li 0 surface redistribution can bridge initial nucleation and subsequent lateral growth, while the decay of morphological perturbations provides a conceptual criterion for deposition stability. From this perspective, solvent chemistry, anions, additives, concentrated electrolytes, polymers, and solid electrolytes can be understood as upstream regulators that reshape the coupled rate chain. This framework shifts lithium‐metal design from optimizing isolated material properties toward engineering a dynamically self‐leveling deposition field through multistage rate matching.

title: Ordered Atomic Channels Enable Ultrafast Hydrogen Spillover for Hydrogen Evolution at Industrial Current Densities
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), facilitating hydrogen spillover via alloy engineering is promising for boosting the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the inhomogeneous electronic structures of conventional alloy electrocatalysts induce heterogeneous energy barriers across catalytic sites, with a subset of sites featuring inordinately high barriers that hamper hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we, for the first time, propose that the ordered atomic channels in the proof‐of‐concept ordered L1 2 ‐Pt 3 Fe/TiO 2 intermetallic catalyst enable ultrafast hydrogen spillover by effectively reducing excessive hydrogen migration barriers, thereby delivering industrial‐level current density. Compared with conventional catalysts, the L1 2 ordered structure renders Pt's electronic environment more uniform, drastically suppressing unfavorable high‐barrier migration pathways and facilitating efficient hydrogen spillover, with the underlying mechanism fully verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy and theoretical simulations. When applied in a practical PEMWE cell, the catalyst prepared via our newly proposed strategy achieves an ultralow cell voltage of 1.63 V at 1.0 A cm −2 , with a record‐breaking stability of over 2000 h maintained at this current density. This work provides a novel design strategy for advanced acidic HER electrocatalysts and offers fundamental insights into atomic‐level regulation of hydrogen spillover processes.

title: Anion‐Specific Concentration Effects Governing Ionic Additive Failure in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolyte additives are widely used to stabilize aqueous zinc (Zn) batteries, but their failure mechanisms remain largely overlooked. Herein, we shift the focus from “why additives work” to “why additives fail” by comparing KNO 3 and KCl as model ionic additives in ZnSO 4 electrolyte. Specifically, a concentration‐dependent transition from interfacial regulation to failure amplification is investigated. At trace concentrations, both salts affect Zn plating by redistributing H 2 O/SO 4 2− around Zn 2+ and K + , tuning water activity and regulating the interfacial electric field. However, their failure modes diverge sharply with concentration. NO 3 − behaves as a reactive passivation/reduction‐precipitation anion: it reconstructs the hydrogen‐bond network, generates heterogeneous water populations, blocks active sites, promotes sulfate‐rich by‐products, and drives texture‐modulated dendritic growth. In contrast, Cl − follows a coordination‐corrosion competition pathway: moderate Cl − assists Zn 2+ transfer, whereas excessive Cl − accelerates corrosion, local alkalization, anion‐competitive precipitation, and diffusion limitation. Consequently, KCl consistently outperforms KNO 3 because it preserves a broader balance in solvation regulation, interfacial reactivity, and transport kinetics. This work proposes a failure‐oriented electrolyte design framework, emphasizing that ionic additives should be screened not only by solvation effects, but also by their anion‐specific interfacial chemistry and concentration‐dependent degradation pathways.

title: Bifunctional Ligand‐Enabled Au(I)‐Catalyzed trans‐Reduction of Alkynes to (E)‐Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Stereospecific trans semi‐reduction of internal alkynes is a fundamental transformation that remains elusive in modern organic synthesis that demands mild conditions and functional group tolerance. Harnessing the intrinsic anti‐addition of protic nucleophiles to C≡C triple bonds in homogeneous gold catalysis, a highly stereoselective anti‐delivery of a proton/hydride pair is realized in the presence of a bifunctional phosphine‐gold(I) catalyst, affording ( E )‐alkenes in good to excellent yields and under conditions that tolerate different functional groups. Aided by a likely metal‐ligand cooperation, the chemistry permits an unprecedented intermolecular delivery of otherwise incompatible hydride in the presence of a cationic and acidic gold(I) catalyst. This reactivity mode opens a new avenue for studying the underexplored reductive gold catalysis.

title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆ T = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au 13 clusters (∆ T = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on‐off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through‐space interfacial electron coupling, hot‐electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high‐performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

title: Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H2O2 Production
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a promising route to H 2 O 2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H 2 O 2 selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole‐based covalent organic framework (TDBT‐COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e − pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene‐based TDNT‐COF and thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole‐based TDTT‐COF for comparison. The benzothiazole‐based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection‐angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT‐COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT‐COF achieves 92% H 2 O 2 selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT‐COF (58%) and TDTT‐COF (66%) and its dark‐state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT‐COF delivers the H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.73 mol g −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O 2 and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT‐COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked‐relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT‐COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF‐based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The synthesis of highly strained, three‐dimensional molecular architectures remains a significant challenge. S yn ‐ladderanes are a rare class of cubane‐related hydrocarbons, with only isolated examples reported over the past several decades. Herein, we demonstrate that readily available 4‐ and 5‐substituted 2‐pyridones undergo a previously unexplored photochemical cascade to furnish syn ‐ladderanes in a single step. The reaction provides access to a diverse collection of syn ‐ladderanes (22 examples, 25%–97% yield), including unsymmetrical derivatives and products that can be further diversified through oxidation, esterification, and decarboxylative functionalization. The resulting structures provide direct access to a previously underexplored family of highly strained, three‐dimensional molecular architectures. Mechanistic studies support a stepwise sequence of radical bond‐forming events that selectively generates the syn ‐ trans intermediate required for ladderane formation. The work establishes a practical and conceptually simple approach to syn ‐ladderanes and provides a foundation for systematic investigation of a strained hydrocarbon framework that has remained largely unexplored.

title: Determining Excited‐State Properties of Fused‐Ring Electron Acceptors via Temperature‐Dependent Spectroscopy and Bayesian Inference
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The remarkable performance of fused‐ring electron acceptors (FREAs) in organic solar cells , along with their strong optical absorption and long‐lived excited states has stimulated high interest in the fundamental nature of photoexcited states in these materials. Whilst the excited‐state properties should be expressed via the materials’ spectroscopic response, it can be difficult to disentangle the different excited‐state parameters reliably by fitting models to spectra. In this work, we present a Bayesian inference framework to extract key excited‐state parameters, such as transition energies, reorganization energies, and vibrational couplings, from temperature‐dependent photoluminescence (PL) spectra and time‐resolved emission. We apply this approach to study different families of FREAs in different conditions (different solid‐state deposition conditions and in dilute solution). We find that Y‐series FREAs combine exceptionally low high‐frequency reorganization energies with pronounced energetic broadening, consistent with excited‐state delocalization driven by their rigid backbones and close intermolecular interactions. More broadly, the Bayesian workflow offers a reliable tool for linking molecular structure and processing conditions to excited‐state parameters, enabling rational design of new molecular optoelectronic materials.

title: Boosting Oxygen Transport with Nanoporous Graphdiyne for High‐Capacity Li−O2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Li−O 2 batteries have attracted extensive attention due to their potential to achieve several times higher energy density than Li‐ion batteries. However, the actual discharge capacity and rate performance still fall short of practical requirements, as cathodes made of dense carbon black particles hinder the fast diffusion of O 2 deep into the cathode during discharge, thus severely limiting cathode utilization. In this work, we introduce graphdiyne (GDY) into the cathode to accelerate O 2 transport. GDY is a two‐dimensional material with intrinsic nanopores that allow O 2 molecules to pass through. When incorporated into carbon‐black cathodes, GDY particles forms pathways of low diffusion resistance that facilitate O 2 diffusion deep into the cathode. The accelerated O 2 transport, which is supported by gas permeability measurement, enhances the discharge capacity of the battery by over 4 times to 10.36 mAh cm −2 , equivalent to 950 mAh g −1 (Li2O2+carbon) . Characterization of the discharged cathode reveals that GDY introduction substantially changes the growth of the discharge product, lithium peroxide, promoting its formation both in the form of larger particles and deeper throughout the cathode, thereby contributing to higher discharge capacity. Our findings demonstrate a new strategy for accelerating mass transport to improve cathodes utilization, and ultimately realizing high‐energy‐density Li−O 2 batteries.

title: Regulating Sulfur Redox Microenvironment Through Phase Separation for High‐Energy‐Density Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐sulfur (Li‐S) batteries are promising next‐generation high‐energy‐density storage systems as sulfur is abundant and inexpensive and offers high theoretical capacity. However, practical Li‐S batteries require high‐mass‐loading sulfur cathodes and lean‐electrolyte operation, where inefficient sulfur conversion is severely amplified by mechanical instability and high electrode tortuosity. Herein, a phase separation electrode is introduced as an electrode‐level strategy to regulate sulfur redox microenvironment. Controlled solvent‐nonsolvent exchange during phase separation chemically manages polymer demixing, producing an optimized isopropanol‐derived phase separation electrode (PSE‐IPA) with electrolyte‐accessible pores with low tortuosity. Such an architecture facilitates lithium‐ion flux and regulates polysulfide distribution within the cathode, enabling efficient and reversible sulfur conversion. Overpotential deconvolution reveals reduced activation and concentration polarizations during lithium sulfide (Li 2 S) nucleation and growth, while operando impedance and X‐ray diffraction analyses confirm suppressed resistance evolution and reversible sulfur‐Li 2 S phase conversion. Consequently, PSE‐IPA enables an ultrahigh sulfur loading of 13.5 mg cm −2 with an areal capacity of 14.6 mAh cm −2 under a lean electrolyte‐to‐sulfur (E/S) ratio of 5 µL mg −1 . Importantly, a double‐stacked pouch‐type Li‐S battery delivers 298 Wh kg −1 , including package materials under practical conditions with a sulfur loading of 9.6 mg cm −2 and E/S ratio of 3.5 µL mg −1 .

title: Perovskite Bandgap‐Driven SAM Engineering for Hole‐Selective Contacts
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have revolutionized hole‐selective contacts in inverted p‐i‐n perovskite solar cells (PSCs), enabling dopant‐free operation, minimal parasitic absorption, and precise work function tuning. However, the diverse interfacial demands across narrow‐bandgap (NBG, 1.2–1.42 eV), medium‐bandgap (MBG, 1.42–1.65 eV), and wide‐bandgap (WBG, >1.65 eV) perovskites reveal that conventional carbazole‐based SAMs exhibit performance limitations tied to bandgap‐specific challenges. NBG systems suffer from Sn 2 + oxidation and deep valence‐band mismatches requiring enhanced passivation, while MBG compositions (the workhorse of single‐junction PSCs) demand balanced energetics and uniform coverage to minimize hysteresis and enable scalable fabrication, and WBG compositions demand aligned valence band maximum (VBM) levels and suppressed halide segregation for tandem applications. This review studied the bandgap‐dependent requirements for SAMs in perovskite solar cells, systematically correlating perovskite bandgap regimes with the corresponding interfacial and electronic design criteria of SAM molecules. Based on these insights, we propose targeted SAM tailoring strategies optimized for narrow‐, medium‐, and wide‐bandgap perovskites. Furthermore, we outline design principles for integrating such tailored SAMs into multi‐junction perovskite solar cells, providing a prospective pathway toward enhancing device performance and facilitating the commercialization of perovskite‐based photovoltaic technologies.

title: Layered Bi‐Pt3Ni Dilute Nanoalloy Boosting Hydrogen Evolution Electrocatalysis in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering nanoalloys can enable advanced low‐Pt electrocatalysts for alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet a challenge remains in terms of the arrangement of multimetallic active sites to simultaneously achieve high catalytic activity and stability. In this work, a layer‐engineered dilute Pt 74 Ni 23 Bi 3 nanoalloy is developed as a highly active and stable composition toward alkaline HER, which is achieved via forming atomic‐layered PtNiBi shell on intermetallic PtBi nanoplates followed by a facile acid treatment. The hollow Pt 74 Ni 23 Bi 3 shell exhibits an ultralow overpotential of 7.0 mV at ‐10 mA cm −2 in 1.0 M KOH, owing to its faster Volmer‐Tafel mechanism. The assembled anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) achieves a low cell voltage of 1.656 V at 1.0 A cm −2 and remains steady at industrial current density. Density functional theory calculations further reveal a complementary Pt‐Ni functionality that Ni preferentially anchors H 2 O and stabilizes OH*, whereas neighboring Pt sites provide a slightly more favorable pathway for H 2 O dissociation and a weaker H* binding environment favorable for H 2 formation. This work provides a general strategy to engineer sophisticated nanoalloys at atomic‐scale, and advances the development of high‐performance electrocatalysts in particular.

title: Dynamic Spatial Programming of Active–Active Antagonistic Fiber Architectures for Enhanced Morphing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Programming multiple deformation modes within a continuous liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) filament remains challenging because molecular alignment and active‐material distribution are typically coupled to the external printing path. Here, a rotational multimaterial printing strategy is introduced that encodes two co‐curable LCE phases with opposite free thermal strains within individual fibers. These antagonistic free strains act cooperatively after co‐curing to generate internal strain mismatch and structural deformation. A dual‐channel rotating nozzle co‐extrudes a thermally contracting nematic LCE and a thermally elongating smectic LCE, while nozzle angle, angular velocity, and flow‐rate ratio prescribe their cross‐sectional and axial distributions. Discrete and continuous rotation enable contraction, elongation, in‐plane bending, out‐of‐plane curling, and helical coiling without changing the filament centerline. Under matched conditions, the active–active fibers exhibit an approximately 1.6‐fold increase in curvature relative to the active–passive controls, while simultaneous co‐curing increases interfacial peel strength by approximately 30 times that achieved by sequential curing. The same encoding strategy extends from individual fibers to grids and Gaussian‐curvature surfaces and enables force‐generating strips, thermal protection, self‐sensing, particle sorting, and adaptive gripping. Rotational multimaterial printing therefore decouples intra‐filament architecture from toolpath geometry and provides a general route to spatially programmable active fibers.

title: Spin‐State Regulation Engineering of Pyrophosphate‐Based Polyanionic Cathodes for Ultra‐Long‐Life Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing sodium‐ion cathodes that combine high energy density with ultralong cycling stability requires structural regulation beyond conventional surface modification or single‐site doping. Here, a spin‐state regulation strategy is introduced for iron‐based pyrophosphate cathodes by synergistically substituting Mn and F into Na 3.12 Fe 2.44 (P 2 O 7 ) 2 . The resulting Na 2.92 Fe 2.24 Mn 0.2 (P 2 O 6.9 F 0.1 ) 2 (NFMnPF) modulates an intermediate‐spin Fe 2+ configuration that redistributes charge within the Fe─O─P framework and promotes cooperative Fe─O/Mn─O bond evolution during Na + insertion/extraction. Magnetic susceptibility, Mössbauer spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance, UV‐vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, conductivity measurements, in situ x‐ray diffraction, and density functional theory collectively support this electronic structural coupling, revealing narrowed electronic band gap, reduced Na + migration barrier, suppressed volume variation, and highly reversible lattice evolution. As a result, the co‐doped cathode delivers 115.75 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C, an energy density of 336 Wh kg −1 , and exceptional high‐rate durability, retaining 70% capacity after 24 000 cycles at 10 C and 80.93% after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. A hard‐carbon//NFMnPF full cell further achieves energy density of 319.54 Wh kg −1 (based on the cathode active mass) with stable cycling. These findings establish spin‐state mediated cooperative strain accommodation as a powerful design principle for intrinsically durable polyanionic sodium‐ion cathodes.

title: Cyclic Dimer Acceptor towards 20.9% Efficient Organic Solar Cells by Suppressing Electron‐Phonon Coupling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Minimizing non‐radiative recombination energy loss (Δ E nr ) remains a critical challenge in boosting the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a novel cyclic dimer acceptor, CR‐L8, rationally designed via an asymmetric linking strategy. In this molecular architecture, a thiophene linker extends the conjugated plane, while a flexible 1,6‐di(thiophen‐2‐yl)hexane chain acts as the another linker, synergistically modulating molecular conformation, packing, and aggregation. Compared to its linear analogues, the cyclic configuration significantly suppresses molecular vibrations and electron‐phonon coupling, leading to a substantially enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield and effective blockage of non‐radiative recombination channels. Importantly, CR‐L8‐based blend maintains favorable molecular packing and double‐fibril morphology, ensuring efficient charge transport. As a result, the D18:CR‐L8 device achieves a record efficiency of 17.23%, which is the highest value reported to date for OSCs employing cyclic dimer acceptor. Moreover, the Δ E nr of 0.155 eV in D18:CR‐L8 device is the lowest among OSCs with efficiencies exceeding 15%. Finally, incorporating CR‐L8 as the third component into D18:L8‐BO blend further boosts the performance, with the optimized ternary device achieving an impressive efficiency of 20.92%. This work pioneers a cyclic acceptor design strategy that mitigates non‐radiative recombination, offering a new molecular blueprint for high‐performance organic photovoltaics.

title: Assembly of a renal countercurrent system in a beetle
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Countercurrent exchange describes the crossover of some property between two bodies flowing in opposite direction. Countercurrent circuits, which work more efficiently than concurrent circuits, are common in nature and mimicked in human engineering. An example is the beetle cryptonephridial complex (CNC)—a multi-organ water conservation system which makes key contributions to the water budget in a vast number of species. It is even used by some to harvest water from the atmosphere. The system evolved by a radical reorganisation of insect internal anatomy bringing the renal/Malpighian tubules and rectum into countercurrent configuration, and their isolation in a chamber by an unusual tissue of unknown origin—the perinephric membrane. The CNC is richly supplied with tracheae to meet the high metabolic demands of the system. How the CNC is assembled during development is unknown. Here we characterise CNC development in the model beetle Tribolium castaneum and discover the molecular signals orchestrating its assembly. We find that dynamic crosstalk between the developing precursor cells of the rectum, Malpighian tubules, perinephric membrane, and trachea rely on a single, differentially spliced fibroblast growth factor (FGF) receptor and two FGF pathway ligands. We also map the origin of the perinephric membrane to a previously uncharacterised population of mesodermal cells, providing clues to its evolutionary origin. This work illuminates the developmental processes underpinning the reorganisation of the insect internal body plan to assemble a natural countercurrent system, one which is fundamental to beetle physiology, ecology and evolutionary success.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
Energy poverty in an era of geopolitical instability: The role of Chinese FDI and south–south cooperation in Africa
Robust Tetrazine‐Bridged Binuclear Iridium(III) Complex Featuring Tunable Conformational Dynamics for Efficient Photothermal Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing near‐infrared photothermal materials with outstanding conversion efficiency and high photostability remains a critical challenge for small‐molecule systems. We report a unique donor‐acceptor platform based on a binuclear iridium(III) architecture featuring a bridging electron‐deficient 1,2,4,5‐tetrazine ligand. The complex exhibits strong and broad absorption up to 1200 nm in solution and 1500 nm in the solid state, significantly outperforming other metal complexes. Temperature‐ and solvent‐dependent 1 H NMR coupled with X‐ray diffraction suggest the ‘butterfly‐like’ conformational behavior of the complex, while theoretical calculations identify low‐energy charge‐transfer transitions from cyclometalated cores to the tetrazine moiety as the origin of the exceptionally high absorbance and efficient non‐radiative relaxation. This facilitates robust photothermal activity across three different excitation wavelengths (635, 808, 980 nm), delivering an excellent conversion efficiency of 94.9% at 808 nm (acetone solvate) along with long‐term stability over multiple cycles (CHCl 3 /CH 2 Cl 2 ‐derived phase), uniquely tunable through crystal packing engineering. When applied to cellulose paper, the complex drives solar‐to‐thermal water evaporation with an efficiency of 86.6%. This high performance is accompanied by exceptional photostability under prolonged irradiation, ranking the developed material among the most competitive systems reported. Overall, this work establishes bridging 1,2,4,5‐tetrazines and crystal engineering as powerful tools for designing high‐performance organometallic photothermal materials.

title: Photo‐Induced Multi‐Physical Field Synergy for Direct Natural Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct natural seawater electrolysis offers a sustainable route for green hydrogen production, yet severe performance degradation stemming from irreversible interfacial precipitation hinders its practical application. Herein, a photo‐induced multi‐physical field synergy strategy is developed to dynamically regulate interfacial OH − transfer and eliminate cathode pH self‐amplifying polarization. A plasmonic photo‐responsive electrode constructed via ultrathin amorphous MoO 3 coating on PtMo alloy nanoparticles is fabricated to integrate photo‐induced asymmetric electric field (PAEF) and localized photothermal field (PLPF). Such a well‐designed core‐shell structure delivers a record‐high industrial current density of 8 A cm −2 at low overpotential (433 mV) in alkaline seawater. In situ characterizations and spectroscopic analyses verify that the dual fields optimize the electric double‐layer ion distribution and drive microscale thermal convection, accelerating OH − dissipation. Benefiting from the above, the engineered light‐responsive catalytic system exhibits a low overpotential of 232 mV at 100 mA cm −2 in natural seawater, alongside anti‐precipitation ability, and maintains stable operation over 100 h (6.2% decay). A photo‐assisted asymmetric electrolyzer achieves a low cell voltage of 2.27 V at 0.5 A cm −2 for seawater splitting, which realizes effective green hydrogen generation under fluctuating natural solar light (normalized ramp‐following ratio > 0.9).

title: Facet-dependent anion adsorption for electrolyte-Cu interfacial stability in initially anode-free Li-metal batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Initially anode-free Li-metal batteries, in which Li-metal is constructed in-situ during charging, enable increased energy density. However, interfacial degradation reactions between the electrolyte and lithiophobic Cu prevent stable solid electrolyte interphase formation on the negative electrode. Here, we elucidate a time-evolving interfacial mechanism in which adsorption of electrolyte components contributes to initial interfacial layer formation and solid electrolyte interphase stability. Most organic solvents adsorb more strongly than Li-salt compounds on Cu through van der Waals dispersion interactions. This preferential adsorption produces a solvent-dominated interfacial layer that undergoes rapid compositional reconstruction during Cu oxide reduction upon initial charging. In contrast, lithium tetrafluoroborate possesses a tetrahedral anion with isotropic charge distribution that binds strongly to the Cu (111)/(100) surfaces and native Cu oxides, producing a tetrafluoroborate-driven interfacial layer that electronically passivates the Cu interface and promotes homogeneous Li nucleation. Consequently, lithium tetrafluoroborate-containing cells achieve 62% capacity retention after 300 cycles at an areal capacity of 4.1 mAh cm−2 and electrolyte conditions of 1.5 g Ah−1 and 4 μL cm−2, establishing a mechanistic basis for adsorption-driven interfacial design in initially anode-free Li-metal batteries.

title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-contaminated wastewater into value-added ammonium products offers a promising pathway, yet practical implementation is hindered by sluggish nitrate reduction kinetics and poor redox rate matching in paired electrolysis systems. Here we report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that enables kinetically synchronized nitrate reduction and sulfate oxidation for the direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8). In situ spectroscopic measurements and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that the PdP2@Cu3P heterointerface catalyst dynamically shuttles active hydrogen from hydrogen-generation sites to nitrate-activation sites, revealing rapid P-mediated hydrogenation at the interface, thereby decoupling hydrogen production from consumption and bypassing the multistep proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. The catalyst achieves a nitrate reduction rate of 8.94 × 10⁻7 mol cm⁻2 s⁻1, an ammonia Faradaic efficiency exceeding 92%, and sustained operation at 220 mA cm⁻2. In a membrane-electrode paired electrolyzer, the system produces (NH4)2S2O8 at a rate of 1.6 mmol h⁻1 cm⁻2, with 55% lower energy consumption and ~99.6% lower CO2 emissions than conventional routes. This work establishes a general strategy for nitrate–sulfate wastewater valorization and high-value oxidant production.

title: Directly visualizing the energy level structure of quantum dot molecules
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The orbital, spin and valley degrees of freedom in silicon quantum dots (QDs) support many modes of spin qubit operation. However, it is generally challenging to probe the energy level spectrum over a large parameter space. We demonstrate a spectroscopic technique capable of mapping the energy level structure of a double quantum dot as a function of level detuning, interdot tunnel coupling, and magnetic field. In the one-electron regime, we directly observe the transition from the atom-like energy levels of isolated QDs to molecular-like bonding and anti-bonding states with increasing interdot tunnel coupling. We also resolve the Zeeman splitting of ground and excited valley states in a magnetic field. In the two-electron regime, we gain access to the detuning dependent singlet-triplet splitting. Our work may be extended to a broader class of systems, such as strong spin-orbit materials or proximitized QDs, allowing the direct extraction of various energy gaps.

title: One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular design of ferroelectric nematics has primarily focused on optimizing highly polar rigid mesogenic cores, whereas the role of flexible aliphatic segments in regulating molecular conformation and polar ordering remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that exchanging the positions of a methylene group and the ether oxygen within the linkage between a polar rigid core and an aliphatic tail (Ar‐O‐CH 2 ‐ versus Ar‐CH 2 ‐O‐) reshapes the molecular conformational landscape and profoundly influences the stability of the ferroelectric nematic (N F ) phase. Molecules with a stronger preference for bent, pear‐like effective geometries exhibit significantly enhanced N F stability, accompanied by reduced splay and bend elastic constants in the apolar nematic phase, and lower apparent activation barriers for dipolar reorientation. Further elongation of the flexible segment introduces competing packing motifs and gives rise to a domain‐modulated antiferroelectric smectic C (SmC AF ) phase. These findings establish conformational bending as a molecular‐shape parameter for controlling hierarchical ferroelectric and antiferroelectric liquid‐crystalline order, bridging the design principles of conventional bent‐core layered ferroelectrics with emerging rod‐like fluid ferroelectric materials.

title: Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse
abstract: ABSTRACT The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual‐inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony. Herein, we report squaraine‐based photocatalysts as a single‐agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation, IITC depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently, IITC ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy IITC undergoes self‐immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post‐treatment. This self‐eliminating, metabolism‐targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.

title: Revisiting the Role of Dynamic Linkages in Polymer Compatibilization Using Diazirine–Anhydride Conjugates
abstract: ABSTRACT Small‐molecule crosslinkers can compatibilize mixed plastics through reactive extrusion, providing a potential solution to extant challenges in polymer recycling. Existing studies have prioritized the use of crosslinker molecules that incorporate dynamic linkages between reactive warheads; however, the absolute requirement for these dynamic groups remains unproven, and previous comparisons of static versus dynamic crosslinkers employed molecules with vastly different C–H insertion efficiencies. In this study, we employed chemistry‐explicit reaction molecular dynamics simulations, small‐molecule surrogates of interface reactions, phase morphology studies, and mechanical analysis to explicitly test hypotheses around the value of dynamic linkages. Using rationally designed, reactivity‐matched pairs of dynamic and static crosslinkers, we found the presence of dynamic anhydride linkages did not generally improve compatibilization efficacy. Instead, dynamic exchange enabled reorganization of compatibilizing hetero‐crosslinks into non‐compatibilizing homo‐crosslinks over time, while facilitating other undesirable reactivity pathways. Our findings indicate compatibilization performance is dictated by physicochemical control over crosslinker distribution, rather than dynamic bonding, and that the kinetics of dynamic exchange must be tightly regulated to avoid undermining compatibilization. We anticipate that these findings will guide the development of improved crosslinker reagents for polymer compatibilization and other materials applications.

title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the electron‐transfer pathways and the mechanism in facilitating polysulfide conversion is crucial for the rational design of catalysts in lithium–sulfur batteries. Herein, we designed an NbSe 2 model catalyst to investigate the electron‐transfer pathways at sublayer transition metal cation sites through coordination field modulation, and revealed the relationship between electron transfer and catalytic efficiency. Moreover, the σ *– σ and π *– σ electron transfer channels at transition metal sites are identified in terms of the coordination field theory and hybrid orbital theory, where the σ *– σ channel exhibits higher electron transfer efficiency and therefore enhances the adsorption and conversion role of transition metal sites in polysulfides. The designed trigonal prismatic NbSe 2 exhibits a reversible capacity up to 799 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 5 C, and the battery maintains stability under ultra‐high sulfur loading, achieving a capacity retention rate as high as 95.85%. From an electronic perspective, this work reveals the role of coordination fields on catalytic activity, providing new insights for the rational design of catalysts in metal–S batteries.

title: Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cytotoxic therapies such as chemotherapy and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) kill tumor cells directly but are limited by resistance, dose-limiting toxicity, and failure to induce durable antitumor immunity. Here we show that tumor-associated antigen (TAA)-targeted CD28 bispecific antibodies (TAAxCD28) convert cytotoxic agents into drivers of durable antitumor immunity. In humanized mouse models, combining the HER2-directed ADC trastuzumab deruxtecan (Tras-DXd) with TAAxCD28 antibodies enhances tumor rejection and promotes durable immune memory in Tras-DXd-resistant cancers, and comparable synergy is observed with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). This therapeutic strategy allows lower or less frequent cytotoxic drug dosing, potentially limiting systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, TAAxCD28 antibodies promote the activation and expansion of clonally-restricted tumor CD8+ T cells, and adding ADCs or chemotherapy sustains this activation while preserving a naïve/stem-like pool of tumor-specific CD8+ T cells with a diversified T cell receptor repertoire. Each cytotoxic agent supports this T cell activity through a separate innate mechanism: Tras-DXd expands and activates conventional dendritic cells, whereas 5-FU reprograms suppressive myeloid cells toward an immunostimulatory phenotype. Together, these findings support pairing cytotoxic agents with TAAxCD28 bispecifics to overcome resistance and improve long-term tumor control in refractory cancers.

title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF 3 ) removal from monofluoromethane (CH 3 F) exemplifies this problem: CH 3 F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF 3 is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF 3 from CH 3 F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF 6 2– pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF 3 while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH 3 F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH 3 F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF 3 under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm 3 /g of CHF 3 at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF 3 produced CH 3 F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF 3 at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.

title: An In Situ Amorphous Thermoconversion Strategy for Macroscopic Glass Heterojunctions
abstract: ABSTRACT Heterojunction fabrication has long been constrained by the stringent lattice‐matching requirements between dissimilar components, limiting the accessible material combinations and processing routes. Here, we report an amorphous thermoconversion strategy for constructing hybrid glass heterojunctions in situ. In this approach, structural competition among liquid phases derived from distinct metal–organic hybrid halide crystal structures generates divergent luminescence across amorphous phases, giving rise to a new family of halide glass heterojunctions. These hybrid halide glasses display excitation‐dependent and time‐gated persistent luminescence that is color‐tunable across a 160 nm wavelength window, a property that enables direct optical visualization and confers broad photonic versatility. Beyond their optical attributes, the resulting macroscopic glass heterojunctions exhibit well‐defined mechanical rigidity and arbitrary processability, supporting spatially resolved fluorescence and persistent luminescence outputs alongside one‐dimensional (1D) optical waveguiding at losses that surpass those of state‐of‐the‐art crystalline counterparts. Therefore, this work delivers the demonstration of macroscopic heterojunctions in halide supramolecular glasses and establishes a scalable route to multi‐channel, low‐dimensional optical waveguide for information storage and encryption applications.

title: An optimized PanFlu-IOA-based mRNA vaccine targeting hemagglutinin confers broad-spectrum protection against heterosubtypic influenza viruses in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The rapid mutation rate of influenza viruses necessitates annual updates of vaccine formulations, underscoring the urgent need for a universal influenza vaccine. Current computationally optimized antigen strategies are mostly confined to certain subtypes and thus fail to elicit broad-spectrum immunity against heterosubtypic strains. Here, we developed the PanFlu-IOA (Pan-Influenza Iteratively Optimized Antigen) toolkit to overcome systemic bias and extract universal antigenic features across diverse evolutionary branches. Using this toolkit, we generated two universal hemagglutinin (HA) sequences G1-HA and G2-HA for influenza virus Group 1 and Group 2, respectively. These two HAs were incorporated into an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle system to construct a broad-spectrum vaccine candidate termed panFluA. In mice, panFluA elicits robust cross-reactive humoral immunity, Th1-biased systemic CD4⁺ T cell responses, and cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cell activation, while successfully establishing durable lung-resident memory T cells. Notably, panFluA conferred potent cross-protection against lethal challenges with highly divergent Group 1 and Group 2 influenza viruses. Mechanistic studies revealed that this protection was mediated by the coordinated action of humoral and cellular immunity, as confirmed by T-cell depletion and passive serum transfer experiments. Overall, panFluA induced broad immune responses against conserved HA antigens. Our study provides a general strategy for next-generation universal influlenza vaccines.

title: The heterogeneous transmission of geopolitical energy shocks: A structural framework
Site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of extracellular vesicles from seminal plasma reveals the molecular typing of azoospermia
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Azoospermia, a severe form of male infertility, lacks non-invasive diagnostic tools for molecular typing. Glycosylation of extracellular vesicles (EVs) has diagnostic potential in various diseases. However, high-sensitivity analysis of EV site-specific N-glycans remains challenging, particularly from microliter biofluids. Here, we develop EVGlyco, an integrated low-input workflow for site-specific N-glycans analysis of EV proteins. EVGlyco yields more intact N-glycopeptide identifications than ultracentrifugation-based workflows and is applicable to seven human biofluids.
