From seminal plasma, 8,435 EV protein site-specific N-glycans are identified in the discovery cohort, and targeted validation via parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) confirms the panel of MPO-N355-H6N2 and ACP3-N94-H5N4F1 distinguishing obstructive azoospermia (OA) from nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA) with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88, while CLU-N374-H10N9 and CLU-N374-H10N9F1 further accurately distinguish three NOA subtypes (hypospermatogenesis: 0.86, maturation arrest: 0.99, and Sertoli cell-only: 0.87). This study supports EV protein site-specific N-glycans as diagnostic signatures for non-invasive molecular typing of azoospermia.

title: Mapping dynamics of subcellular RNA and protein localization and organization using optimal transport
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Subcellular molecular polarity is essential for early development and represents a key layer for building virtual cell models that connect molecular organization to cell fate. Yet how RNA and protein localization patterns are established, erased, and rebuilt during the transition from oocyte to zygote remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we integrate high-resolution axial cryo-sectioning with multi-omics profiling across six stages of Xenopus laevis early development and develop an optimal-transport-based framework to quantify spatial polarity and temporal remodeling of molecular distributions. Here, we show that proteins, rather than RNAs, carry the dominant and rapidly remodeled polarity signature, undergoing polarity collapse from stage VI oocytes to unfertilized eggs and rapid re-establishment after fertilization; this protein-specific rewiring contrasts with relatively stable RNA localization, reveals uncoupling between transcript storage and protein spatial deployment, and provides a spatial multi-omics foundation for modeling early embryogenesis toward virtual cells.

title: Rhizospheric pH mediated thermo-signalling coordinates root growth under heat stress
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Heat stress events pose a major threat to global agriculture due to elevated air and soil temperatures. While plant roots regulate their growth in response to elevated soil temperatures, they appear to rely on thermosensory mechanisms distinct from those used by shoots. Here, we report pH as a key component of a thermo-signaling mechanism that regulates temperature-dependent root responses via ROS-mediated control of cell cycle dynamics in Arabidopsis thaliana. At moderately high temperatures, alkalization of meristematic and transition zones increases superoxide (O₂⁻) levels, promoting cell division and root growth. Conversely, higher temperatures inhibit growth by increasing acidification and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) accumulation in these zones. Elevating external pH buffers this acidification, reduces H₂O₂ levels, and confers heat resistance. Our data support that this pH-mediated heat resistance is also effective under soil conditions. The heat-induced pH shifts are controlled by plasma membrane H⁺-ATPases (PM-H⁺-ATPases), which are under the control of the kinases TOT3 and TOI5. Our findings reveal an interesting pathway for plant adaptation to heat stress, linking pH, ROS and root thermomorphogenesis, with major implications for improving plant resilience in warming climates.

title: Chromatin priming of skeletal stem and progenitor cells governs cell fate during bone repair
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Skeletal stem/progenitor cells (SSPCs) involved in bone regeneration reside in the periosteum and bone marrow, as well as in adjacent skeletal muscles. Given the diversity of SSPCs and their distinct contributions to healing, the regulation of their tissue-specific fate remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how SSPC transcriptomic profiles and chromatin priming govern cell fate decisions in response to bone injury. We generate murine and human musculoskeletal stromal cell atlases that encompass all previously identified SSPCs, grouped into two transcriptionally distinct populations: CXCL12-abundant reticular (CAR) cells, restricted to the bone marrow, and PDGFRα+ Sca-1+ (PαS) cells, predominant in the periosteum and skeletal muscle. Combined single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing reveals CAR- and PαS-specific cis-regulatory elements at steady state in mice. We identify a Sox9-dependent chondrogenic program in PαS cells that controls cartilage formation and is required for bone repair. Although PαS cells in the periosteum and skeletal muscle exhibit similar transcriptomes, we uncover distinct chromatin profiles that correlate with their post-injury fate. Periosteal PαS cells also show a specific osteogenic program involving the transcription factor DLX5, which drives bone formation. Chromatin priming in distinct SSPCs is thus a critical regulator of cell fate during bone repair.

title: Anionic Lone‐Pair‐Like Electrons Induced Ultra‐Low Lattice Thermal Conductivity and High Thermoelectric Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT The traditional lone‐pair electron strategy primarily reduces lattice thermal conductivity ( κ L ) by enhancing anharmonic lattice vibrations. However, this mechanism has long been considered to exist only in specific cations with ns 2 electron configurations (e.g. Sb 3+ , Bi 3+ ), severely restricting the broader applicability of this lone‐pair‐based approach. In this study, CuInSnSe 4 is successfully synthesized via atomic cross‐substitution from the diamondoid CuInSe 2 , wherein the Se atoms exhibit an anionic lone‐pair‐like electronic behavior, revealing a new approach to reducing κ L that differs from conventional cation‐based mechanisms. In contrast to the traditional mechanism that relies on cations to enhance lattice anharmonicity, the anionic lone‐pair electrons weaken the Se‐Se interactions, flatten the optical phonon branches, and consequently significantly expand the scattering phase space, providing more scattering channels for phonons. This anionic lone‐pair electron strategy reduces the room‐temperature κ L from 4.48 to 1.26 W m −1 K −1 . Ultimately, the predicted optimal thermoelectric figure of merit ( ZT ) for p‐type and n‐type CuInSnSe 4 attains values of 1.99 and 0.79, respectively. This work systematically expands the conventional application boundaries of the lone‐pair electron strategy and elucidates a fundamentally distinct mechanism for κ L reduction, providing a new theoretical basis for designing and developing novel high‐efficiency thermoelectric materials with intrinsically low κ L .

Common-path evaluation of electric boiler and thermal storage dispatch in Finnish district heating under electricity-price uncertainty
abstract: The value of uncertainty-aware district-heating dispatch depends on when prices become known and how long heat remains in storage. This study develops a price-taking mixed-integer linear model for a Finnish system with biomass CHP, a 50 MW th electric boiler (EB), a natural-gas peak boiler, and thermal energy storage (TES). Daily 72 h problems implement the cleared first 24 h and propagate each policy's realised TES state. Deterministic, stochastic, and budgeted robust policies are compared on one 2023 hourly path and on 800 held-out price trajectories; their economic differences are assessed against TES value and parameter sensitivity. With 200 MWh th TES, annual costs are EUR 4.902, 4.920, and 4.939 million, respectively, compared with EUR 4.783 million for a rolling perfect-foresight benchmark. Stochastic dispatch has the lowest held-out mean cost and regret, while deterministic dispatch has slightly lower P 95 and CVaR 95 . TES saves EUR 1.974 million a − 1 relative to matched no-storage dispatch; the stochastic and robust annual premiums are only EUR 0.037 and 0.075/MWh th . Storage mainly shifts heat within one day. A 200-sample annual rolling sensitivity analysis identifies CHP power-to-heat ratio, EB capacity, fuel price, and TES duration as the dominant cost drivers. Biases of ±5% and ± 10% in look-ahead heat demand preserve the annual policy ranking. The EB dispatch-weighted carbon intensity is approximately 26 g CO2/kWhel, below the national consumption-weighted mean of 37.69 g CO2/kWhel.

title: Photovoltaic greenhouses in the European south: balancing energy generation and agricultural productivity - an economic analysis
abstract: This study evaluates the techno-economic feasibility of photovoltaic greenhouses in representative Mediterranean regions in Spain and Italy. A techno-economic model was developed to analyze the interaction between photovoltaic technology choice including present-day crystalline silicon PV (c-Si), current-state Organic Photovoltaics (OPV) modules with 63 W m −2 , and a projected future OPV scenario with 145 W m −2 , greenhouse electricity demand profiles, PV coverage levels, battery storage integration, remuneration schemes and crop yield responses to shading. Without taking crop yields into account, results show that greenhouse electricity demand and the resulting self-consumption potential are the dominant drivers of economic performance. Under high-demand conditions several configurations become profitable, reaching net present values (NPVs) of up to 51,640€ in Bari and 22,176€ in Almería. Under the optimistic OPV145 scenario, which combines a projected module output of 145 W m −2 with future upscaling-related cost reductions, NPVs reach values comparable to the present-day c-Si PV reference in selected high-demand configurations. Profitability declines under less favorable performance assumptions, with initial performance losses exerting a stronger economic effect than higher annual degradation rates. The current-state OPV63 scenario, based on commercially oriented module cost assumptions and 63 W m −2 output, remains economically constrained across most configurations, although NPVs at low PV coverage indicate that moderate improvements in efficiency or costs could enable feasibility. When crop yield impacts are incorporated, profitability becomes strongly crop-dependent. High-value crops such as strawberries are better able to offset PV investment costs, as the shading effect can enhance crop yields. Lower-value crops remain economically challenging. Sensitivity analysis indicates that, if the PV system alone does not achieve break-even, additional crop revenues of up to 4700€ year −1 in Bari and 6400€ year −1 in Almería are required to reach economic break-even. Conversely, economically viable configurations can withstand revenue losses of up to 3600€ year −1 and 1600€ year −1 , respectively. Overall, the results demonstrate that photovoltaic greenhouse systems can become economically viable under favorable demand conditions, suitable crop selection and future OPV cost and performance improvements.

title: Advances in sorption-based thermochemical energy storage: from material properties to prototype-level performance
Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

A Phosphonium Relay for Integrated Cleavage‐to‐Cyclization of Cyclic Peptides
abstract: ABSTRACT Head‐to‐tail macrocyclization of peptides is typically performed through stepwise workflows that separate resin cleavage, isolation of linear intermediates, and subsequent cyclization, largely due to incompatible activation requirements for each transformation. Here we report a phosphonium‐mediated relay that unifies these steps within a single activation node. In this design, an electrophile‐activated phosphonium species promotes cleavage from standard 2‐chlorotrityl chloride (2‐CTC) resin and is proposed to enable in situ formation of a C ‐terminally activated intermediate for intramolecular amidation. The strategy directly couples cleavage to cyclization on standard peptide supports without auxiliary linkers, intermediate purification, or high‐dilution cyclization conditions. The method is compatible with diverse peptide sequccnces and functional handles and can be integrated into a closed‐loop automated workflow for end‐to‐end synthesis, with advantages for hydrophobic substrates by avoiding isolation of poorly soluble linear intermediates such as Vespid chemotactic peptide 5f . Process‐level benchmarking against side‐chain anchoring further demonstrated favorable process metrics and gram‐scale scalability. This work establishes a linker‐free cleavage‐to‐cyclization strategy and provides a practical framework for integrated and automation‐compatible cyclic peptide synthesis.

title: Colloidally Prepared Homogeneous Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Efficient Tandem Solar Cells with Industrial Silicon
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites, based on mixed halide-cation compositions, are widely employed as top cells in perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells to overcome the theoretical limitations of single-junction devices and exploit the full potential of crystalline silicon photovoltaics. However, uncontrolled nucleation rates and disordered crystallization kinetics in WBG perovskites pose a grave challenge to the preparation of phase-homogeneous perovskite films. Herein, we identify the undesirable precursor suspension as the main underlying reason for the compositional inhomogeneity and propose a colloidal engineering strategy to reconstruct the perovskite intermediate complex. According to classical colloidal theory and theoretical calculations, long-chain alkylphosphonic acid molecules are selected to precisely regulate colloidal structures and properties via their specific coordination strengths, leading to colloid-guided rapid nucleation and slow crystallization processes. Assisted by the uniform colloidal nucleation template, the prepared WBG perovskite films with compositional homogenization and reduced trap density enable tandem devices based on industrial silicon heterojunction cells to yield a champion power conversion efficiency of 34.01% (a certified reverse-scan PCE of 33.65%) for a 1 cm2 active area. The resultant encapsulated tandem device maintains 93% and 88% of its initial efficiency after 1211 h and 1000 h of one-sun operation at 25 and 65 °C, respectively, under their maximum power points.

title: Remarkable Low‐Temperature Magnetocaloric Performance in a Frustrated Divalent Eu(II) Magnet Eu 5 FP 3 O 12
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of 3 He‐free sub‐Kelvin adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR), which relies on the magnetocaloric (MC) effect in magnets, is constrained by the lack of magnetic refrigerants operating from several Kelvin to the milli‐Kelvin range. This work reports a geometrically frustrated divalent Eu(II)‐dominated magnet, Eu 5 FP 3 O 12 , designed by combining moderate magnetic frustration with a dense Eu(II) magnetic lattice, which is distinct from conventional trivalent Gd(III)‐based systems. Eu 5 FP 3 O 12 crystallizes in a hexagonal structure in which a subset of magnetic Eu(II) ions occupies a triangular lattice, giving rise to moderate magnetic frustration and a very low magnetic ordering temperature of 530 mK. Consequently, the Eu 5 FP 3 O 12 exhibits a large low‐temperature MC effect with a maximum magnetic entropy change of 64.5 (370.3) J/kg K (mJ/cm 3 K) and a maximum adiabatic temperature change of 16.9 K under a magnetic field variation of 0–5 T. These values substantially surpass the commercial standard Gd 3 Ga 5 O 12 and are comparable to or exceed those of the best reported low‐temperature magnetic refrigerants under comparable conditions. Together with its good environmental stability and facile solid‐state synthesis, these results identify Eu 5 FP 3 O 12 as a promising refrigerant for 3 He‐free ADR applications and highlight the frustrated divalent Eu(II) magnets as a viable design route for low‐temperature magnetic refrigerants.

title: Multiscale Characterizations Toward Energy Storage Carbon Materials From Precursors to Electrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The sp 2 ‐hybridized carbon materials such as graphite, soft carbon, and hard carbon, are broadly used as anodes for alkali‐metal‐ion batteries owing to their stable and controllable microstructures. However, the inherent structural complexity and multi‐stage synthesis processes of carbon materials pose challenges to their comprehensive characterization, limiting a deeper structural understanding and performance improvement of carbon electrodes. This review establishes a comprehensive characterization framework for the multiscale understanding of carbon materials from their precursors to carbon electrodes. Because the structural features of carbon materials are largely inherited from their precursors, we first summarize the recent advances in the characterization of their molecular structures and pyrolysis behaviors. We then discuss advanced characterization techniques and corresponding analysis methods used to understand the multiscale structures of carbon materials, including particles, microcrystals, and pore structures. We further provide a comprehensive overview of static and real time characterization techniques for studying interfacial ion transport and bulk ion diffusion kinetics in carbon electrodes. On this basis, we draw a decision‐making framework for multiscale characterization to help readers quickly navigate from problem definition to characterization strategy. Finally, we provide future perspectives to facilitate the efficient scientific investigation and rational design of high‐performance carbon materials for alkali‐metal‐ion batteries.

title: Self‐Sustaining Lattice‐Oxygen Cycling Enables Durable Industrial‐Level Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Lattice oxygen‐mediated seawater oxidation offers fast kinetics for energy‐efficient hydrogen production, but its practical application is hampered by catalyst degradation arising from transient oxygen vacancies and chloride corrosion at industrial current densities. Here we report an Ag‐decorated amorphous RuFeCo layered double hydroxide (Ag‐RuFeCo LDH) that enables self‐sustaining lattice‐oxygen cycling by integrating disorder‐activated lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) with an anion‐selective interface. Ru incorporation induces structural disorder and enhances Fe─O covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen participation in seawater oxidation. Meanwhile, oxophilic silver oxide reconstructed in situ establishes an OH − ‐enriched interfacial environment that mitigates Cl − adsorption and rapidly replenishes LOM‐generated oxygen vacancies, thereby stabilizing the catalyst structure. Consequently, Ag‐RuFeCo LDH requires only 308 mV overpotential to achieve 1.0 A cm −2 in alkaline natural seawater and maintains stable performance during a cumulative operation exceeding 9500 h. An anion‐exchange‐membrane electrolyzer using Ag‐RuFeCo LDH as both electrodes reaches 1.0 A cm −2 at 1.92 V and operates continuously for 1000 h with a low energy consumption of 4.59 kWh Nm −3 H 2 . This strategy successfully overcomes the corrosion bottleneck of LOM in seawater electrolysis and offers a general strategy for durable and sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Thermodynamically Controlled Multiphase Evolution in Single‐Crystal Cation‐Disordered Li‐Ion Cathode Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Mn‐based disordered rock‐salt (Mn‐DRX) cathodes are promising materials for Li‐ion batteries, yet their application is limited by sluggish Li transport, voltage instability, and capacity fading. Here, we show that thermodynamic control of multiphase evolution from single‐crystal Mn‐DRX overcomes these limitations. Using grand‐potential phase diagrams with in situ and ex situ X‐ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy, we demonstrate that DRX composition and annealing conditions govern transformation into nanocomposites containing DRX, spinel, and monoclinic layered phases, with anatase formation predicted in specific Li–Mn–Ti–O compositions. Oxidative annealing at 300–500°C induces decomposition pathways: Li‐deficient compositions form DRX–spinel (DS) nanocomposites, whereas Li‐rich compositions form DRX–spinel–monoclinic layered (DSM) architectures. Unlike DS materials, which exhibit lower first‐charge capacities than discharge capacities, the monoclinic phase in DSM nanocomposites enables substantially improved first‐charge Li extraction, critical for practical Li‐ion batteries. The DSM nanocomposites deliver reversible capacities approaching 300 mAh g −1 and discharge specific energies exceeding 800 Wh kg −1 , while their cycling stability can be substantially improved by using a highly concentrated electrolyte and restricting the voltage window. This work establishes thermodynamically guided multiphase engineering as a strategy for addressing transport and stability limitations in DRX cathodes.

title: Field‐Free Brightening of Dark Excitons in a Two‐Dimensional Perovskite by Organic Spacer Fluorination
abstract: ABSTRACT Modifying the organic spacer is a powerful way to tune the excitonic properties of two‐dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (R–P) hybrid halide perovskites. Here, fluorination of the spacer, replacing phenylethylammonium (PEA) with 4‐fluorophenylethylammonium (4‐FPEA), is shown to brighten dark excitons in (4‐FPEA) 2 PbI 4 without an external magnetic field. Below 30 K, (4‐FPEA) 2 PbI 4 exhibits a sharp photoluminescence (PL) signal 7.8 meV below the bright exciton that is absent in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 . Its long lifetime, strong linear polarization, and quadratic magnetic‐field dependence identify this signal as dark‐exciton emission. A magnetic field of up to 0.7 T changes this emission only weakly, whereas it strongly brightens dark excitons in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 . The response is also asymmetric, with its minimum displaced from the zero field. This offset, absent in (PEA) 2 PbI 4 , points to a built‐in mixing of dark and bright states that acts as an internal field. Under two‐photon excitation, which generates excitons deep inside the crystal, the dark‐exciton emission persists. The brightening, therefore, originates in the bulk, unlike the surface‐related brightening reported for other 2D R–P perovskites. These results identify spacer fluorination as a simple chemical route to access spin‐forbidden excitonic states in 2D R–P perovskites.

Materials Control of Nitric Oxide in Cancer Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitric oxide (NO) can suppress antitumor immunity, support tumor adaptation, or promote immune‐mediated killing, making its therapeutic manipulation highly dependent on exposure. This Review examines how materials control NO source, localization, release kinetics, and chemical fate in cancer immunotherapy, with particular attention to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). We analyze polymeric donors, nanocarriers, injectable depots, and strategies for restricting endogenous NO production, linking their physicochemical properties to target exposure and immune function. Evidence from checkpoint‐treated models is distinguished from mechanisms established with other therapies and from human associations. Comparative analyses separate donor capacity from measured NO exposure, carrier accumulation from cellular delivery, and distant‐tumor control from demonstrated immune memory. Four overlapping endogenous contexts, comprising tumor adaptation, myeloid suppression, vascular dysfunction, and inflammatory effector activity, guide intervention design without constituting validated patient categories. We identify testable predictions concerning cellular selectivity, release kinetics, and spatial pharmacodynamic responses. Translation requires measurements that connect material behavior to a defined NO‐dependent process while demonstrating preservation of beneficial endothelial and immune functions. This framework provides a basis for evaluating when localized NO delivery or selective inhibition may support ICB, while recognizing the limits of current preclinical and clinical evidence.

title: Non‐Precious Metal High‐Entropy Oxide Sub‐1 nm Nanowires for Li‐O2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Highly active and structurally robust cathode catalysts are critically required to boost the electrochemical performance of lithium‐oxygen batteries (LOBs). Herein, a generally synthetic method of non‐precious metal high‐entropy oxide‐polyoxometalate sub‐1 nm nanowires (NPMHEO‐POM SNWs) has been successfully developed induced by POM clusters under mild solvothermal conditions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that the dominantly driving forces for the assembly of POMs and multi‐metal oxides are the Coulomb and van der Waals forces, enabling precise theoretical guidance for targeted material synthesis. Benefiting from the 1D ultrafine structure with fully exposed active sites, the precise adjustment of components optimizing the adsorption capability of intermediate (LiO 2 *) and discharge product (Li 2 O 2 ), and the strong interactions of multi‐metal oxides and POMs contributing to the stability, the BiVZrNiCeO x ‐phosphomolybdic acid SNWs‐based LOB achieves a highly specific capacity of 9944 mAh g −1 and stable cycling durability for 312 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , highlighting their great promise as high‐efficiency electrocatalysts for advanced LOBs.

title: Ultra‐Stable Phosphide Barrier Layer for Thermoelectric Bismuth Telluride
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The long‐term reliability of bismuth telluride (BT) thermoelectric power generation devices is severely constrained by the lack of reliable barrier layers. In this work, Ni 2 P is proposed as an ultra‐stable barrier layer for N‐type BT (N–BT). The low thermodynamic driving force for interfacial reaction and the sluggish Ni migration in Ni 2 P together ensure the favorable chemical inertness of the Ni 2 P/N–BT interface, while atomic‐scale bonding endows the interface with high bonding energy, leading to the lowest interfacial contact resistivity (∼1 µΩ cm 2 ), highest bonding strength (∼20 MPa), and longest verified stable duration at 523 K (90 days) among reported barrier layer systems. The resulting seven‐pair BT thermoelectric device achieves a maximum energy conversion efficiency of 6.9% at a temperature difference of 230 K. This work not only addresses the long‐standing bottleneck in power generation applications of BT‐based devices since the 1950s, but also provides guidance for barrier layer design in other thermoelectric systems.

title: Topological Superlattice Stabilized Layered Oxide Cathodes With Sustainable Anionic Redox
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing the oxygen anionic redox (OAR) at high voltage is envisaged as a fascinating approach to promote the energy density of rechargeable batteries. However, the layered transition metal (TM) oxide cathode materials with OAR activity suffer severely from detrimental phase transformations and local structural disorders, leading to electrochemical performance degradation. Herein, we propose a topological superlattice regulation strategy to construct a cathode material with the Li/Mg/Ni‐triple‐center honeycomb superlattice for sodium‐ion batteries. The combined theoretical and in/ex situ investigations demonstrate that the Li/Mg‐centered superlattice topology activates the OAR reaction to boost specific capacity, while the Ni‐centered honeycomb motif prevents the lattice oxygen release by increasing the TM−O covalency. Furthermore, the multi‐topology superlattice configuration suppresses the P−O phase transition and Li/TM interlayer/intralayer migration to reinforce the honeycomb superstructure stability, improving the oxygen redox reversibility. Consequently, the topological superlattice‐stabilized cathode delivers a high capacity of 242 mAh g −1 and exhibits outstanding cycling stability (91.8% capacity retention after 100 cycles). This work provides new insights into the superstructure regulation of state‐of‐the‐art cathode materials for sustainable batteries.

title: Quicklime Slaking‐Mediated Exothermic Reactions in Polidocanol‐Integrated Ablators with Inhibited Heat Diffusion Enable Cancer Thermal Ablation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite showing a wide application in tumor therapy, the clinically‐used exogenous thermal ablation still suffers from uncontrollable temperature field with rapid heat diffusion. Here an endogenous trigger‐encouraged thermal ablation, namely exothermic reaction‐based thermal ablation (ERTA) based on quicklime slaking and acid‐base neutralization reactions, has been established, wherein CaO nanoparticles were encapsulated with Ag nanoparticles by liposomes to construct ERTA ablators. CaO consumes H 2 O and H + after exothermic reactions to give birth to Ca 2+ and heat. Liposome shell prolongs ERTA via limiting the exothermic reaction rate, and intracellular Ca 2+ overload unites with Ag nanoparticles to produce antitumor ROS to boost cancer ERTA. Importantly, polidocanol‐based foam sclerosing agent (PFSA) with low heat conductivity was integrated to inhibit heat diffusion and confine heat in tumor to elevate temperature and enhance ERTA efficiency. Additionally, PFSA as a routine clinical embolism agent destroys intratumoral blood vessels to occlude blood vessels and establish starvation therapy, which further improves PFSA‐enhanced ERTA efficiency. Consequently, such ERTA‐based ablators and PFSA‐integrated ones outperform the scale‐matched microwave ablation and laboratory‐in photothermal ablation in repressing subcutaneous and orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma, and orthotopic pancreatic cancer. This endogenous trigger‐activated thermal ablation method provides distinctive insights into thermal ablation, presenting a new thermal ablation protocol.

title: Holistic evaluation for deployment
abstract: Thermoelectric technologies can convert waste heat directly into clean electricity, but high laboratory efficiency does not necessarily translate into practical deployment. By revisiting the long-neglected material zinc antimonide, researchers now show that strong thermoelectric performance can go hand in hand with affordability and sustainability.

title: Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres
abstract: The growing number of hyperscale data centres raises concerns about their environmental impacts. title: Unlocking sustainable thermoelectric generation with zinc antimonide
abstract: Thermoelectric technologies must balance conversion efficiency with resource sustainability. Here the authors demonstrate that eco-friendly zinc antimonide (ZnSb) is a viable materials choice, delivering ~8% efficiency alongside exceptional cost-effectiveness.

abstract: Climate warming is expanding thousands of glacial lakes with unstable natural dams, yet high-risk lakes remain outside formal safety oversight despite their potential for downstream harm. Extraction-Limited Charge Loss in Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Tin-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) present a promising lead-free alternative for photovoltaics, yet their performance remains markedly inferior to that of lead-based counterparts. A limited understanding of the underlying differences in charge transport dynamics between tin- and lead-based PSCs continues to impede efforts to overcome the reduced open-circuit voltage (Voc) and fill factor (FF) characteristic of tin-based devices. Here, using bias-modulated electrical transient measurements, we reveal a previously neglected extraction-limited charge loss mechanism in tin-based PSCs (efficiency > 14%) that is not evident in lead-based counterparts (> 25%) and fundamentally constrains both Voc and FF. Under high forward bias, the defects and their associated self-doping at the perovskite/electron transport layer interface severely reduce charge extraction efficiency by limiting the extraction of low-mobility carriers due to bulk field screening, which in turn leads to reduced collection efficiency as the unextracted carriers are forced into nonradiative recombination. This mechanism explains the low Voc and FF in tin-based PSCs and underscores interfacial doping control as critical for further performance enhancement.

title: Low-Temperature CO2 Desorption Enables Ammonium Carbonate Electrolysis Beyond pH Swing Limits
abstract: Abstract Bipolar membrane (BPM) electrolysis enables direct conversion of carbon capture solutions to fuels, eliminating energy-intensive CO2 purification and compression. However, CO2 desorption from potassium carbonate limits Faradaic efficiency (FE), with a theoretical maximum CO FE of 50% due to stoichiometric constraints. Here, we examine aqueous ammonia as an alternative carbon capture solution, where CO2 desorption can be enhanced using low-grade waste heat. Gas-phase CO2 release from 1 M ammonium carbonate increases 7.7-fold from 20 to 65 °C, increasing CO FE from 32 to 53% at 100 mA cm–2. This enhancement is consistent with increased CO2 availability from temperature-sensitive NH3–CO2–H2O equilibria. Using a hydrophilic SiO2-decorated Ni single-atom catalyst, we achieve 84% CO FE at 100 mA cm–2 with 2 M ammonium carbonate at 50 °C and 3 bar. Integration with a carbon capture absorber enables stable operation and electrolyte recapture, establishing a closed-loop capture-conversion process.

title: Multifunctional Dendrimer Interlayers for Tin-Based Perovskite Solar Cells: Inducing Interfacial Dipoles and Suppressing Electrode Corrosion
abstract: Abstract Tin-based perovskite solar cells (Sn-PSCs) offer eco-friendly optoelectronics but suffer from low efficiency and ambient instability. Here, we introduce a second-generation poly(amidoamine) (PAMAM) dendrimer interlayer between the C60/BCP electron transport layer and the Ag top electrode. Electrostatic field orientation induced by the metallic electrode activates a PAMAM dipole that shifts the effective interface work function by ∼0.55 eV. This modification of the interfacial energetics is accompanied by an increase in the open-circuit voltage (VOC) by ∼50 mV and is consistent with reduced contact-induced energetic losses. Additionally, the dendrimer forms a physical/chemical barrier against iodine-mediated electrode corrosion. Consequently, unencapsulated Sn-PSCs retain 80% of their initial power conversion efficiency (PCE) after 1000 h in ambient air (∼30 °C, 20–35% RH), a benchmark stability also demonstrated here for Sn–Pb PSCs. This electrode-induced dipole orientation presents a generalizable strategy for boosting efficiency and operational durability in lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Structural and Electronic Properties of Lead Halide Perovskite Thin-Film Surfaces
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Polycrystalline perovskite thin films are consistently associated with high-performance optoelectronic devices. The main challenges currently under the spotlight lie with the stability and reliability of these devices, requiring a better understanding of thin-film surfaces and interfaces. However, their consistent investigation is often very challenging. Given the soft nature of these materials, there is a struggle to directly assign the origin of the electronic features and correlate them to the chemical nature of the surfaces. Here, by exploiting a multimodal approach, we measure for the first time, at submicrometer scales, the diffraction patterns of the thin-film grain surface, which provide the material fingerprint and experimental evidence that the surface of such soft semiconductors is not as disordered as often claimed. Then, building on such knowledge, we move to ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy, which provides information about the electronic structure of the first few nanometers of the thin-film surface. Having identified the structural nature of the surface, we are eventually able to unambiguously assign the origin of the photoemission spectra for a wide range of metal halide perovskites. In particular, metallic lead is identified to be the origin of the often-reported midgap photoemissive states, thus far assigned to deep electronic states within the halide perovskite semiconductor band gap. The chemical composition of the metal halides, the photodegradation of the perovskites under visible light, the quality of the precursors, and the actual stoichiometry of the thin film heavily define the presence of such states and elucidate the origin of carrier loss, photodegradation, and sample reproducibility in metal halide perovskite optoelectronics.

title: Guest-Mediated On-Surface Growth of 2D COF Heterobilayer for Synaptic Devices
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Chemically defined organic heterobilayers offer a route to programmable interfacial coupling, yet their on-surface construction remains challenging due to the instability of dynamic covalent frameworks during sequential growth. Here, we report a guest-induced COF-on-COF growth strategy that enables deterministic heteroepitaxy of imine/boroxine covalent organic framework (COF) heterobilayers at solid–liquid interfaces. Coronene guest molecules occupy the pores of the underlying imine COF, stabilizing the framework while promoting interfacial molecular diffusion, thereby redirecting growth from framework degradation to directional epitaxy. This yields a structurally precise heterobilayer with a commensurate √3 × √3 R30° rotational relationship and long-range order. The resulting 2D COF heterobilayer is continuous over large areas with low defect density, enabling direct device integration without transfer. Electrical measurements, supported by theory, reveal interfacial charge redistribution arising from chemically encoded asymmetry, manifested as interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced charge trapping. Device responses, including nonvolatile switching and analogue conductance modulation, provide a macroscopic readout of the molecularly defined heterointerface. These results establish a route to programmable organic heterostructures in which interfacial growth, coupling, and electronic functionality are codesigned through molecular assembly.

title: Proton-Coupled Electrostatic Regulation of Anion Electrosorption in Electric Double Layers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Electric double layers underpin electrochemical energy storage and modulate interfacial reactivity through the organization of ions and solvent molecules. However, regulating anion accumulation at compact aqueous interfaces while limiting parasitic water reactions remains challenging. Here, anodic polarization reconstructs oxygen-deficient TiO2–x into a depth-graded architecture comprising a rutile interior, a disordered interlayer, and a thin crystalline anatase surface. This architecture establishes an internal electric field that promotes subsurface proton accumulation, creating a responsive charge distribution that regulates anion electrosorption and moderates lateral anion interactions. The thin crystalline surface complements this electrostatic regulation by extending the accessible anodic operating range, combining enhanced interfacial charge storage with high-voltage aqueous operation. Symmetric aqueous supercapacitors sustain cycling over 3.0 V in neutral Na2SO4 for 45,000 cycles and over 2.7 V in natural seawater. These findings identify subsurface ionic chemistry as a design variable for regulating anion electrosorption at aqueous oxide interfaces.

title: Secondary Solvation Shell Regulation for Fast-Charging Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Most electrolyte strategies in lithium metal batteries (LMBs) target the first solvation shell or solvation diversity. However, such approaches have shown limited success in enabling fast-charging, as Li+ depletion inevitably develops at polarized interfaces. Here, we identify the secondary solvation shell as a critical regulator of fast-charging stability and show that a gradient solvation structure (GSS) overcomes ion depletion-induced failure. Guided by intrinsic solvation strengths, we design a tri-solvent electrolyte comprising 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), 1,1,1-trifluoro-2,3-dimethoxypropane (TFDMP), and N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethane-sulfonamide (DMTMSA). DME and TFDMP define a stable primary solvation shell and balanced ion-pair distribution, whereas DMTMSA localizes in the secondary shell, suppressing long-range ionic clustering and maintaining interfacial ion availability. Despite similar primary-shell structures and equilibrium impedances, only the tri-solvent system preserves interfacial kinetics under depletion conditions. This architecture enables a Coulombic efficiency of 98.4% at 16 mA cm–2, a specific capacity of 162.0 mAh g–1 at 10C, and 90.4% capacity retention for 200 cycles. These findings establish a gradient solvation structure as a governing principle for fast-charging LMB electrolytes.

title: Thiol-ene Radical Polymerizations of Regio - and Stereo -Isomers of a CO2-Derived δ-Lactone Leading to High Molar Mass Polythioethers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Thiol-ene radical polymerization of CO2-derived lactones containing α,δ-dienes offers a route to sustainable polythioethers with up to 20 wt % CO2. The direct product from CO2/1,3-butadiene telomerization is 3-ethylidene-6-vinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one ((E)EVP) whose α-alkylidene group causes poor reaction kinetics and nonquantitative alkene conversion with dithiols affording low molar mass polythioethers. Here, we use 3,6-divinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one (DVP) which was synthesized from the base-catalyzed contrathermodynamic α,β- to β,γ-photodeconjugation of EVP, resulting in the transformation of the α-alkylidene to an α-vinyl functional group. This subtle regio-isomerization was found to result in a 17-fold and 8-fold increase in the rate of α- and δ-ene consumption, respectively, owing to the relative stability of the intermediate carbon-centered radicals. Leveraging these rapid kinetics, high molar mass polythioethers (34 kDa) could be prepared via thiol-ene step-growth polymerization of DVP with 2,2’-(ethylenedioxy)diethanethiol. These molar masses are 10-fold higher than the upper limits obtained with the EVP-derived counterpart, and the polythioethers display mechanical performance suitable as a pressure sensitive adhesive.

title: A Mirror-Image L-RNA Aptamer Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Promoter G-Quadruplex Potentiates Tumor Radiotherapy In Vivo
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) coordinates the response of tumors to low oxygen by stimulating genes involved in metabolism and angiogenesis. HIF pathway activation is highly associated with tumor progression and radiotherapy resistance. Ligands that target this pathway are potential agents for the treatment of solid tumor malignancies. We developed an L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt5–4, targeting the HIF-1α promoter DNA G-quadruplex (dG4) via mirror-image SELEX. This L-RNA aptamer adopts a stem-loop secondary structure, binds HIF-1α dG4 with high affinity and specificity, and enters the nucleus to effectively downregulate HIF-1α and its downstream targets in cancer cells. By suppressing HIF-1α, L-Apt5–4 not only inhibits tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, but also acts as a potent radiosensitizer, synergizing with radiotherapy to enhance cancer cell death. The combination therapy significantly suppresses tumor growth and metastasis while exhibiting excellent biosafety in vivo. Thus, L-Apt5–4 represents a novel HIF-1α-targeted therapeutic and radiosensitizer for combined cancer treatment.

title: Antiaromaticity for Through-Space Molecular Thermoelectricity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Charge transport in molecular junctions has largely relied on aromatic frameworks, where intramolecular π-delocalization stabilizes the electronic structure but inherently limits intermolecular electronic coupling. Here we show that antiaromatic Ni(II) norcorrole assemblies outperform their aromatic counterparts in thermally driven charge transport. This superior performance arises from strong intermolecular coupling, facilitated by the externalized electronic stabilization of antiaromatic building blocks. Such strong intermolecular coupling enables unusually thick molecular stacks within molecular junctions and yields Seebeck coefficients of up to 600 μV K–1, far exceeding those of the aromatic analogue. Quantum transport calculations reveal that π–π stacking in the antiaromatic assemblies shifts the HOMO transmission resonance closer to the Fermi level while progressively narrowing it, accounting for the substantial enhancement of the Seebeck coefficient while maintaining efficient long-range charge transport with a low tunneling attenuation coefficient. These findings establish antiaromaticity as a design principle for thermoelectric energy conversion based on collective intermolecular coupling rather than isolated molecular orbitals.

title: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Spin state offers a fundamental yet underexplored handle for controlling stereoselectivity in transition-metal catalysis. Here we show that metal-centered spin-state switching, within an invariant weak-field bipyridine framework, promotes E/Z divergence in allylic substitution, enabling access to geometrically defined allylamines from common precursors. High-spin Ni catalysts selectively afford E-allylamines, whereas low-spin Pd catalysts deliver the corresponding Z-isomers. Broad metal studies with Fe, Rh and Ir systems further support the association between metal-centered spin state and alkene geometry. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory (DFT) analyses reveal the origin of this stereodivergent outcome: spin-state-dependent electronic structures reshape catalyst–substrate interactions, thereby selectively stabilizing the competing E- or Z-forming transition states. The paired E/Z products enable concise syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant molecules and reveal configuration-dependent biological activities. This work establishes catalyst spin state as a design parameter for the stereodivergent control of alkene geometry.

title: Expanding Chemical Space Enables Data–Driven Structure–Activity Relationships in Cage Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Data-driven approaches are increasingly popular in catalysis, supplementing and even replacing traditional strategies that relied on empirical optimization. However, their application in the field of bioinspired cage catalysis remains largely unexplored, primarily due to the limited chemical space of known catalytically active cages. As a result, mechanistic insights are often obtained using computationally intensive DFT calculations on a handful of structurally similar cages. As chemical systems grow in complexity, this approach becomes impractical. Herein, we report a framework that significantly expedites the exploration of a much wider structural landscape while offering computational insights. This is made possible by a novel in situ experimental procedure─which circumvents the traditional time-consuming process of prepare, isolate, characterize, and test─coupled with data-driven methods to identify molecular features that govern activity. Using this approach, we experimentally explore 30 unique PdnL2n cages (n = 2–4) that mediate a nitro-aldol reaction with activities spanning over 4 orders of magnitude. Using this data set, a random forest model trained on molecular descriptors was developed to predict ΔG‡ (MAE of 0.4 kcal mol–1 and R2 = 0.9). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted geometric preorganization and electrostatic interactions within the cage as key determinants of catalytic efficiency. Moreover, DFT calculations on a selection of cages further validated these insights, indicating that meaningful mechanistic understanding can be achieved at significantly reduced computational cost. We anticipate that this integrated, screening, data-driven, mechanistic strategy will provide a blueprint workflow for understanding metal–organic cage reactivity and encourage the generation of more comprehensive structural data sets, ultimately enabling the rational design of improved catalytic architectures.

title: Correlative Multidimensional Tracking and Modeling Reveals Mechanical Regulation of Nanoparticle Endocytosis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Understanding nanoparticle–membrane interactions during endocytosis is critical for advancing nanomedicine. However, a comprehensive understanding of its dynamic complexity remains elusive, largely due to limitations in often oversimplified theoretical models and experimental challenges in correlating nanoparticle conformations and protein assemblies. To bridge this persistent theoretical–experimental divide, we developed an integrated approach combining multidimensional single-particle tracking with theoretical modeling for understanding clathrin-mediated endocytosis of rod-shaped nanoparticle cargos in live cells. Real-time tracking reveals a characteristic seesaw-like rotational motion of nanocargos that is temporally correlated with clathrin and dynamin recruitment, enabling the endocytic process to be classified into six distinct stages. Theoretical modeling, informed by these experimental observations, identifies orientation-dependent energy preferences arising from the interplay between membrane-associated effects and clathrin lattice elasticity, yielding orientation trends consistent with experimental observations. By focusing on this core structural framework, our work establishes a quantitative foundation for understanding how geometric and mechanical interactions govern the nanoparticle internalization. This correlative experimental and theoretical work is exemplary of the renewed efforts to establish closer connections between experimental evidence and theoretical modeling with higher biological complexity.

title: Hydration Shell Structure and Water-Mediated Binding of Closo -Dodecaborates Probed by Raman Hydration-Shell Spectroscopy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The binding of closo-dodecaborates, B12X122– (where X = H, Cl, Br, I), to solutes and interfaces has widely been attributed to a water-mediated (super)chaotropic effect. The role of water, however, has so far been inferred only indirectly from thermodynamic measurements. Herein, we employ Raman hydration-shell spectroscopy in the OH stretch region to investigate B12X122– in aqueous solution. Specifically, we elucidate (i) the water structure in the hydration shell, (ii) its temperature dependence, and (iii) the water release upon superchaotropic binding. The hydration-shell spectra reveal that all dodecaborates give rise to a sharp Raman band close to 3600 cm–1. This feature is strongly blue-shifted compared to bulk water and represents weakly H-bonded, “almost dangling” OH groups in the hydration shell. Heating is found to blue-shift the hydration water resonance less than the bulk water resonance. Hydration and bulk water resonances thus become more similar at high temperature. This trend reflects a progressively reduced difference in hydrogen-bonding energy upon heating between hydration and bulk water, and is opposite to that of hydrophobic hydration. Furthermore, hydration difference spectra in the presence of the nonionic polymer hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) reveal that weakly H-bonded hydration water is released from B12X122– upon superchaotropic binding, together with more strongly H-bonded hydration water from the hydration shells of both B12X122– and HPC. These findings identify weakly bound hydration water, its weak temperature dependence, and its spontaneous release upon binding as molecular hallmarks of the superchaotropic behavior of B12X122–.

title: Planar-Chiral Metal Clusters Direct Polarization-Responsive Supercrystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Chiral metal clusters are promising atomically precise building blocks for hierarchical chiral materials, but their programmed assembly into structurally resolved supercrystals with traceable chirality transfer remains challenging. Here, we show that planar-chiral Cu5 clusters can serve as symmetry-defined modules for constructing polarization-responsive supercrystals. Through single-site capping control and symmetry-matched linker-directed coordination assembly, the Cu5 unit is organized into monomeric, dimeric, trimeric, and helical crystalline architectures, thereby enabling chirality to be traced from discrete clusters to higher-order supercrystalline structures. Single-crystal analyses reveal how the planar chirality of the cluster is encoded locally and propagated through distinct, orientationally ordered packing sequences. Quantitative Mueller matrix measurements show architecture-dependent circular and linear optical responses, including circular and linear retardance, which correlate with the crystallographic orientation and packing sequence of the Cu5 units, particularly Cu···Cu bonding. This work establishes planar-chiral metal clusters as versatile, stereochemically programmable synthons, providing a quantitative framework that links cluster-level chirality, arrangement orientation, and macroscopic polarization-dependent optical responses. The strategy offers a novel modular route to structurally defined chiral supercrystals, in which optical polarization responses can be traced to atomically resolved anisotropic sequences of chiral cluster assembly.

title: Regio- and Diastereoselective Thiol-ene Click Reaction and Application for the Synthesis of Semicrystalline Polythioethers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Thiol-ene click is a powerful reaction for its high efficiency, functional-group tolerance, and operational simplicity, yet regio- and stereocontrol in radical thiol addition to internal alkenes as well as its potential use in the stereoselective synthesis of semicrystalline polymers has received much less attention. Here, we report a substrate-enabled, perfectly (>99%) regio- and diastereoselective thiol-ene click reaction of a bicyclic lactone alkene, BiL=, with diverse thiols and its application in thiol-ene photopolymerization to regio- and stereoregular polythioethers (PTEs) with excellent thermomechanical and barrier properties. Using either racemic (rac) BiL= or enantiopure (1S,5S)-BiL=, the reaction proceeds through the same highly regio- and facial-selective addition pathway to afford the preferred thioether product, with rac-BiL= forming an enantiomeric pair of diastereomers and (1S,5S)-BiL= affording a single diastereomer. This unique selectivity is translatable into regio- and diastereoselective step-growth photopolymerization between a bis(bicyclic lactone alkene), Bis-BiL=, and various dithiols, affording semicrystalline PTEs with melting temperature up to 131 °C, high thermal stability, tunable mechanical properties, melt processability, and excellent oxygen-barrier performance. The inherently available main-chain postmodification sites in the PTE structure can be readily utilized to achieve reversible or irreversible modifications of the polymer main-chain structure, further modulating material performance.

title: Electronic Polarization of Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy. This unique pore environment promotes the uptake and transport of polar solvents, while enhancing separation selectivity by retarding highly polar solutes through polarity-dependent solute-framework interactions. Furthermore, the low surface energy imparted by the robust C–F bonds also reduces irreversible foulant adhesion and facilitates permeance recovery after cleaning. The resultant COF membrane achieves a molecular weight cutoff down to 350 Da and stable operation for over 550 h. Notably, it differentiates structurally related fluoroquinolone antibiotics according to their molecular polarity and delivers a favorable separation factor of 8.9 for norfloxacin over its synthetic intermediate piperazine. This work demonstrates that engineering pore-wall polarity in COF membranes provides a viable route to chemically regulated molecular recognition beyond size-based separation.

title: Zeolite Crystallization via Seed-Mediated Chemical Vapor Deposition
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The demand for zeolites with specific, tailored characteristics is expected to further accelerate. For decades, however, zeolites have been predominantly synthesized by hydrothermal methods, in which tightly coupled sol–gel processes, nucleation, and crystal growth constrain property control and complicate device-oriented fabrication. Here we report the direct synthesis of zeolites by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), in which vapor-delivered precursors crystallize on preexisting zeolite seeds. Mechanistic investigations reveal that zeolite growth under CVD follows a fundamentally distinct pathway, where vapor-phase hydrolysis–condensation reactions are spatially decoupled from interfacial crystallization. This decoupling enables the maintenance of a controlled and steady supersaturation, offering a facile strategy for fabricating zeolite films with low dielectric constants and robust mechanical properties. The unique mechanism and operation mode of CVD bring zeolite crystallization into a manufacturing-relevant vapor-phase regime that could be extended to other zeolite types and deployed in diverse applications.

title: Disrupting Hidden Antiaromaticity in N -Hydroxyphthalimide Reveals a Design Principle for Highly Reactive N -Oxyl Hydrogen Atom Transfer Mediators
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) and its corresponding N-oxyl radical, phthalimide N-oxyl (PINO), have long been used as mediators for hydrogen atom transfer (HAT), particularly in radical-mediated C–H oxidations. Although numerous NHPI/PINO derivatives have been developed, the absence of an intuitive model connecting scaffold structure to intrinsic HAT reactivity has left catalyst development largely empirical. Herein, we show that insertion of a heteroatom between one carbonyl group of the NHPI/PINO framework and the fused aryl ring substantially accelerates HAT in electrochemically driven oxidations, with rate enhancements of up to 36-fold for benzylic alcohol substrates. This enhanced reactivity correlates with significantly larger computed O–H bond dissociation enthalpies relative to NHPI (ΔBDEO–H = 6.5–8.1 kcal/mol), which increase the thermodynamic driving force for HAT by the corresponding N-oxyl radicals. NICS, NBO, and DFT-based structural analyses support a model in which previously overlooked antiaromatic destabilization within the five-membered imide motif weakens the O–H bond of NHPI and is relieved upon formation of PINO. Among the heteroatom-containing analogues examined, sulfur-containing N-hydroxythiobenzouracil (NHTBU) provided a favorable balance of high HAT reactivity and catalyst persistence, enabling the electrochemical oxidation of numerous substrates under mild conditions with activity superior to NHPI.

title: Detecting Catalytically Competent Surface-Bound Hydrogen on Electrocatalysts with Weak Acids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The characterization of catalytically competent molecular metal-hydride intermediates distinguishes mechanistic possibilities in reductive molecular electrocatalysis. While surface-bound hydrogen is invoked in several heterogeneous electrocatalytic schemes, the synthetic and spectroscopic tools to establish catalytic competence in molecular systems are not readily translated to surfaces. Molecular systems offer uniform and well-defined active sites; however, surface systems consist of multiple possible binding sites. Here, we discover that the judicious choice of the proton donor enables the independent generation and characterization of catalytically competent surface-bound hydrogen using hydrogen evolution as a model reaction. Using dimethyl sulfoxide, a solvent where Brønsted acid pKa values are well-characterized, and Ag electrocatalysts, compatible with surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (SEIRAS), we find that acids with pKa values higher than the protonated solvent generate spectroscopic signatures consistent with the reductive formation of long-lived and linearly bound hydrogen. Conversely, stronger acids that protonate the solvent do not give rise to detectable surface-bound hydrogen, and instead, yield electrokinetic data consistent with hydrogen evolution proceeding via rate-limiting formation of the same linearly bound surface hydrogen. By independently generating the Ag-bound hydrogen with a weak, general acid and subsequently introducing a stronger acid that protonates the solvent, we show that the accumulated surface-bound hydrogen is catalytically competent for hydrogen production via specific-acid-coupled electron transfer. Our work demonstrates that catalytically competent surface-bound hydrogen intermediates in heterogeneous electrocatalysis can be detected and characterized through the strategic choice of the proton donor.

title: Chemical Control of Quorum Sensing Rewires Mixed Bacterial Communities
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Microbial communities are central to host and environmental health, yet their dysregulation can drive diseases. Chemical strategies for selectively reprogramming community composition remain limited. Here, we show that agonists of the accessory gene regulator (agr) quorum sensing system provide a powerful, nonbactericidal approach to reshape staphylococcal biofilm communities. In mixed biofilms of multiple Staphylococcus epidermidis strains, selective agr activation produces pronounced sequence-dependent shifts in community composition in vitro. This targeted remodeling enhances the susceptibility of the community to antibiotic treatment. Extending this strategy to interspecies systems, we demonstrate that agr agonists reduce the abundance of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by >95% in mixed biofilms with S. epidermidis without relying on bactericidal activity. Notably, the efficacy of agr-mediated community control is modulated by iron availability, revealing an environmental layer of regulation. Together, these findings support quorum sensing agonism as a chemically precise strategy to manipulate microbial communities by exploiting intrinsic signaling differences with implications spanning human health and agriculture.

title: Highly Tunable Metal-Peptide Piezoelectrics for Tissue Regeneration
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Piezoelectricity, first discovered in 1880, has been dominated by inorganic materials, whose strong electromechanical responses typically arise from achiral, noncentrosymmetric crystal structures and highly polar bonds. However, their brittleness and poor biosafety, biocompatibility and biodegradability under physiological conditions severely limit biomedical applications and clinical translation. Here we report a general design strategy for constructing a distinct class of highly tunable metal-peptide piezoelectrics that enable efficient tissue repair and regeneration. By coordinating metal ions with sequence-defined peptides, we achieve molecular-level control over crystal symmetry, polarization and mechanical stiffness across 25 single-crystal structures. The resulting crystals generate strong polarization and exhibit piezoelectric responses up to 227.4 pm V–1, representing a 65-fold enhancement through side-chain engineering, and enable nanogenerators with stable electrical output. They are chemically robust, cytocompatible, and promote tenocyte proliferation and extracellular matrix production. In rat and porcine tendon injury models, the d-enantiomeric system substantially outperformed its l-form counterpart by driving transcriptional reprogramming toward regenerative signaling, thereby overcoming intrinsic limitations of natural tendon repair. These findings establish metal–peptide assemblies as a versatile platform for biointegrated piezoelectrics and identify chirality as a previously unrecognized determinant of piezoelectricity-mediated tissue regeneration.

title: Regulating Functionalized MXene Crystal-Field Splitting toward Efficient Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis of Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract MXenes offer fast conductive frameworks with abundant intrinsic active metal sites, making them promising cathode catalysts for lithium–oxygen batteries for addressing sluggish oxygen kinetics and severe cathode passivation. However, the predictive electronic descriptors for rationally regulating these intrinsic active sites remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of crystal-field splitting engineering at Ti sites of Ti3C2-MXene to achieve bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis. Through coordinated anionic and cationic modifications, we regulate the local coordination environment of Ti atoms, weakening crystal-field splitting and promoting electron delocalization within Ti3C2-MXene frameworks. X-ray absorption spectra reveal systematic shifts of Ti K-edge and contraction of the pre-edge splitting, consistent with weakened and distorted Ti ligand fields. This electronic rearrangement promotes an asymmetric Li2O2 adsorption configuration, thereby lowering the energy barriers for both ORR and OER. Consequently, the functionalized Cu–Ti3C2Br2 delivers a high discharge specific capacity of 11,662 mAh g–1 and reduces the initial charge overpotential by 50% compared with Ti3C2OF. This study indicates crystal-field splitting as a key descriptor governing oxygen electrocatalytic behavior in lithium–oxygen batteries.

title: Stimulus-Driven Reconfigurable Memristors with Volatile-to-Nonvolatile Transition for Spatiotemporal Neuromorphic Computing
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic hardware for spatiotemporal information processing requires both transient dynamics and programmable weight storage, whereas existing implementations typically rely either on heterogeneous integration of volatile dynamic units and nonvolatile memory devices or on compliance-current regulation to reconfigure volatile/nonvolatile operation within a single device, increasing device diversity or peripheral control complexity. This work reports a stimulus-reconfigurable Ag/ZnS/FTO memristor in which the stability of Ag conductive pathways is regulated by the strength and temporal scale of external stimuli, enabling volatile short-term dynamics and nonvolatile conductance modulation within a single device. Under weak or short stimuli, the device exhibits multiscale short-term plasticity governed by pulse amplitude, width, interval, and number, enabling Morse-code temporal encoding. Under strong or prolonged stimuli, it realizes long-term potentiation/depression and multilevel conductance modulation. Leveraging this dual-mode behavior, a volatile–nonvolatile reservoir computing architecture is constructed, where volatile responses act as reservoir states for dynamic feature expansion and nonvolatile conductance stores readout weights. For spatial image recognition, the architecture achieves 92.94 and 82.27% accuracies on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, respectively, with an estimated 84.5% fewer devices than a purely nonvolatile multilayer perceptron. The same architecture further achieves 96.13% accuracy and a 95.14% Macro F1 score in ECG heartbeat classification, highlighting a unified device strategy for hardware-efficient spatiotemporal neuromorphic computing.

title: Exchange-Bias-Gated Temporal Memory in PtMn/NiFe Heterostructures for Physical Pattern Recognition
abstract: Abstract Physical information processing relies on the ability of a dynamical system to transform external stimuli into distinguishable internal states. Although nonlinear magnetization dynamics in magnetic materials exhibit memory and rich dynamical behavior, engineering responses that depend on the temporal ordering of inputs remains a central challenge for spintronics-based physical computing. Here, we show that exchange-biased PtMn/NiFe heterostructures create input-selective magnetic state spaces through history-dependent magnetization dynamics driven by microwave excitation. Above a threshold microwave power, nonlinear excitation modifies the interfacial magnetic configuration so that sequences delivering identical total excitation energy but differing in temporal order evolve into distinct resonance states. Short four-bit microwave pulse sequences generate sixteen experimentally distinguishable magnetic resonance conditions, with only a selective subset of patterns producing large state transitions and yielding sparse activation. Using the shifted resonance fields as physical features, a multinomial logistic regression classifier achieves 88.5% accuracy on the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) handwritten-digit recognition task. These results establish exchange-biased antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interfaces as an effective platform for engineering history-dependent magnetic state spaces and demonstrate that the interfacial spin dynamics can perform temporal information processing of short pulse sequences directly in hardware, with relevance to edge artificial intelligence, radar, and sensing applications.

title: Hydroxy-Functionalized n-Type OMIECs as Multifunctional Conductive Biointerfaces for Simplified Biosensor Fabrication
abstract: Abstract Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) have emerged as key materials for bioelectronics owing to their ability to couple ionic and electronic transport. However, their potential as multifunctional biointerfaces for biosensing remains largely untapped, particularly for n-type systems. Here, we report a hydroxy-functionalized n-doped poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO-OH) that unifies efficient electron transport and enzyme immobilization within a single material platform. By introducing terminal hydroxy groups into the polymer backbone, PBFDO-OH enables the direct immobilization of glucose dehydrogenase through a simple one-pot strategy, eliminating the gold substrates, self-assembled monolayers, and multistep surface activation protocols that underpin conventional biosensor fabrication. This streamlined approach yields robust biofunctional electrodes with enhanced electrochemical performance while preserving enzyme activity and long-term stability. Integrated with additively manufactured electrodes, the resulting glucose biosensor demonstrates a high sensitivity of 17.4 μA L mmol–1, a low detection limit of 3.42 μmol L-1, excellent reproducibility (RSD = 5.35%), reliable quantification in human serum (RSD

title: HIFU-Enhanced Transdermal Delivery of Hyaluronic-Acid-Functionalized Solid Lipid Nanoparticles for Localized Melanoma Therapy
abstract: Abstract Cutaneous melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer for which localized treatment remains difficult because of limited drug penetration through the stratum corneum and the systemic toxicity of conventional chemotherapy. Here, we developed a noninvasive physicochemical platform combining hyaluronic acid (HA)-functionalized paclitaxel-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) with high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) for localized melanoma therapy. The optimized SLNs exhibited a hydrodynamic diameter of 134.6 ± 4.2 nm and a zeta potential of –22.3 ± 1.5 mV. HIFU induced changes in the structural organization of the lipid matrix, accelerating paclitaxel release and enhancing skin penetration. In vitro, SLNs with HIFU reduced B16F10 melanoma cell viability to below 20% while maintaining approximately 65% viability of HaCaT keratinocytes. The combined treatment increased intracellular ROS generation by 6.2-fold and enhanced apoptotic signaling. In ex vivo porcine skin, HIFU-assisted delivery of coumarin-6-loaded SLNs increased fluorescence penetration to approximately 1500 μm, compared with 750 μm without HIFU. In B16F10 tumor-bearing mice, topical SLNs combined with HIFU under mild hyperthermia (41–43 °C) achieved 90.1% tumor growth inhibition at Day 8, 81.5% tumor necrosis, and 86.5% TUNEL-positive cells without significant body-weight loss or treatment-related toxicity. These findings support HIFU-enhanced SLNs as a potential strategy for improving cutaneous paclitaxel delivery and suppressing localized melanoma growth.

title: In Situ Synthesis of Quantum Dot–Polymer Nanocomposites: Mechanisms, Interfacial Engineering, and Optoelectronic Applications
abstract: Abstract Quantum dot (QD)–polymer nanocomposites have emerged as promising optoelectronic materials for next-generation technologies, including high-performance displays, photovoltaics, optical sensing, and bioimaging systems. Nevertheless, conventional physical blending strategies for fabricating QD–polymer composites face critical limitations such as environmentally unfriendly processing protocols, aggregation-induced fluorescence quenching, and compromised photoluminescence stability, which collectively hinder their practical implementation. In situ synthesis of QDs within polymer matrices has recently emerged as a transformative methodology to address these challenges. This comprehensive review systematically examines three categories of in situ synthesized QDs (II–VI, IV–VI, and perovskite nanostructures) within diverse polymeric architectures, including conventional thermoplastics, block copolymers, and conjugated polymers. A critical analysis is presented on how polymer composition (e.g., functional groups and chain mobility) and nanostructural design (e.g., micellar confinement and template-directed assembly) govern the nucleation kinetics, crystallographic features, and optoelectronic properties of QDs. The review further highlights cutting-edge applications spanning ultrasensitive chemical detection, multimodal bioimaging platforms, and high-color-purity QD-LED displays. Finally, we discuss fundamental challenges and propose strategic directions for scalable manufacturing, focusing on interface engineering and stability enhancement. With the advent of solution-processable polymer platforms and precision nanofabrication techniques, in situ QD–polymer nanocomposite synthesis is poised to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial-scale production in optoelectronic device manufacturing.

title: Suppressing Photoinduced Phase Segregation in Wide-Bandgap Perovskites via Guanidinium-Thiocyanate-Mediated Electrical Homogenization
abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap perovskites are pivotal for tandem photovoltaics but suffer from photoinduced halide segregation, where grain boundaries (GBs) act as hotspots for ion redistribution. Here, we show that suppressing this instability is associated with coordinated grain-growth regulation and more uniform electrical response across grain interiors and grain boundaries. Among the four thiocyanate (SCN–)-based additives, GASCN produces a compact, predominantly large-grained morphology accompanied by more uniform nanoscale current distribution. Correlative photoluminescence (PL) and time-resolved PL mapping further indicate that GASCN treatment suppresses photoinduced carrier accumulation at GBs, a phenomenon pronounced in small-grained regions. Kelvin probe force microscopy further uncovers that GASCN induces an inversion of the GB surface potential, reconstructing the local electrostatic environment to oppose halide redistribution under illumination. As a result, GASCN-treated films exhibit stabilized absorption edges, negligible PL peak shifts, and suppressed lattice expansion upon light soaking. Combined with interfacial passivation, the devices deliver a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.25% with an open-circuit voltage of 1.34 V. This work establishes coordinated grain-growth regulation and nanoscale electrical homogenization as a design principle for stabilizing mixed-halide perovskites, and provides direct nanoscale evidence for electrostatic modulation at GBs as a suppression mechanism against photoinduced phase segregation.

title: Supramolecular Matrine-Proanthocyanidins Nanocomplex-Integrated Carboxymethyl Chitosan Hydrogel with Phenylboronic Acid Modification for Atopic Dermatitis Therapy
