abstract: Abstract Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease featured by immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, and an impaired epidermal barrier. Oxidative stress and inflammation establish a self-sustaining vicious cycle that accelerates the progression of atopic dermatitis. However, few naturally derived self-assembled nanohydrogels have been developed to disrupt this reciprocal loop for the treatment of cutaneous AD. In this study, matrine (MAT) and proanthocyanidins (PAC), two Chinese medicine-derived molecules with inherent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, co-assembled spontaneously into nanoparticles (PM NPs) in aqueous solution. Incorporation of PM NPs into the phenylboronic acid-modified carboxymethyl chitosan (CP) crosslinked network enhanced the mechanical strength of carboxymethyl chitosan, forming a composite hydrogel (CPPM). Spectral results verified that PM NP self-assembly was mediated by hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking. CPPM efficiently scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), suppressed the activation of the Ox-CaMKII and NF-κB signaling pathways, and activated Nrf2 to restore epidermal redox homeostasis. CPPM exhibited favorable moisturizing capacity, appropriate rheological properties, and mild ROS-triggered release to realize local therapeutic effects. In 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB)-induced AD mice, topical CPPM application significantly alleviated epidermal hyperplasia, itching, and inflammatory cytokine expression without obvious toxicity. This self-assembled bioactive hydrogel can concurrently regulate oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, offering a promising topical therapeutic approach against AD.

title: Scale-Dependent Friction in Rough SiO2/Single-Crystal MoS2 Contacts
abstract: Abstract The scale limits of superlubricity in realistic multiasperity contacts remain poorly understood. Although lateral atomic-force cancellation in incommensurate or disordered interfaces can generate low friction, how experimentally accessible contact size, local stress state, and load distribution regulate this scale-dependent behavior remains unclear. Here, we investigate the scale-dependent shear strength of SiO2 glass sphere/single-crystal MoS2 contacts with different sphere radii using atomic force microscopy and a custom microtribometer across extended load ranges. By combining power spectral density-based random rough surface generation with boundary element method simulations, we evaluate a dimensionless contact-scale parameter ai/bcore,i defined by the ratio between contact-patch radius and a characteristic elastic core width in rough multiasperity interfaces. The results show that the effective shear strength decreases continuously with increasing real contact area at small-to-intermediate contact scales, consistent with enhanced statistical cancellation of lateral atomic forces expected for disordered interfaces. As contact scale further increases, this reduction is progressively suppressed as the maximum scale parameter (ai/bcore,i)max approaches unity and an increasing fraction of the load is carried by contact patches satisfying ai/bcore,i > 1. The R = 2.5 mm probe condition exhibits a higher effective shear strength and a broader simulated contact-pressure distribution than the smaller-probe conditions. However, because sphere radius and the measured roughness spectrum were not independently varied, these differences cannot be attributed uniquely to sphere curvature. Instead, they reflect the combined influence of probe geometry, roughness statistics, and the resulting multiasperity contact state. Our results establish a multiscale framework linking atomic-force cancellation, finite contact-size effects, and rough-contact statistics, revealing how structural superlubricity gradually loses its scale invariance in realistic multiasperity interfaces.

title: A Multifunctional Core–Sheath Fiber Patch Based on Cellulose Nanocrystal-Reinforced and Curcumin-Loaded Polylactic Acid for Enhanced Pelvic Tissue Repair
abstract: Abstract Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) affects millions of women due to tissue defect, marked by disrupted collagen homeostasis and abnormal immune reaction. Therefore, there is a demand for developing a multifunctional patch resolving these current straits. Herein, we fabricated a multifunctional core–sheath fibrous patch via coaxial electrospinning, comprising cellulose nanocrystal (CNC)-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) sheath and curcumin-loaded PLA core. Post-electrospinning heat treatment enhanced PLA crystallinity improved mechanical properties and enabled sustained curcumin release. The patch exhibited stable degradation, good biocompatibility, and potent anti-inflammatory activity. In vivo, the CNC-PLA/Cur-h patch achieved native-tissue-comparable biomechanical strength within 4 weeks, with enhanced neovascularization, elevated collagen I/III ratio, and well-organized extracellular matrix. RNA sequencing confirmed upregulated angiogenesis and ECM-related genes, as well as downregulated inflammatory markers. This multifunctional platform integrates mechanical robustness, controlled biodegradability, and proregenerative capacity, presenting a promising strategy for POP repair.

title: Diverse Impact of Ionic Liquid Additives on Lubricant Electrical Conductivity
abstract: Abstract The electrical conductivity (EC) of the lubricating oils and greases in electric vehicles should be neither too high nor too low. Primarily, these lubricants serve as electrical insulators with high dielectric strength to prevent current leakage or short circuits. On the other hand, lubricants with extremely low conductivity can lead to buildup of electrostatic charges at the tribological interfaces, potentially resulting in arcing and associated surface pitting. Ionic liquids (ILs) have recently been developed as candidate lubricant additives. ILs are ionic in nature and thus are intuitively expected to increase the lubricant EC. However, there is a lack of a quantitative measure of the exact impact and fundamental understanding of the correlation with IL chemistry. In this work, we measured the change in oil EC upon introducing several oil-miscible ILs as additives at various concentrations and temperatures and modeled the relationship using the Arrhenius equation. Most ILs substantially increased the oil EC as expected. For example, adding 1 wt % of aprotic phosphate ILs, such as [N8888][DEHP] and [P8888][DEHP], to PAO4 boosted the EC by two to three orders of magnitude. In contrast, adding 1 wt % of other types of ILs, such as [N888H][DEHP], [P66614][C7H15COO], [P66614][C17H35COO], and [P66614][BTMPP], increased the oil EC by one to two orders of magnitude. A protic IL has less effect on the oil EC than an aprotic IL likely due to its hydrogen-bonding interactions between the cations and anions leading to reduced charge carrier mobility. Furthermore, the protic IL [N888H][DEHP] was surprisingly found to decrease the oil EC when added into a fully formulated lubricant, possibly due to competitive interactions with certain additives in the package that hinder the mobility of charge carriers. Overall, these results provide fundamental insight into the impact of IL molecular structures on oil EC and offer guidance for future development of ILs for advanced lubrication.

title: Combustion of Boron Nanoparticles Encapsulated within Perchlorate Matrices: A Mechanistic Study
abstract: Abstract Boron is an attractive high-energy fuel, but its practical combustion efficiency is limited by a viscous oxide layer that impedes oxygen transport and promotes agglomeration. Here, we address these limitations by assembling boron nanoparticles into spray-dried mesoparticles in which boron is encapsulated within an ammonium perchlorate (AP) matrix and a nitrocellulose binder. This architecture enhances fuel oxidizer proximity, accelerates AP decomposition onset by ∼60 °C, and enhances reaction kinetics as evidenced by a ∼50% pressurization rate and a ∼58% shorter burn time relative to the physically mixed formulation. In situ TEM, TGA/DSC, and T-jump time-of-flight mass spectrometry reveal that mesoparticles promote interfacial reactions producing both B2O3 and boron nitride (BN). BN formation is identified as a thermodynamic efficiency-loss pathway, releasing significantly less energy per mole of boron than oxidation to B2O3. Substituting AP with potassium perchlorate eliminates the nitrogen source, significantly reducing BN formation, and further improves combustion performance. These results demonstrate that mesoscale encapsulation combined with targeted oxidizer selection provides a practical strategy to enhance boron combustion efficiency.

title: Dimensionality and Nanoporosity Effects on the Electrochemical Reactivity of Ti-Oxo Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) incorporating redox-active metal–oxo clusters offer an emerging platform for diverse applications, including electrochemical energy storage, yet their electrochemical reactivity remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first systematic electrochemical investigation of Ti-MOFs in aqueous electrolytes, focusing on the microporous Ti tetracarboxylate MIP-177 family, which exists in two polymorphs featuring either discrete Ti12O15 oxoclusters (MIP-177-LT) or infinite one-dimensional Ti-oxo nanowires (MIP-177-HT). Using cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic cycling, we demonstrate that only MIP-177-HT exhibits measurable electronic conductivity, enabled by its extended 1D metal–oxo network, whereas MIP-177-LT remains electronically insulating. Deconvolution of Faradaic and non-Faradaic contributions across different aqueous electrolytes indicates that the internal nanoporosity of MIP-177-HT significantly enhances double-layer charge storage. In LiCl electrolytes, MIP-177-HT also undergoes reversible Li+ insertion with thermodynamic behavior comparable to anatase TiO2, but with markedly reduced voltage hysteresis. Galvanostatic cycling in this electrolyte delivers a capacity of 60 mAh g–1 with a Coulombic efficiency of 97% at 0.11 A g–1, demonstrating the almost absence of parasitic hydrogen evolution. Nonetheless, post-cycling X-ray diffraction analyses reveal pronounced structural degradation of MIP-177-HT, indicating insufficient stability for long-term aqueous operation. Overall, these findings establish the fundamental electrochemical behavior of Ti-oxo MOFs and underscore the need to enhance their structural robustness to fully exploit their potential in aqueous-based energy storage applications.

title: Bromide-Rich Phase Enhances the Photovoltaic Performance in Fabricating the Hybrid Wide-Bandgap Perovskite-Based Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Nowadays, high-performance tandem solar cells may be fabricated by connecting the organic–inorganic hybrid wide-bandgap (WBG) halide perovskite film-based solar cells (PSCs) with the silicon-based one. The major challenge for both academia and industry is the performance of the WBG-based solar cell. Here, to improve the efficiency and stability of WBG PSCs, ethylenediammonium halides are designed to passivate and exclude the defects in fabricating the WBG-based solar cells. Ethylenediammonium bromide forms a Br-rich phase, which not only passivates surface defects but also suppresses light-induced phase segregation, thereby improving the performance of WBG mixed-halide PSCs. The champion PSCs achieve an open-circuit voltage of 1.255 V, a fill factor of 84.12%, and a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 23.64%. Device stability is also markedly enhanced, with 99.6% of the initial PCE retained after 1728 h under ISOS-D-1I conditions and a T80 lifetime of 1020 h under ISOS-T-1I conditions. This work provides a new insight into optimization strategies for mixed-halide WBG perovskites.

title: Binary-Crosslinked Alginate/Zwitterionic Interpenetrating Polymer Network Coatings for Lubricious and Antifouling Urinary Catheters
abstract: Abstract Hydrophilic hydrogel coatings can mitigate catheter-associated infections and friction-induced mucosal trauma during urinary catheterization by providing hydration-driven lubrication and antifouling surfaces. Here, we report an alginate/sulfobetaine methacrylate-based zwitterionic interpenetrating polymer network (Alg-ZW IPN) that integrates a binary crosslinker system into the IPN architecture by pairing a short-chain crosslinker, N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide (MbAm), with a long-chain crosslinker, poly(ethylene glycol) dimethacrylate (PEGDMA). In the binary crosslinked IPN (Alg-ZW BIPN), MbAm establishes dense local junctions for structural integrity, while PEGDMA spans the interjunction domains to mechanically bridge the network, confine alginate chains, and stabilize Ca2+–alginate coordination. This architecture redistributes mechanical stress across length scales, thereby improving coating durability. The Alg-ZW BIPN coating exhibited ultralow friction, with a friction coefficient of 0.01–0.02, and maintained 49% lower friction than MbAm single crosslinker coatings. In catheter insertion tests using a standard vascular phantom, the coating reduced insertion force by up to 75% compared with uncoated catheters. The coating also inhibited Escherichia coli adhesion by 97.4% relative to uncoated substrates and showed excellent biocompatibility, with a hemolysis ratio of 0.17% and >95% endothelial cell viability after 24 h. Overall, the Alg-ZW BIPN design provides a general and scalable route to mechanically robust, lubricious, and antifouling hydrogel interfaces for indwelling medical devices.

title: Tuning Inter- and Intraparticle Crosslinking and Packing Density Governs the 3D Bioprintability and Biological Performance
abstract: Abstract Granular hydrogels are an emerging class of microporous biomaterials assembled from annealable microparticles that enhance cell survival, function, infiltration, and cell migration through their interconnected cell-scale void spaces. Here, we aimed to understand how balancing inter- and intraparticle interactions, alongside microparticle packing density, influences the printability and cellular responses of granular hydrogels. Mechanically fragmented microparticles, made of tyramine-modified alginate (TAlg) and gelatin (TGel), underwent primary enzymatic gelation and secondary photocrosslinking for construct stabilization. Balancing this two-scale chemical trade-off yielded a compressive modulus of 12.9–24.7 kPa, while rapid photoinitiator clearance (>90% within 1 h) ensured high cytocompatibility. Incorporating 10–40 vol % interstitial matrix tuned total porosity from ∼7 to 18%, with medium-packed inks (20 vol % matrix) achieving high fidelity for three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting without sacrificing void connectivity. The resulting interconnected network accelerated cell infiltration to a depth of 450 μm within 3 days (∼3-fold higher than bulk hydrogels) and enabled ex vivo tissue adhesion (7.1 kPa shear strength). 3D-bioprinted granular constructs supported dense interconnected 3D cellular network formation over 7 days. This scalable strategy to deconstruct di-tyramine-mediated bulk hydrogels provides a versatile toolbox for advanced biofabrication and complex tissue engineering.

title: Synergistic Molecular-Nano Engineering Enabling Ultralong-Cycling and High-Capacity Lithium Storage of Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) combine the high energy density of batteries with the high-power density of supercapacitors for potential advanced applications. As promising anode candidates for LICs, the practical application of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is hampered by the intrinsically low electronic conductivity. Here, a “molecular-nano” dual-scale synergistic strategy is proposed to enhance the charge transport and utilization of active sites. At the molecular scale, three highly crystalized COFs (2,6-DAAQ-COF, 2,6-DAA-COF, and 1,4-DAAQ-COF) via donor-acceptor (D–A) structural design are synthesized to enhance the intramolecular charge separation and electron transfer processes. At the nanoscale, a three-dimensional conductive network is constructed by in situ compositing with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) to yield core-shell structured COF@CNT, which also effectively exfoliates COF layers and exposes active sites. Benefiting from the synergistic enhancement between intramolecular charge transfer and the macroscopic conductive network, the optimized 2,6-DAAQ-COF@CNT50 exhibits exceptional lithium storage performance, retaining a high discharge capacity of 1983 mAh g–1 after 1000 cycles at 1 A g–1. Furthermore, the electrode also exhibits excellent electrochemical performance at low temperature (–20 °C), retaining 220 mAh g–1 after 2000 cycles at 0.5 A g–1. The assembled LICs demonstrate superior stability of up to 10,000 cycles. This study provides a new strategy and mechanistic insights for designing high-performance organic anode materials for LICs.

title: Chloroacetate Buffer-Modified SnO2 Electron Transport Layer for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Tin oxide (SnO2) is a popular material for the electron transport layer (ETL) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the defects at the SnO2/perovskite interface tend to induce non-radiative recombination and deprotonation of formamidinium (FA+), limiting the device performance. Herein, a chloroacetate (CA) buffer system consisting of chloroacetic acid and its potassium salt was employed as a unique multifunctional interface modifier to synergistically engineer the SnO2 ETL/perovskite interface. The chloroacetate anion anchors to Sn and Pb sites, while the chloroacetic acid stabilizes FA+ through the hydrogen bond. As a result, the acidic buffer system suppresses FA+ deprotonation, enhances perovskite film quality, and improves carrier transport. Consequently, the CA buffer-modified PSC devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.8%, considerably higher than 22.6% for the control devices. They also demonstrate prolonged dark-storage stability; particularly, the unencapsulated devices retain 99% of initial efficiency after 1500 h of ambient storage. This work shows that combining an organic acid and its conjugated base offers a facile yet effective strategy to simultaneously passivate the buried interface and stabilize perovskite components for efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Recent Progress in the Reutilization of Epoxy Resins: Strategies after End-of-Life
abstract: Abstract The production and demand for thermosetting epoxy resins have been increasing steadily, and the massive decommissioning of equipment has generated a substantial volume of solid waste that urgently requires proper disposal. The stable three-dimensional crosslinked networks of epoxy resins endow them with excellent service performance, yet simultaneously render them difficult to recycle after retirement. The accumulation of such waste not only leads to resource wastage but also exacerbates environmental pollution. Meanwhile, growing concerns over fossil resource depletion have reinforced the strategic importance of recognizing end-of-life materials as a renewable resource. This review focuses on current strategies for the reutilization of waste epoxy resins. Based on the end-application of the regenerated products, the strategies fall into three categories: (i) polymeric derivatives, including both remanufactured epoxy materials and non-epoxy polymers; (ii) functional material applications; and (iii) small-molecule products. For each pathway, the chemical rationale and major challenges are discussed. This review aims to provide a framework for understanding current utilization approaches for waste epoxy resin, facilitating the transition of thermosetting waste from a disposal burden to a valuable resource base.

title: Voltage-Driven Transition from Steady-State Fluctuations to Phase-Transition Noise in Nanoscale VO2 Devices
abstract: Abstract We investigate the electrically driven metal-to-insulator transition (MIT) in a nanoscale vanadium dioxide (VO2) Mott memristor through noise spectroscopy and two-dimensional resistor network simulations. Our experiments focus on both the insulating phase as the applied voltage approaches the threshold voltage (set transition) and the metallic phase as the voltage is reduced toward the reset voltage (reset transition). In both regimes, we observe an order-of-magnitude increase in relative current noise near the transition points. To analyze the origin of this noise enhancement, we use simulations that capture the stochastic dynamics of the phase transition. The simulations indicate that the increased noise stems from amplified phase fluctuations near the switching threshold, where competing metallic and insulating domains lead to the dynamic reconfiguration of conduction paths. In addition, we show that the precursor current fluctuations observed near the switching threshold have a relative magnitude comparable to the cycle-to-cycle threshold voltage variation, indicating that transition-related fluctuations may remain a limiting factor for the achievable threshold voltage variation in optimized devices. These findings provide a comprehensive picture of the noise performance of VO2 devices, capturing the heavily voltage-dependent noise characteristics all along the switching cycle.

title: Silk Fibroin Nanoparticles Coated with an Extracellular Vesicle–Liposome Hybrid Shell for Controlled Cargo Delivery
abstract: Abstract Silk fibroin nanoparticles (SFNPs) are promising nanocarriers for drug delivery owing to their biocompatibility, bioactivity, controllable biodegradability, and low toxicity. However, their translation is limited by formulation-dependent variations in morphology, colloidal stability, drug loading, and aggregation, all of which can affect release behavior and biological performance. Here, we investigated how fibroin solubilization conditions govern the self-assembly, internal structure, surface properties, and cargo delivery performance of SFNPs, using curcumin as a hydrophobic model compound. SFNPs were prepared by lithium bromide (LiBr) solubilization followed by desolvation and were characterized using complementary scattering, microscopy, and spectroscopy techniques. Fibroin solubilization temperature and curcumin loading modulated SFNP size, internal organization, and surface roughness. In particular, SFNPs formed 70–150 nm mass-fractal aggregates composed of smaller primary nanoparticles, and this morphology affected cargo loading and release by controlling accessible internal surface area and solvent contact. To further stabilize the system and engineer the external interface, SFNPs were incorporated into a liposome/extracellular vesicle (EV) hybrid shell by sonication, generating a carrier-in-carrier system containing EV-derived membrane-associated components. The hybrid lipid–EV/SFNP platform reduced aggregation in aqueous media and provided a tunable external shell for controlled release of hydrophobic cargo. Overall, this work establishes a structure-based proof of concept connecting upstream solubilization parameters to downstream nanoparticle architecture, supporting the rational design of hybrid silk-based nanocarriers for cargo delivery.

title: A Robust Bifunctional Envelope for Synergistic Superhydrophobic Anti-Icing and Electrothermal Deicing
abstract: Abstract Integrating passive superhydrophobic anti-icing with active electrothermal deicing offers a promising approach to ice protection. However, conventional layered designs often suffer from weak interfacial adhesion and limited heat transfer between the superhydrophobic layer and the underlying heater. Here, we develop a robust superhydrophobic anti-icing and electrothermal deicing bifunctional envelope by incorporating nanoporous polydivinylbenzene into a nickel-foam framework. The resulting monolithic composite combines mechanical durability, whole-body superhydrophobicity and electrothermal heating. Its capabilities are evidenced by retained superhydrophobicity after 3000 friction cycles, prolonged icing time, a low ice adhesion strength of 3.3 kPa, and efficient electrothermal deicing. Direct laser writing tailors the conductive network, reducing deicing energy consumption by 76.8% relative to the unpatterned composite and enabling thick ice to melt within 24 s at a low power density of 0.43 W/cm2. The flexibility and patternability of the envelope allow conformal integration onto curved surfaces, providing a route to durable surfaces that combine passive anti-icing with active deicing.

title: Three-Dimensional Folded Electrode Smart Finger Sleeve Based on a Silica Reinforced Ionic Hydrogel Composite for Multidirectional Tactile Sensing
abstract: Abstract Human fingers can perceive multidirectional tactile information through spatially distributed mechanoreceptors, thereby enabling delicate manipulation and interactive behaviors. However, most existing wearable tactile sensors primarily focus on unidirectional normal force detection, making it difficult to effectively recognize direction-related tactile inputs. Here, we report a three-dimensional finger sleeve that spatially encodes multidirectional mechanical stimuli into distinguishable multichannel piezoresistive signals by integrating spatially distributed folded electrodes and an ionic hydrogel sensing layer within a three-dimensional TPU supporting structure. The localized thin-walled groove design enhanced deformation concentration and force transmission, while the incorporation of 1 wt % SiO2 improved the hydrogel sensitivity by approximately 77%. The SiO2 nanoparticles were proposed to serve as dispersed rigid nodes, amplifying local strain gradients and deformation-induced changes in ion migration pathways. The device exhibited stable piezoresistive responses under normal forces of 0–20 N, enabled directional discrimination under shear forces of 0–5 N, and further detected an out-of-plane torque of 3 × 10–4 N·m together with its directional information. The distinguishable multichannel tactile patterns further enabled accurate gesture recognition and a two-dimensional direction-digit authentication strategy, in which directional information was introduced as an additional input dimension to enhance password complexity. This work provides a versatile strategy for wearable multidirectional tactile perception and offers possibilities for secure human–machine interaction, wearable control, and intelligent robotic sensing.

title: Coupled Regulation of Oxygen-Vacancy-Modified Near-Surface Structure and Interfacial Stability for High-Performance Li-Rich Mn-Based Cathodes
abstract: Abstract Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are prospective next-generation cathodes, delivering high specific capacities via coupled cationic and anionic redox. However, sluggish reaction kinetics, irreversible oxygen loss, and progressive interfacial structural degradation limit the practical application of LRMOs. Herein, a coupled strategy for regulating the near-surface structure and interfacial stability is developed using ammonium titanyl oxalate (ATO) as a multifunctional precursor. During thermal treatment, an approximately 10 nm Li2TiO3 coating layer forms to stabilize the cathode interface. Meanwhile, reducing gases released from precursor decomposition induce oxygen vacancy formation, whereas Ti incorporation suppresses excessive transition-metal (TM) reduction in the near-surface region, thereby alleviating the associated increase in Mn3+ content and Jahn–Teller distortion. Moreover, the coupled Ti and oxygen vacancy configuration enhances anionic redox reversibility, stabilizes the near-surface oxygen framework, and lowers the Li+ migration barrier, thereby improving Li+ transport and structural stability. The optimized ATO-2% cathode achieves an average initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of 90.07% at 0.1 C and a capacity retention of 88.1% after 300 cycles at 1 C. This work establishes a coupled regulation strategy for the oxygen vacancy-modified near-surface structure and interfacial stability, providing a route for optimizing oxygen vacancy engineering in LRMO cathodes.

title: Orientation-Controlled In-Material Physical Reservoirs Based on Polymer-Wrapped Carbon Nanotube Nanofilms
abstract: Abstract Semiconducting polymer poly(m-phenylenevinylene-co-2,5-dioctoxy-p-phenylenevinylene) (PmPV)-wrapped single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT–PmPV) nanofilms were fabricated using the Langmuir–Blodgett (LB) method to investigate the effects of structural orientation on their electrical and reservoir computing properties. Polarized ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy and atomic force microscopy revealed that repeated compression–expansion cycles during LB deposition produced highly oriented SWCNT nanofilms. The oriented films exhibited an anisotropic electrical response, pronounced hysteretic current–voltage characteristics, and enhanced generation of higher-order harmonics, while water adsorption further enhanced the current and nonlinear electrical response. In waveform generation tasks, the advantage of the highly oriented films was most pronounced for the sawtooth and sin(2ω) targets, which involve more complex waveform features and frequency components. Additional delayed-input reconstruction and nonlinear autoregressive moving average (NARMA) 2 tasks revealed enhanced fading memory and nonlinear temporal processing under humidified conditions, with the highly oriented film exhibiting a larger memory capacity and lower NARMA2 error than the less-oriented film. These results indicate that structural orientation, together with humidity-dependent electrical dynamics, contributes to the nonlinear and temporal information-processing capabilities of SWCNT–PmPV nanofilms. These findings provide a practical strategy for modulating in-material reservoir computing performance through structural control of anisotropic material networks.

title: Bone Marrow-Targeted Nano-delivery Systems for Refractory Hematologic Malignancies: From Delivery Barriers to Clinical Translation
abstract: Abstract Hematologic malignancies (HMs) pose a serious threat to human health and are associated with a high metastatic rate and poor prognosis. The strong tumor heterogeneity, marked therapeutic resistance, poor targeting of conventional therapies, and toxic side effects make them a major challenge in the clinical treatment of HMs. As the principal site of hematopoiesis and immune cell production, the bone marrow (BM) is a critical site in the treatment of HMs. However, low blood perfusion and the complexity of the microenvironment severely hinder drug accumulation within the BM, which is also the core bottleneck in the treatment of HMs. Owing to their unique physicochemical properties, nano-delivery systems enable efficient BM-targeted delivery, providing effective strategies to overcome this therapeutic bottleneck. This review discusses the structure of the BM and the mechanisms of delivery barriers, systematically analyzes the design advances of BM-targeted nano-delivery systems, highlights different delivery strategies, and addresses key issues in the clinical translation of nano-delivery systems, including biosafety, manufacturing, and regulation of in vivo delivery efficiency. It also outlines future directions, establishing a BM-targeted delivery framework to advance the treatment of HMs and providing a theoretical reference for the development and clinical application of BM-targeted nano-delivery systems, thereby facilitating breakthroughs in precision therapy for HMs.

title: Food-Grade Hyaluronidase-Driven Janus Zein Nanomotors for Targeted Curcumin Delivery in Colorectal Microenvironments
abstract: Abstract Curcumin, a bioactive polyphenol, exhibits high therapeutic potential, but its poor solubility and bioavailability restrict its application. Furthermore, conventional nanocarriers face cumbersome fabrication, poor biocompatibility, and insufficient tumor extracellular matrix penetration. Here, we constructed a hyaluronidase-driven, curcumin-loaded food-grade Janus zein nanomotor (HAase-CZ-JNs) via Pickering emulsion templating and genipin crosslinking. Its asymmetric "half-hydrophilic, half-hydrophobic" topology minimizes mass transfer resistance and stabilizes the enzyme's active conformation, boosting immobilized HAase catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) 4.01-fold over free enzyme. Driven by endogenous HA, HAase-CZ-JNs exhibit robust substrate-dependent self-propulsion (effective diffusion coefficient: 63.69 μm2/s), 8.2-fold higher than that of fully modified nanoparticles (HAase-CZ-NPs). In vitro, these nanomotors actively penetrate dense 3D spheroids, enhancing deep cytotoxicity against HT-29 cells (IC50 = 1.364 μg/mL) with a 12-h core-killing efficacy 7.9-fold greater than HAase-CZ-NPs. Utilizing biosafe natural materials, this system offers a promising nanokinetic strategy for targeted curcumin delivery in colorectal microenvironments.

title: High-Performance Ionic Thermoelectric Conversion toward Self-powered Human–Computer Interaction
abstract: Abstract Ion thermoelectric conversion has great potential for application in thermoelectric energy harvesting and self-powered devices due to its high ionic Seebeck coefficient. However, existing systems generally suffer from problems such as low thermoelectric conversion efficiency, insufficient mechanical properties, and difficulty in assembling functional devices. Here, we report a novel ionic thermoelectric hydrogel based on a sodium alginate–polyacrylamide dual network with zirconium oxychloride as the electrolyte. The hydrogel achieves a tensile strength of 44.77 kPa and an elongation at break of 327.64%. Simultaneously, a crosslinked structure with ion transport pathways is formed, providing continuous pathways for the differential dissociation and migration of Zr(IV)-containing species and free Cl– ions, thereby enhancing ion thermodiffusion. This yields an ionic Seebeck coefficient as high as –14 mV K–1. A single ionic thermoelectric hydrogel generates 56 mV at ΔT = 4 K, while four hydrogels connected in series produce an output voltage of approximately 0.2 V, demonstrating the feasibility of hydrogel array integration for practical applications. Through series integration, voltage boosting, and capacitive energy storage, a self-powered system for gesture recognition and drone control is successfully constructed. The integrated equipment drives a low-power microprocessor and gesture recognition module, enabling real-time interactive control for raise-to-fly. This work provides a strategy for high-performance, integrable, and environmentally stable ionic thermoelectric devices, advancing their practical applications in self-powered systems and human–machine interaction.

title: A Metal–Organic Framework-on-Metal–Organic Framework Chemical Nose for Intelligent Identification of Depression-Related Biomarkers via Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Depression is a complex mental disorder associated with dysregulation of multiple neurotransmitter-related biomarkers, including Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, and 5-HTP. Herein, we report a MOF-on-MOF fluorescent sensor array, RhB@ZIF-8-on-FL@UiO-67, for simultaneous discrimination and detection of these biomarkers. Spatial separation of dyes within the hierarchical architecture effectively suppresses fluorescence crosstalk and generates multiple independent luminescent channels, enhancing signal diversity and sensing performance. The resulting multidimensional fluorescence responses enable accurate identification of Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, 5-HTP, and their mixtures. Both LDA and HCA achieved a classification accuracy of 100% for the tested samples. Furthermore, machine learning models, including BP, RF, DT, SVM, and KNN, confirmed the robustness of the sensing platform. This work integrates MOF-on-MOF engineering with machine learning-assisted pattern recognition, offering a sensitive and reliable strategy for multiplex biomarker analysis and providing a promising approach for intelligent diagnosis of complex diseases.

title: Atom-Economic Intramolecular Rearrangement Enables High-Film-Retention Non-chemically Amplified Resists for Advanced Lithography
abstract: Abstract The transition to high-numerical-aperture (High-NA) extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) imposes stringent constraints on resist film thickness, posing a critical challenge in terms of maintaining film thickness consistency to ensure pattern fidelity during subsequent etching processes. Herein, we introduce a molecular design strategy that intrinsically addresses this issue by employing an atom-conservative photochemical reaction. A series of non-chemically amplified resists (n-CARs) based on ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde (o-NBA)-modified PMMA polymers (PoMA) were developed. Distinct from conventional resists that suffer from decomposition-induced thickness loss, PoMA leverages a unique intramolecular rearrangement mechanism. Upon exposure, the o-NBA moieties undergo an intramolecular photorearrangement into ortho-nitrosobenzoic acid (o-NSBA), inducing a polarity switch for negative-tone development (NTD) without mass loss. Consequently, the PoMA resists exhibited near-quantitative film retention after exposure and development. By tuning the molecular weight of PoMA, we optimized the delicate balance between sensitivity and resolution, achieving 18 nm half-pitch (HP) resolution with a line edge roughness (LER) of 1.7 nm in electron beam lithography (EBL) and 30 nm HP with 2.5 nm LER in EUVL. Furthermore, etch resistance and pattern transfer capability into silicon at feature sizes down to 25 nm HP were also demonstrated. These findings highlight the atom-economic rearrangement strategy as a promising paradigm for designing photoresists for advanced lithography, effectively addressing the critical issue of film thickness loss in ultrathin resist layers.

title: Structural Engineering of Bio-Alkaloid Ionic Liquid-Mesoporous Silica Nanohybrids for Optimized Transdermal Atopic Dermatitis Therapy
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) are highly promising drug carriers owing to their exceptionally large surface area and tailorable pore structures for high drug-loading capacity, but their transdermal delivery is severely restricted by the skin barrier. Integrating natural ionic liquids (ILs) can modulate skin permeability; however, the mechanistic impact of distinct IL molecular structures on the interfacial properties of MSN-IL nanohybrids remains poorly understood. In this study, we engineered a structure-specific transdermal delivery platform by assembling citric acid-functionalized MSNs with various natural bio-alkaloid cations (choline, L-carnitine, and matrine). Density functional theory (DFT) and macroscopic physicochemical evaluations revealed that the matrine-based system (CA-M 1:2) forms a highly stable, tight ion-pairing conformation. This specific configuration endows the formulated MSN-IL nanohybrid with a robust dynamic viscosity, providing effective steric occlusion to prevent premature drug leakage within the MSN pores. Despite this internal cohesion, in vitro assays and transmission electron microscopy confirmed that the CA-M 1:2 hybrid dynamically facilitated the highest transdermal flux, transporting intact MSNs across the skin barrier via an IL-associated enhancement of skin permeation. In the atopic dermatitis mouse model, topical treatment with the optimized DEX/MSN-IL system significantly accelerated lesion resolution, restored epidermal architecture, and suppressed inflammatory cascades by downregulating IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IgE levels. This work establishes a physical chemistry-driven molecular-to-macro framework for the rational design of structure-specific nanohybrids, advancing high-performance topical therapeutics for inflammatory skin diseases.

title: Impedance Matching Optimization and Meta-Structure Design of 3D-Printed Ion-Enhanced Hydrogels for Broadband and Strong Absorption of the Electromagnetic Wave
abstract: Abstract Flexible hydrogels endowed with highly tunable 3D network architectures and multiple dielectric loss mechanisms hold tremendous application potential in electromagnetic wave (EMW) protection for wearable devices and conformally curved surfaces. Compared with conventional mold-casting fabrication, photocuring-based 3D printing enables the precise construction of complex macroscopic hydrogel geometries, including periodic arrays, lattice configurations, and gradient structures, thereby facilitating the synergistic optimization of structural design and microwave absorption performance. Herein, a series of ion-enhanced hydrogels were fabricated via digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing. The incorporation of metal cations simultaneously enhanced the dielectric response and optimized impedance matching, while markedly improving the elastic modulus by 215.2% and the volumetric toughness by 305.5%. Among these, the glycerol-modified hydrogel achieved an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 8.17 GHz at a thickness of only 2.39 mm, and at the same thickness, the pure hydrogel failed to achieve effective absorption across the entire frequency range. Furthermore, after meta-structure design, the CST simulation results show that the ion-enhanced hydrogel delivered dual intense absorption peaks of –27.68 and –26.37 dB, with the EAB broadened to 14.0 GHz, fully covering both X and Ku-bands. Overall, this work provides a novel design strategy for developing high-performance flexible microwave absorbers that simultaneously possess printability and broadband absorption capability.

title: Self-Gelling Powdered Hydrogel Dressing Based on Dynamic Ion-Cross-Linked Natural Polypeptides for Shape-Adaptive Hemostasis and Accelerated Wound Healing
abstract: Abstract Effective hemorrhage control and wound closure are frequently compromised by the poor shape adaptability of preformed bulk hydrogel dressings, which fail to maintain intimate contact with irregular, bleeding tissue. To address this, we developed a freeze-dried polyelectrolyte complex powder (GLF-K) composed of dopamine-grafted γ-poly-l-glutamic acid, ε-poly-l-lysine, keratin, and iron ions. The network architecture relies on primary electrostatic cross-linking, synergistically reinforced by dopamine-Fe3+ coordination, which enables the GLF-K powder to rapidly rehydrate and transition into a cohesive hydrogel upon exposure to moisture. Compared to commercial chitosan hemostats, the GLF-K powder exhibited comparable or enhanced hemostatic efficacy in both in vitro and in vivo hemorrhage models, alongside excellent biocompatibility. More importantly, in a full-thickness skin defect model, GLF-K treatment accelerated the early-stage healing rate to 55.8% by day 3, significantly outperforming the control group. These findings suggest that GLF-K powder represents a promising integrated platform for managing acute hemorrhage and promoting expedited wound healing in irregular tissue defects.

title: Bio-Inspired Photothermal-Responsive P(NIPAM -co- NaAMPS)@SWCNT-COOH Hydrogel with Donnan-Driven Salt Rejection for High-Rate Solar Water Purification
abstract: Abstract The global water shortage and pollution crisis motivates the development of high-efficiency, durable water remediation technologies. Solar-driven interfacial evaporation attracts broad interest for its high efficiency and environmental friendliness; nevertheless, vaporization-related latent-heat loss and salt accumulation severely restrict practical water-purification performance. Inspired by biological mechanisms, we report a thermoresponsive hydrogel evaporator based on poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-sodium 2-acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonate) (P(NIPAM-co-NaAMPS)) composite network. Sulfonate groups (–SO3−) from NaAMPS impart high hydrophilicity to accelerate water uptake, while local Donnan equilibrium within the network suppresses salt ingress and accumulation. Under 1 sun irradiation (1 kW·m−2), PNIPAM-derived thermoresponsiveness triggers hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic chain collapse above the lower critical solution temperature (LCST). Upon photothermal contraction, the hydrogel achieves a stable-release water-purification rate of 9.87 ± 0.19 kg·m−2·h−1 (photothermal efficiency of 96.6%) during the 0.7 h plateau, alongside a cycle-averaged productivity of 0.87 ± 0.07 kg·m−2·h−1 over the full 9.0 h absorption-release cycle. Different from reported Donnan-type salt-rejection hydrogels, thermoresponsive draw agents, and polyelectrolyte evaporators, our innovation lies in coupling photothermally activated liquid-water extrusion with Donnan-mediated salt rejection, instead of simple material blending. The hydrogel maintains good stability across 30 cycles in 3.5 wt % saline water, showing promise for partial-salt-rejection pretreatment of brackish and diluted seawater. This work provides a strategy for cyclically stable solar water purification combining salt rejection and contaminant removal.

title: Understanding the Role of Solid Polymer Electrolyte Network Structure and Modulus in In Situ Anode Formation of “Anode-Free” Sodium Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract “Anode-free” solid-state battery concepts based on sodium metal have attracted greater research interest recently due to their potential economic advantages, namely lower material costs and simplified, less expensive processing. However, these cell concepts suffer from poor cycling reversibility and cycle life, and little is understood about the fundamentals that govern sodium metal growth during in situ anode formation in solid-state batteries (SSBs). In this work, we use two model cross-linked network solid polymer electrolyte systems with varying cross-link density and modulus to investigate how such properties influence sodium metal growth and cycling stability. Using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, we show that solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) modulus strongly influences the early-stage morphology and charge-transfer kinetics of in situ formed sodium metal anodes. The higher-modulus SPE promotes faster in-plane growth of sodium metal, particularly during the early stages of in situ anode formation. Consequently, the higher-modulus SPE displays 3.0× and 1.9× lower interfacial resistances than the lower-modulus SPE at plating capacities of 0.05 and 0.1 mAh cm–2, respectively. Despite lower interfacial resistance early in anode formation, the higher-modulus SPE displays shorter cycle life in Na|SPE|Cu “anode-free” half cells at 2.3 ± 1.1 mAh cm–2 compared to 6.6 ± 2.9 for the lower-modulus SPE. This work demonstrates that tuning SPE network structure through cross-link density can increase modulus and accelerate electroactive Na-SPE interface formation, but improved interfacial kinetics do not necessarily translate to greater long-term cycling stability. In situ indentation experiments in SEM showed that increasing cross-link density also yields a more brittle network that is more susceptible to crack propagation, which likely facilitates dendrite penetration and reduces cycle life.

title: Conductive MOF Heterostructures with Enhanced Interfacial Charge Transfer and Improved Humidity Tolerance for Superior Room-Temperature H2S Detection
abstract: Abstract Conductive metal–organic frameworks (C-MOFs) have emerged as promising candidates for room-temperature chemical sensing due to their intrinsic conductivity and tunable structures. However, their practical application is still hindered by limited sensitivity and poor humidity tolerance. In this work, CuO nanoparticles were introduced onto Co-HHTP nanorods to construct interfacial heterojunctions, followed by hydrophobic ZIF-8 modification to regulate gas–surface interactions. The optimized Cu10Co-HHTP sensor exhibited a high response of 15.8 toward 50 ppm H2S, excellent selectivity, and a low detection limit of 24 ppb at room temperature. Although ZIF-8 modification slightly reduced the H2S response, it substantially enhanced the humidity tolerance, decreasing the response loss at 85% RH from 59.1% to 18.4% relative to that at 33% RH. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory calculations revealed that the CuO/Co-HHTP heterointerface promotes charge redistribution and enhances H2S adsorption, while the hydrophobic ZIF-8 layer weakens the interaction between H2O and the outer surface, thereby suppressing competitive water adsorption and alleviating humidity-induced interference. These findings demonstrate that combining heterojunction engineering with hydrophobic surface regulation provides an effective strategy for the development of high-performance C-MOF-based gas sensors for reliable room-temperature operation with improved sensitivity and environmental stability.

title: A Scalable Presodiation Strategy Enabling Dry‐Air‐Processable Hard Carbon Anodes for High Energy Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Hard carbon (HC) anodes hold promise for sodium‐ion batteries but are plagued by low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) stemming from irreversible sodium sequestration. Chemical presodiation offers a direct route to compensate this deficit, yet its translation to high‐loading electrodes is crippled by sluggish mass transport and air sensitivity of the sodiated product, a barrier to scalable manufacturing. Here, we break this impasse by synchronizing acoustic field enhanced transport with in situ interfacial engineering. Ultrasound‐driven microconvection and cavitation overcome diffusion limitations within thick electrodes, delivering ∼100% ICE within one minute, approximately twice as fast as conventional immersion. A five second quenching in sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate constructs a B/F‐rich hybrid interphase that not only passivates the highly reactive sodiated surface against dry‐air degradation, retaining >79% ICE after 6 h exposure, but also selfregulates subsequent solid‐electrolyte interphase evolution, suppressing impedance growth and stabilizing charge transfer kinetics. Practical pouch cells deliver 76% capacity retention over 700 cycles at 0.5 C/1 C and exhibit superior wide‐temperature adaptability from −40°C to 55°C. By resolving the coupled bottlenecks of kinetic inhomogeneity and environmental instability, this work establishes a scalable, dry‐air‐compatible presodiation paradigm that bridges the gap between laboratory innovation and industrial battery manufacturing.

title: Frontispiece: Isolated Ir–Se Sites in Nickel Selenide for Glyoxal‐Mediated Ethylene Glycol Oxidation to Formate and PET Upcycling
An Oxidative Twist to the Interrupted Pummerer Reaction: Unlocking Inaccessible Aryl Sulfonium Salts
abstract: ABSTRACT The interrupted Pummerer reaction is a time‐honored and enduringly versatile tool in organic synthesis, and has recently found widespread application in the preparation of aryl sulfonium salts. However, the classical interrupted Pummerer protocol suffers from long‐standing intrinsic limitations: (a) The key reactants, sulfoxides, are rarely commercially available; (b) the use of harsh electrophilic activator often leads to limited functional‐group tolerance. To address these issues, we have herein developed a Selectfluor‐mediated oxidative interrupted Pummerer variant, which is applicable to synthetic C─H functionalization, allowing approaches to a range of aryl sulfonium salts, including thianthrenium, dibenzothiophenium, and phenoxathiinium frameworks. The present strategy circumvents the use of electrophilic activator and directly utilizes sulfides as starting materials, thereby enabling the scope to be expanded to unprotected amine‐containing arenes.

title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Cyclobutane motifs are widely present in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition provides a facile route for synthesizing four‐membered rings. However, controlling the regio‐ and stereo‐selectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. In topo‐photochemical reaction, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules can place the atoms at specific positions in the products. In this work, irradiation‐wavelength‐controlled, stepwise photo‐induced topo‐[2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives was achieved in crystals. Under blue light, one kind of monocyclobutane was produced via the cycloaddition of the vinyl groups; for ( E )‐1‐(5‐bromo‐1 H ‐indol‐1‐yl)‐3‐(3,5‐difluorophenyl)prop‐2‐en‐1‐one ( PEOBr 5 F 35 ), this process proceeded via a single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformation. Upon subsequent irradiation with 365 nm light, the monocyclobutane product underwent a second‐step [2+2] cycloaddition between C = C bonds on five‐membered heterocyclic ring in indole, converting into a bicyclobutane product. Such catalyst‐free dearomatization of indole via [2+2] cycloaddition provide a facile and green strategy for constructing cyclobutane‐fused heterocyclic architectures. Driven by [2+2] cycloaddition, the molecular crystals exhibited obvious macroscopic mechanical motion.

title: Topological Regioisomerism Enables Triplet–Triplet Energy‐Transfer for Reversible Dual Delayed Fluorescence–Phosphorescence Multicolor Afterglow
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving concurrent thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) afterglow in purely organic systems remains elusive owing to limited control over triplet dynamics, competing decay pathways and unclear operational mechanisms. Reversible TADF/RTP modulation within a single host‐guest system is challenging, hindering advances in color‐ and lifetime‐tunable afterglow materials. To achieve this, we utilized regioisomerism as a structural topology control parameter in a host‐guest platform to modulate triplet‐triplet energy transfer (TTET), enabling the transition from exciplex TADF to dual TADF‐RTP afterglow. The optimized system exhibits TADF‐associated delayed emission with an intensity‐weighted apparent lifetime of 617 ms, along with persistent RTP and ∼6.5‐9.5 s afterglow. Temperature‐dependent modulation of I TADF / I RTP ratio enables reversible cryogenic afterglow color evolution from yellow to orange and red through thermally regulated exciton redistribution.

title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li + Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish Li + transport in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)‐based solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) arises from restricted polymer segmental motion and persistent Li + ‐FSI − association, while conventional fillers provide limited regulation of the local electronic and coordination environments. Herein, amino‐functionalized UiO66‐NH 2 is introduced into a PVDF/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) electrolyte to construct electronically active composite SPEs (U6NP). The electron‐donating ─NH 2 groups induce p‐π conjugation, redistribute the linker electron density, and strengthen ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT)‐related electronic coupling between the organic linkers and Zr‐O clusters. This electronic reconstruction, together with amino‐associated modulation of local O‐centered coordination environments, reshapes the electrostatic landscape, weakens Li + ‐FSI − interactions, and facilitates Li + migration. U6NP delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.41 × 10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.56, and an oxidative stability of 4.42 V. More importantly, Li||U6NP||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cells with a cathode loading of 21.5 mg cm −2 retain 98.51% after 120 cycles at 0.05 C. The Li||U6NP||NCM811 pouch cell delivers 136.6 mAh g −1 initially and 120.9 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles. This work establishes ─NH 2 ‐induced p‐π conjugation‐enhanced LMCT as an effective strategy for electronically active MOF‐reinforced PVDF electrolytes toward high‐loading solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: In Situ Product Separation Suppresses Self‐Poisoning in 2‐Butanol Electrooxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with the electrooxidation of 2‐butanol (SBA) offers an energy‐efficient route to co‐production of hydrogen and methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), yet achieving selective MEK formation while maintaining sustained operation remains challenging because of sluggish anodic kinetics and product accumulation. Here, we integrate alloy‐catalyst engineering with reaction–rectification to address these coupled catalytic and process‐level limitations. A self‐supported PdAu/NF anode exploits Pd–Au ligand interactions to regulate the adsorption of SBA, surface hydroxyl species and MEK, thereby suppressing C─C bond cleavage and facilitating product desorption. The optimized PdAu/NF catalyst delivers 300 mA cm − 2 at 0.74 V versus RHE. Despite weakened MEK adsorption, accumulated MEK and MEK‐derived intermediates inhibit SBA oxidation on PdAu and hydrogen evolution on Pt. At the process level, membrane‐free PdAu/NF||Pt/NF electrode arrays are integrated with reaction–rectification, enabling continuous MEK removal, recovery and SBA recycling. This in situ product separation mitigates product accumulation and its inhibitory effects, enabling continuous electrolysis at 14 A with a cell voltage of approximately 1.3 V over 10 h. The integrated system produces MEK with 99% purity while simultaneously generating hydrogen, highlighting the potential of coupling molecular‐level catalyst regulation with process‐level product management for MEK and hydrogen co‐production.

title: Iron‐Catalyzed Regioselective Amidation of Pyridines via Zincke Imine Intermediates
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving precise site‐selective functionalization of pyridines is highly desirable in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we present an operationally simple iron‐catalyzed protocol for accessing C3‐amidated pyridines. The reaction harnesses an in situ‐generated Fe–acylnitrenoid that interacts with Zincke imines, which serve as temporarily dearomatized forms of pyridines. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope across C2‐, C3‐, C4‐, or disubstituted pyridine substrates. This approach was also successfully implemented in a telescoped one‐pot procedure by directly employing pyridines. Mechanistic and computational studies revealed that a high‐spin Fe(III)–imidyl radical would be the key amidating species.

title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS 1 /CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO 2 ‐to‐*NO 2 H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH 2 O‐to‐*NH 2 OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS 1 /CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO 3 − battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

title: Coking–Crosslinking Competition Shapes Alveolar Hard Carbon Formation From Heterogeneous Precursors for Wide‐Temperature Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Competing with lithium‐ion technology on cost and resource abundance requires sodium‐ion batteries to use hard‐carbon anodes produced from abundant, inexpensive feedstocks without sacrificing structural control. Yet the natural and residual feedstocks that meet these requirements are typically chemically heterogeneous. Competing transformations among their constituent fractions before high‐temperature treatment make the carbonization pathway and carbon architecture difficult to predict and direct. Here, controlled fraction removal and reintroduction reveal a new mechanism whereby coking‐crosslinking competition selects the carbonization pathway. Surface coking blocks oxygen access and suppresses bulk crosslinking, whereas low‐temperature pre‐purification removes coking‐prone fractions, preserving an oxygen‐accessible skeleton that forms alveolar hard carbon (AHC). Operando x‐ray diffraction (XRD)/Raman and synchrotron x‐ray absorption near‐edge structure (XANES) establish that the low‐potential plateau arises from reversible formation of highly reduced sodium species within confined pores. AHC‐120@15‐1400 delivers 388.3 mAh g −1 with 91.3% initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), retains 94.3% capacity after 10 500 cycles at 4 A g −1 , and operates from −25°C to 45°C. A 1.2 Ah pouch cell retains 82.5% capacity after 1,000 cycles, while the route lowers cradle‐to‐gate material‐resource impact by 35.6% relative to commercial hard‐carbon production. Controlling coking‐crosslinking competition establishes a pathway‐selective design principle for converting heterogeneous carbon resources into durable, wide‐temperature sodium‐storage carbons.

title: Reconfiguring Interfacial Electrochemical Potential for Boosting Sodium‐Ion Transport in Composite Solid Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish ion transport kinetics between the ceramic and polymer phases remain a key challenge in composite solid electrolytes (CSEs), primarily due to a severe interfacial barrier arising from their intrinsic physicochemical incompatibility. Herein, molecular design‐enabled electronic structure engineering is proposed to reconfigure the interfacial electrochemical environment at the Na 3 Zr 2 Si 2 PO 12 –poly(ethylene oxide) interface, based on a dual‐axis screening guided by the electron‐donating capability and molecular electronic asymmetry. By grafting different functional trimethoxysilanes from a targeted library onto the ceramic surface, the effect of the interfacial electrochemical potential on Na‐ion transport is investigated, revealing a strong negative correlation with the ionic conductivity of CSEs. The CSE with the optimal grafting molecule (phenyltrimethoxysilane) reduces the potential mismatch by 87% and lowers the Na‐ion migration barrier, thereby boosting Na‐ion conductivity by two orders of magnitude. All‐solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries using this CSE show boosted electrochemical performance with a high capacity of 91.8 mAh g −1 delivered at 5 C and retain ∼99% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes a screening framework for reducing interfacial potential mismatch and addressing the long‐standing ion‐transport bottleneck across ceramic–polymer interfaces in CSEs.

title: Synthesis of Enones and Enals From Alkenes via Alkenyl Thianthrenium Salts
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we show the stereoselective conversion of alkenes into enones and enals. Alkenyl thianthrenium salts are used as a readily accessible pool of stereodefined alkenyl electrophiles that can be engaged in two types of carbonylative Pd‐catalyzed three‐component coupling reactions. Using alkyl zinc species generated in situ from alkyl iodides, enones can be accessed via a carbonylative Negishi coupling. In the presence of triethylsilane, enals can be generated via reductive carbonylation.

title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO 2 Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling plastic waste into high‐value chemicals is an attractive pathway for the sustainable development of human society. Here, we demonstrate the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen (H 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) gases on an iron (Fe) species‐dispersed silica (SiO 2 ) catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. During the mechanocatalytic process, Fe species from the milling balls were anchored to the surface of pristine SiO 2 nanoparticles, forming the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst. Simultaneously, the Fe and Si sites in the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst synergistically facilitate the C─H bond activation and C─C bond cleavage pathways, enabling a favorable dehydrogenation‒cracking‒hydrogenation process to produce commercially valuable H 2 and CH 4 . Notably, this catalytic system also exhibits exceptional versatility in processing mixed plastic wastes without requiring prior sorting, while maintaining robust cycling stability. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.

title: Photocatalytic 1,2‐Boron Migrative Alkene Homologation to Access 1,3‐Difunctionalized Alkenes
abstract: ABSTRACT In contrast to well‐established methods for vicinal di‐functionalization of alkenes, remote di‐functionalization is much more challenging and has achieved limited success. Herein, we disclose a visible light photocatalytic boron‐directed alkene homologation with alkyl halides activated by a traceless tert ‐butylsulfonyl (Bus) leaving group. The reaction produces a myriad of 1,3‐difunctionalized alkenes under mild conditions with excellent functional group tolerance. β‐Elimination of the Bus group not only drives the contra‐thermodynamic 1,2‐boron migration, but also regenerates a C─C double bond, thus transforming the sulfone‐based alkyl halide into a vinylidene precursor, rather than a traditional alkyl source. The synthetic utility of this method is well demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis, downstream transformations, and the formal total synthesis of 24‐fluoro‐25‐hydroxyvitamin D 3 analogues. This work represents a very rare example of one‐carbon homologation of ubiquitous alkenes, thus establishing a new strategic paradigm for chemical synthesis.

title: Active Targeting Across Scales in Medical Robotics
abstract: ABSTRACT The diagnosis and treatment of human diseases often involve interventions that target different levels of the body's complex hierarchical organization, from macroscopic organs through microscopic cells, down to nanoscale molecular structures such as proteins. These interventions are hindered by challenges, such as biological barriers and dynamic microenvironments, which necessitate the development of more effective diagnosis, therapy, and microsurgery strategies. Multiscale medical robots are an emerging strategy to address these challenges: advances in micro and nano engineering have enabled the development of sophisticated medical robots with size adaptability and hierarchical navigation for active targeting. Such systems can connect organ‐level access and navigation with local action at tissue, cellular, or molecular scales. Here, we discuss advances in micro/nano engineering to design and fabricate multiscale medical robots, with focus on their active targeting capabilities in precision medicine. We provide an overview of the current state of these systems, from accurate diagnosis and targeted therapy to minimally invasive microsurgery across the various scales of the human body, and explore how anatomical, biological, and imaging constraints shape their design. Finally, we discuss the practical challenges of clinical translation, including system‐level assessment within the intended clinical workflow and the need for collaboration between engineers and clinicians.

title: Self‐Confinement‑Tailored Energy Routing for Superior Thermal‐Adaptive Ln‐MOFs Scintillator
abstract: ABSTRACT Noncontact radiation monitoring in extreme environments is essential across scientific and industrial fields, driving the development of x‑ray scintillators. Conventional scintillators continue to suffer from inadequate exciton utilization, poor thermal stability, or limited processability. In this study, we propose a self‐confinement strategy to tailor energy routing for constructing superior thermal‐adaptive scintillators. Two lanthanide‐organic frameworks, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln and Ln‐BDC‐F, are rationally designed and synthesized. Compared with the free state of pure ligand or its quasi‐confinement state in Ln‐BDC‐F, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln exhibits a strong molecular self‐confinement state arising from compact ligand packing, thereby enhancing exciton utilization, suppressing nonradiative energy dissipation, and optimizing the energy routing. These features endow ZJNU‐1006‐Ln with superior radio‐luminescent performance, including high light yield (max ∼ 62,000 photons MeV ‒1 ), low detection limit (92.7 nGy air s ‒1 ), and great thermal‐stability (3+ /Eu 3+ doping ratios enables precise localization of radiation‐exposed regions over a broad temperature range, particularly encompassing the Earth surface temperature window. This work highlights the self‐confinement effect as a promising strategy for designing advanced inorganic‐organic scintillators.

title: Universal Thermally‐Driven Non‐Noble Metal Redistribution Strategy Boosts High‐Temperature CO 2 Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable CO 2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires cathodes that integrate high activity with robust stability. Herein, a thermally‐driven non‐noble‐metal redistribution strategy is proposed to overcome the long‐standing limitation in dispersing non‐noble metals on perovskite surfaces, enabling perovskite–ceria composite cathodes with dynamically optimized active sites. Thermal treatment of Cu‐dispersed CeO 2 (Cu 0.05 Ce 0.95 O 2 , 5CC) coupled with Sr 2 Fe 1.5 Mo 0.5 O 6− δ (SFM) induces spontaneous Cu migration and redistribution, which can tailor the electronic structure, increase oxygen vacancies and extend triple‐phase boundaries, thereby enhancing CO 2 adsorption, activation and O 2− /e − transport. As a result, a single cell with 5CC–SFM cathode achieves exceptional current densities of 4.14 A cm −2 at 1.5 V under 850°C, respectively. Owing to strong interaction between the redistributed Cu species and perovskite oxide, the single cell maintains stable catalytic performance for 400 h under harsh high‐temperature CO 2 electrolysis conditions. Moreover, this work demonstrates the extended applicability of 5CC–SFM cathode in reversible solid oxide cells (RSOCs) and establishes the generality and methodological significance of thermally‐driven redistribution in achieving highly dispersed non‐noble‐metal species on oxide supports. These findings offer a general framework for the rational design of next‐generation CeO 2 –containing SOEC cathodes and advanced composite materials.

title: Electrochemically Passivated Liquid Metal Printing for Two‐Dimensional Wafer‐Scale, Atomically‐Thin Non‐Layered Oxides
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) non‐layered metal oxides (NMOs) are promising for advanced electronics and catalysis owing to their tunable electronic structures and highly active surfaces. However, synthesizing wafer‐scale, atomically thin NMOs is challenging due to their intrinsic isotropic bonding. Here, we present an electrochemical passivation liquid metal printing strategy that regulates oxidation kinetics via galvanic coupling, enabling the synthesis of wafer‐scale, atomically thin NMOs in air. Critically, using aluminum foil as both a sacrificial anode and a high‐surface‐energy substrate enables a self‐limiting oxidation reaction and produces wafer‐scale and uniform α ‐Bi 2 O 3 films with thickness down to 0.7 nm when coupled with ultralow contact‐angle wetting (13.8°). This method demonstrates broad applicability, facilitating the synthesis of ultrathin films of various NMOs, including Ga 2 O 3 (1 nm), In 2 O 3 (1.5 nm), and ZnO (1.7 nm). Notably, the quantum confinement and abundant active sites in the 2D α ‐Bi 2 O 3 film enhance its light‐harvesting and promote charge separation, resulting in a photocatalytic degradation efficiency of 98.6% with a rate constant of 0.0355 min −1 . This work provides a scalable strategy for synthesizing large‐area, ultrathin 2D NMOs, establishing a foundation for their applications in next‐generation photocatalysis.

title: An Interfacial Electron Pump Enhanced Photo‐Assisted CO 2 ‐to‐Bioplastic Microbial Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Most solar‐ and electrochemical CO 2 ‐utilization strategies still terminate in small‐molecule products, whereas direct access to recoverable carbon products such as bioplastics remains uncommon. Here, we develop a photo‐assisted bioelectrochemical platform by coupling a Shewanella oneidensis MR‐1 bioanode functionalized with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene quantum dots (MQDs) to a Cupriavidus necator biocathode modified with Ni‐doped carbon dots/poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (Ni‐CDs/PDDA). Cell‐associated MQDs form a conductive and photoactive biointerface, operationally described as an interfacial electron pump, that facilitates lactate‐dependent extracellular electron transfer (EET) under applied anodic bias and adds an illumination‐dependent current contribution. The MQDs‐enabled microbial fuel cell (MFC) delivers a peak power density of 0.82 ± 0.03 mW cm −2 under illumination. In the coupled CO 2 ‐fed system, anodic illumination raises polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) productivity to 131 mg L −1 d −1 at −0.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), approximately 47% above the matched dark value over a 12 h interval. The coupled platform reaches an apparent total‐energy‐to‐PHB efficiency of 3.42% when electrical, incident optical, and lactate‐derived chemical inputs are included. Multiscale analyses support an EET‐coupled interfacial relay involving cytochrome/heme‐associated components within the native EET network. This interface‐to‐synthesis strategy links photo‐assisted microbial electron harvesting to H 2 ‐mediated CO 2 ‐to‐PHB biosynthesis.

title: Armoring Bubbles With Wettability‐Adaptive and Self‐Fusible Particles for Efficient Gas Handling in Air
abstract: ABSTRACT Mixing small quantities of gas and storing them in air is promising for developing a miniature gas reactor. Bubble encapsulation by liquid film has been considered; however, stabilizing the liquid layer while keeping bubble coalescence ability is challenging. Here, a time‐programmed wettability‐adaptive and self ‐ fusible particle is designed to modulate the coalescence ability and stability of gas bubbles. The adaptive particles remain initially hydrophobic and adsorb on the liquid layer surface, forming a stable gas‐barrier layer. After a modulated time of 10 to 600 s, the particles switch to hydrophilic and absorb available liquid. This adaptive wettability enables capillary‐driven automated coalescence of the contacting bubbles in air. After the preprogrammed time, the diffused particles self‐fuse and provide a continuous gel layer, allowing robust shell formation with tolerance to gas escape for at least 30 days. Proof of concept shows gas/gas and gas/liquid micro‐reactions and their long‐term storage.

title: Transoceanic dispersals and island extinctions shape global snipe and woodcock diversity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Island colonization through transoceanic dispersal has been central in shaping insular biodiversity. Following colonization, island populations often undergo morphological shifts, which may promote ecological specialization and endemism, but often increase vulnerability to extinction. Most species in the shorebird family Scolopacidae are highly migratory, which likely underpins their propensity for long-distance dispersal. Notably, snipes ( Gallinago , Coenocorypha ) and woodcocks ( Scolopax ) have colonized diverse island regions, including the southwest Pacific, Malay Archipelago, Japan’s Amami, and the Caribbean, although none of the extant island endemics are migratory. The southwest Pacific and Caribbean taxa have suffered substantial recent extinction driven by human impacts. Here, we investigate avian evolutionary and biogeographic dynamics using a combination of morphology and phylogenomic data from target capture sequencing of key extant and extinct snipes and woodcocks. Our results reveal four independent dispersals from the Eastern to Western Hemisphere and a trans-Pacific dispersal from South America to the southwest Pacific islands. Comparative analyses of migratory behavior and morphology demonstrate pronounced changes in insular groups. For example, the small Austral snipes Coenocorypha are nested within Gallinago , sister to a group of much larger, continental South American snipes. Another case is the extinct Scolopax brachycarpa of Hispaniola which osteologically more resembles Scolopax , but genetically belongs to Gallinago . Gallinago brachycarpa and other extinct Caribbean snipes may represent a radiation that is lost forever. Our findings shed light on the processes that generate and erase avian diversity on islands, highlighting the dynamic interplay of dispersal, adaptation to novel conditions, and risk for extinction.

title: Calculated residue protonation states find functional, conserved E-channel proton-loading sites in Complex I from bacteria to mammals
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Bioenergetic proton pumps take protons from one side of a membrane, transiently binding them at a loading site within the protein matrix, and then release them to the other side against an electrochemical gradient. The E channel of Complex I, from bacteria to mammals, contains a conserved proton-loading region whose function is distributed among several interacting residues. Noting extensive sequence divergence across homologous Complex I structures, we asked how this function is conserved during evolution despite many amino acid changes. Multi-Conformation Continuum Electrostatics (MCCE) calculations were performed on the five E-channel subunits from 41 experimental structures from bacteria, cyanobacteria, insects, and mammals. A Monte Carlo sampling identified five to seven residues in each species that function as a proton-loading cluster. Structures with a closed E-channel have ~1 more proton in the cluster than those with open conformations. Proton binding represents ensemble averages across thousands of accessible microstates, each with an integer protonation state. A mean-field analysis showed that the proton affinity depends on both titrating residues and the surrounding protein electrostatic environment. Closely related proteins use nearly the same cluster of residues, whereas more divergent proteins substitute alternative proton-handling residues and modify electrostatically important fixed-charge groups to preserve cluster proton affinity.
