Thus, E-channel reversible proton-loading is preserved during sequence evolution by maintaining a local “electrostatic architecture,” often involving quite different evolutionary solutions. Thus, conservation of E-channel proton loading depends more strongly on the local electrostatic environment than on conservation of the individual residues that create it.

title: Sustainability of violence prevention after a randomized vacant lot greening intervention in Philadelphia: A 10-y follow-up
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Vacant lot greening has been shown to reduce violence and crime in the short-term [C. C. Branas et al. , Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 115 , 2946–2951 (2018)]. We assessed the 10-y impact of a 2013 clustered randomized controlled trial (RCT) of lot greening in Philadelphia on violence and crime. We measured lot greening by treatment assignment from the original 2013 cluster RCT and a longitudinal greening score to assess the sustainability of the treatment assignment from 2012 through 2023. Our outcomes were the annual reported total crime, violent crime, and firearm violent crime per square mile at each lot. We conducted intent-to-treat and contamination-adjusted intent-to-treat analyses to estimate the local average treatment effect on relative change in crime. Lots randomized to the full greening intervention remained greener over time compared to other lots. In intent-to-treat analyses, compared to lots that received no intervention, lots that received any intervention had a 9% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.96) and a 9% decrease in violent crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.97) per square mile per year. In contamination-adjusted analyses, compared to lots without sustained greening treatment, lots with sustained greening treatment had a 12% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.88, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.93) and an 11% decrease in density of violent crime (estimate = 0.89, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.95) per square mile per year. Even after a decade, vacant lot greening continues to prevent violence.

title: Localization mechanisms and function of postsynaptic K v 7 (KCNQ) channels and their reduction in KCNQ2 epileptic encephalopathy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: K v 7 channels composed of K v 7.2 and K v 7.3 subunits are enriched in neuronal axons where their hyperpolarizing potassium current suppresses repetitive and burst firing of action potentials. Mutations in their genes, KCNQ2 and KCNQ3 , cause neonatal epilepsy, underscoring their critical role in regulating neuronal excitability. In this study, we provide evidence that K v 7 channels are present at and near the postsynaptic density within dendritic spines of hippocampal neurons, where their current decreases calcium influx through NMDA receptors. This spine localization is promoted by heteromerization of K v 7.2 and K v 7.3 and their binding to AnkyrinG-190, which is the only AnkyrinG isoform present in dendritic spines. Lastly, spine localization of K v 7 channels and their ability to suppress NMDA receptor activity are markedly reduced by select variants of KCNQ2 that cause developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). These findings reveal a subcellular population of K v 7 channels that can dampen excitatory synaptic transmission and implicate their dysregulation in KCNQ2 -associated DEE.

title: Supercritical snapping and controlled launching via dual-latch gels
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Natural organisms have evolved integrated Latch-Mediated Spring Actuation systems (LaMSA) that consist of multiple latches and springs to enhance power output and adapt to diverse environmental conditions. Similar designs are appealing yet largely unexplored in engineered materials due to the complexity of integrating multiple components into a single material platform. Here, we report a dual-latch magneto-elastic shell device capable of selectively activating the latches to regulate snapping pathways and energy output based on specific actuation requirements. Differential deswelling across the thickness acts as the “motor” to load the elastic energy into the shell, which is then released via the snap-through instability once the loading reaches the critical threshold, constituting an intrinsic mechanical latch. Activation of the external magnetic latch delays snapping onset beyond the threshold of the intrinsic latch, leading to a power-amplified supercritical snap-through instability as well as a bifurcation instability. The combined function of both latches allows for flexible control over energy storage and release. Additionally, this integrated LaMSA system possesses an untethered anchoring mechanism, enabling the device to launch in arbitrary directions from the substrate, driven by the energy released during snapping. We envision that the design principles of dual-latch LaMSA systems will create opportunities for power-dense actuation in engineered materials and robotic devices.

title: Distinct nanoscale architectures of GABAergic inhibitory synapses predict diverse synaptic output
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: GABAergic synaptic inhibition is heterogenous across neuronal compartments, and plays a critical role in shaping local, cellular, and circuit excitability. In pyramidal neurons, inhibition is mediated by GABA A receptors (GABA A Rs) clustered at the inhibitory postsynaptic domain (iPSD). Synaptic strength depends not only on the number of GABA A Rs within the iPSD, but also on their precise nanoscale organization into discrete subsynaptic domains (SSDs). These SSDs often align with presynaptic GABA release sites to form nanocolumn structures that enhance synaptic efficacy. While nanocolumn organization is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of synaptic function, most studies of GABAergic synapses have focused on archetypal dendritic synapses, which control the plasticity and integration of excitatory inputs. Nonetheless, it remains unclear whether somatic synapses—which deliver robust inhibition to suppress neuronal output—share a similar nanoarchitecture. Here, we used complementary superresolution imaging approaches to directly compare inhibitory synapses in somatic and dendritic compartments. We found that somatic synapses are larger and exhibit greater structural diversity and nanoscale complexity than dendritic synapses. Dendritic synapses display relatively compact architectures with GABA A R SSDs frequently arranged into nanocolumns. In contrast, somatic synapses show a broader range of organizations, including aligned nanocolumns as well as more disorganized configurations with misaligned release sites or receptor SSDs, arrangements that likely exhibit input-specificity. Computational modeling revealed that these structural differences produce distinct functional outcomes, including increased inhibitory postsynaptic current amplitude and altered kinetics at somatic synapses. Together, our findings demonstrate that nanoscale organization differentially shapes inhibitory strength and signaling properties across neuronal compartments.

title: A decadal record of isotopic trends in martian atmospheric CO 2
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: This work represents the first long-term record of the isotopic composition of martian atmospheric CO 2 , acquired in situ by the Curiosity rover at Gale crater during Mars Years (MY) 31–38 (2012–2025). Measurement campaigns were designed to investigate possibilities of both diurnal and seasonal effects on CO 2 isotopes. Coordinated pairs of analyses during MY 31 and 38 revealed no significant differences in isotopic composition of CO 2 acquired during daytime and nighttime hours. However, here we show evidence for modest enrichment in heavy isotopes of oxygen in both northern and southern hemisphere spring-summer seasons. We assessed several processes, including precipitation/sublimation and adsorption/desorption of CO 2 , CO 2 photolysis, and oxygen isotope exchange as potential candidates for producing the observed fractionations. We find that while sublimation of CO 2 from polar caps, sublimation and desorption of CO 2 from lower latitude reservoirs, and CO 2 photolysis are insufficient alone, we can reproduce the measured enrichment through modeling of isotope exchange between CO 2 and 18 O-enriched H 2 O in thin liquid-like films at Mars’ surface or adsorbed within the regolith as Mars approaches and transits through perihelion. Lesser 18 O enrichment near aphelion may reflect less favorable conditions for oxygen isotope exchange at lower temperatures. Observed seasonal variations in CO 2 carbon isotopic composition are less pronounced, consistent with less carbon isotope exchange with surface reservoirs than seen for oxygen. Since our measurements were obtained at a single near-equatorial location on Mars, the relative contributions from global, regional, and local processes cannot be well-constrained by the available data.

title: Short-term flexibility and long-term stability in models of mind perception
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Understanding how people decide whether someone or something possesses a mind is central to a myriad of psychological, biological, and philosophical questions. It shapes fundamental processes at the individual (e.g., social interaction) and societal level (e.g., morality and ethics). While mind perception has been studied, it remains unclear which internal model people use when ascribing mental capacities to entities. Across four experiments (total N = 256), we explored what model people hold and its flexibility when ascribing agency and experience to entities encountered in everyday life and which differ in animacy and socialness (e.g., humans, pets, robots, voice assistants, tools). Using representational similarity analysis combined with lab-based experiments, a 6-wk long social interaction intervention, and longitudinal real-life exposure, we tested which model people use to ascribe agency and experience by comparing observed rating data to theoretical models. We demonstrated that an animacy distinction underlies the representational structure of experience attributions, while internal models for agency attributions are more idiosyncratic and flexible. When receiving explicit information on one entity, the internal model of agency changes. People update their model by incorporating this information, generalizing across the entire category of entities. We found no evidence that extended exposure to or ownership of inanimate technology, such as robots or voice assistants, or pets leads to restructuring of the models for experience or agency. Overall, these results provide insight into the internal models people hold when perceiving minds, the flexibility thereof, and offer ways to understand the roots and consequences of mind perception.

title: No evidence for a universal effect of writing on language use or the evolution of syntax
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The acquisition of writing has a lasting effect on how languages are processed in the brain, raising the possibility that it also affects how they are used and evolve over time. A popular hypothesis is that writing specifically leads to the increased use and evolution of complex hierarchical structures in language. While most case studies on individual languages have supported this, it remains unclear whether results scale to larger and more diverse sets of languages. Here we test this prediction in two ways: 1) synchronically, by modeling the effect of modality (written vs. nonwritten) on syntactic complexity, operationalized via hierarchy depth and clause count inside sentences, in corpora from 30 languages; and 2) diachronically, by modeling whether the development of writing affected the phylogenetic dynamics of hierarchy in clause combinations across 59 languages from three families. We found no effect of writing on the response variables in either analysis. Hierarchy depth and clause count inside sentences do not demonstrably differ between spoken and written use of language, and the introduction of writing had no discernible effect on the evolution of clause combinations in grammar. There is weak evidence for a decrease in variance in structural asymmetry after the introduction of writing in one family, possibly reflecting the impact of increased normativity. Our findings challenge popular beliefs about the relationship between writing and hierarchy and suggest that the evolution of syntax is more driven by culturally variable ideas about style in linguistic expression than by the evolution of writing.

title: China’s energy transition strategy favoring both coal and renewables: Economic risks and global implications
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: China’s energy strategy is navigating a complex policy landscape: While leading the world in renewable energy manufacturing and deployment, it is simultaneously pursuing a continued expansion of its coal-fired power fleet. This paper examines this dual trajectory by building an integrated analytical framework that combines domestic and international perspectives to analyze the social, economic, climate, and geopolitical impacts of China’s new coal-power plant investments. Combining historical trends, government planning, and projections from influential policy teams, we find that a tripling of renewable capacity by 2030, a pace China is on track to meet, is sufficient to satisfy all projected electricity demand scenarios when considered alongside the evolving generation mix and planned storage deployment. We further show that additional coal capacity is not required to ensure adequate electricity supply under these scenarios. The coal pathway could expose up to $223.6 billion of stranded assets from new projects and add an additional 327,000 workers in a declining industry. Furthermore, this trajectory may weaken the alignment between China’s domestic energy investment and its international clean energy leadership. We conclude that a clean-energy-led pathway that halts new coal construction is lower-cost, better for job growth, and more consistent with China’s role as a leader in the global clean energy transition.

title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC–HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. Time-resolved X-ray diffraction reveals that the transformation occurs on a timescale at least as fast as 1 to 2 ns, orders of magnitude faster than diffusion-controlled nucleation-growth processes, yet reversible upon pressure release, unlike classical FCC–HCP martensitic transformations. We hypothesize that the high Hugoniot temperature may provide the atomic mobility for reversibility, while the extreme deviatoric stress likely promotes rapid, displacive atomic motion. This fusion of athermal speed and thermal reversibility is difficult to classify within the classical dichotomy of phase transitions as either purely martensitic or purely thermally activated and may represent a class of stress-assisted, thermally reversible transformation accessible only under extreme pressure–temperature ( P-T ) conditions. First-principles Gibbs free-energy calculations show that the HCP phase is thermodynamically favored at low temperature over the pressure range 50 to 142 GPa, and that the computed FCC–HCP phase boundary places the laser-shock P-T state on the HCP-stable side, making it accessible to the transient LSC path. Our findings are consistent with chemical complexity acting as a powerful parameter for controlling phase transformation pathways under extreme P-T conditions, and reveal a distinct class of ultrafast, reversible transformations.

title: Impact pathways of a jurisdictional approach to slowing deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Governance of many of the world’s largest remaining tropical forests is shared across multiple levels of government, giving subnational jurisdictions a central role in forest management. This has motivated growing interest in jurisdictional approaches (JAs) to control deforestation. For JAs to deliver on national and international conservation priorities, those priorities must be translated into incentives that reduce deforestation at the jurisdictional level. Brazil’s Priority List (PL), launched in 2008, creates such incentives by identifying high-deforestation municipalities, subjecting them to intensified monitoring, enforcement, and credit restrictions, and establishing jurisdiction-wide criteria for exit that make municipalities accountable for deforestation within their borders. While prior studies show that the PL reduces deforestation, it remains unclear where these reductions occur and whether there is displacement across land tenure types or into neighboring municipalities. We assemble a municipality-level panel dataset for the Brazilian Legal Amazon (2000–2024) that combines PL designations with annual deforestation disaggregated by land tenure. Using a heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences estimator, we estimate effects within and across municipalities. We find large and statistically significant reductions concentrated on private lands, including agrarian reform settlements and other private properties. Within listed municipalities, we find no evidence of decreased or increased clearing in Protected Areas, Indigenous Territories, or undesignated public lands. Total deforestation also declines in neighboring municipalities, with reductions concentrated on private lands. These findings are consistent with the PL translating national conservation priorities into local land-use change while limiting displacement, offering insights for the design of jurisdictional approaches aimed at forest conservation.

title: A Neandertal-derived genetic variant reduces occipital brain volume in present-day humans
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Neandertal crania were less globular than those of modern humans, suggesting differences in the relative volumes of brain regions, including the frontal and occipital lobes. Here, we show that a common genetic variant influencing occipital brain volume in present-day people was inherited from Neandertals. The variant lies in predicted transcription-factor recognition motifs near DAAM1 , a gene that is known to be involved in brain development. Carriers of the Neandertal variant have altered DAAM1 expression and occipital lobe volumes that are about 0.85 cm³ smaller per gene copy. The variant is associated with reduced schizophrenia risk by almost 10% in homozygous carriers, while Neandertal ancestry as a whole does not show such a tendency. Any association with cognition or schooling is small or nonexistent, amounting to at most two weeks of education per allele against an average of about 15 y. Thus, this Neandertal-derived variant is linked to altered brain anatomy in present-day humans and lower schizophrenia risk while having little or no association with general cognitive ability.

title: Peak water: Trends in decoupling regional and global water use
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Water use for human activities, including food and fiber production, energy generation, and residential, commercial, and industrial supply, has grown significantly over the past century, driven by rising populations, expanding economic activity, and changes in technologies and consumer demands. Traditional water planning has long assumed that the demand for water, like other resource demands, will grow in perpetuity, shaping infrastructure development, land-use decisions, and water-system investments. However, recent data and analysis challenge this assumption, suggesting that total water use in certain regions and sectors has peaked or even begun to decline, despite continued population and economic growth. This paper’s primary contribution is to reevaluate the status of “peak water” and decoupling based on observational and statistical data, as well as multimodel simulations. Data on global, national, and regional water withdrawals indicate that certain peak water-use levels are being reached and the paper discusses past, current, and projected demand estimates; potential drivers of observed water use reductions; and different strategies for managing and modeling water use in the future. These findings indicate that the long-presumed correlation between water-resource use, economic development, and human well-being can be decoupled and that models of water use should reflect this. Decoupling solutions must focus on efficiency technologies, regulatory water-use caps, environmental flow protections, and enhanced monitoring networks.

title: Music illuminates sociocultural dimensions of autobiographical memory
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Researchers have long theorized that autobiographical memory relies on sociocultural structures, such as life scripts and event schemas. The potency of music as a marker of social and personal identity, combined with its ubiquity in everyday life, allows us to connect these everyday scripts to larger patterns of socially and culturally shaped behavior. We collected free-response descriptions of autobiographical memories evoked by short clips of familiar songs from university undergraduates (n = 233). The songs spanned three popular genres and aligned with two significant periods of listeners’ lives. We analyzed the similarities and differences in the content of memories for particular songs using natural language processing. Memories cued by songs from the same category displayed striking similarities, suggesting that particular types of music cue memories that are similar between listeners but that vary according to characteristics such as music genre and release date. Two control conditions, in which a new set of participants reported memories evoked by key words from the lyrics (n = 121) and short narrative summaries of the lyrics (n = 129), indicate that these results cannot be explained by within-category similarities in the songs’ lyrical content. Instead, we suggest that the intersubjective structure of music-evoked autobiographical memories reflects socioculturally-defined scripts tied to song characteristics such as genre and release date. Thus, while memories may feel idiosyncratic and personal, there are also substantial similarities in life experiences between individuals with broadly similar backgrounds, and these shared experiences can be spontaneously called to mind through the seemingly innocuous act of turning on the radio.

title: isSPA-vesicle: AI-assisted structure determination of membrane proteins on vesicles
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The demand for three-dimensional reconstruction of membrane proteins in native lipid environments has grown substantially in recent years. Both single-particle analysis and tomographic techniques have enabled structural studies across diverse vesicular samples; however, these methods remain limited in either efficiency or resolution. Here, we present an AI-enabled, vesicle geometry-guided 3D reconstruction strategy based on untilted data. Given that some vesicles exhibit anisotropic shapes in solution and adopt near-spherical or ellipsoidal geometries, we trained an AI model to estimate membrane geometric parameters and compute normal vectors based on the fitted ellipsoidal surface. This information facilitates post hoc filtering of particles picked using the isSPA framework based on the angular difference between their orientations and the membrane normals, and also enables the exclusion of particles outside the vesicles. This allows efficient localization of target membrane proteins enabling near-atomic-resolution reconstruction. Using this approach, we efficiently reconstructed membrane proteins ranging from 130 kDa to 2 MDa across two classes of enveloped viruses and three types of synthetic liposomes, achieving 2.7 Å resolution for influenza A virus hemagglutinin and 3.1 Å for the prefusion spike protein of HCoV-OC43. Our method provides a simple and efficient tool for achieving such reconstructions in physiological lipid bilayers.

title: Stature reveals changing patterns of the biological standard of living in Europe and Asia over the past 7,000 y
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Human stature is a valuable indicator of nutritional status and health. Reconstructing this indicator allows insights into which types of societies were providing better health and nutrition—also termed the “biological standard of living” in the literature. Yet, archaeological evidence has not previously been assembled on a scale large enough for systematic comparison across premodern Eurasia. We present a dataset of 18,457 stature observations based on 783 sites from Asia and Europe, roughly spanning the 7,000 y before the twentieth century. Using harmonized estimates derived from long bones, we document broad regional variation in stature over time and examine how these patterns relate to population density and historical indicators of technological development. We observe marked declines in stature in most regions during the 500–1900 CE period, in both Asia and Europe. To interpret these patterns, we combine our stature series with estimates of population density, technological advancement, and related controls. As [Q. Ashraf, O. Galor, Am. Econ. Rev. 101 , 2003–2041 (2011)] predicted, higher technology levels were associated with higher population density, but not correlated with higher stature before the modern era. This relationship also holds after controlling for other potentially confounding factors such as latitude or transport access. By assembling the largest archaeological stature dataset for Eurasia to date and linking it to long-term demographic and historical indicators, this study provides an empirical basis for comparative research on premodern health, nutrition, and population pressure.

title: Automating inequality? Gender bias in AI-mediated labor markets
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Generative AI is rapidly entering labor markets, with large language models (LLMs) now used to help write CVs and evaluate applicants. We study the risks this creates in a series of audit experiments in which applicant gender is randomly assigned while all other information is held constant. We find that LLMs generate gender-stereotypical CVs and exhibit gender bias in screening scores and wage recommendations. Screening scores track occupational gender segregation, penalizing women in male-dominated occupations and favoring them in female-dominated ones. Wage recommendations track occupational gender wage gaps when gender is explicit in the prompt, though this gradient weakens under name-based gender signaling and is sensitive to the LLMs being used. These disparities arise through two channels: evaluation bias, when identical CV content is evaluated differently by gender, and generation bias, when gendered content produced by the model affects later evaluation. Because the same systems shape both CV content and its subsequent assessment, these channels can reinforce one another. Taken together, our findings identify measurable risks of algorithmic amplification in AI-mediated job search.

title: Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth’s surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. By integrating satellite observations with century-scale sedimentary archives from ~2,000 lakes, we reveal a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000. This synchronization, coinciding with converging climatic and socioeconomic pressures, signals a widespread erosion of the spatial heterogeneity and regional distinctiveness that historically characterized inland waters. We propose that increasing lake synchrony represents an emergent property of the Anthropocene, transforming lakes from regionally structured, asynchronous waterscapes into dynamically coupled planetary commons. By temporally aligning carbon and nutrient dynamics across broad spatial scales, this synchronization modifies the timing and amplitude of aggregate biophysical fluxes, altering how inland waters interact with larger-scale environmental cycles. Ultimately, this finding motivates a macroscale monitoring framework that jointly tracks synchrony, modularity, and their functional consequences, demanding a shift in governance toward preserving the ecological heterogeneity essential for maintaining long-term environmental stability.

title: Coupled human–cattle mobility shaped the socioeconomic landscapes of the Holocene Middle Nile Valley
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: We present a synthesis of strontium isotope data ( 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) from human and cattle dental enamel across Middle Nile. This dataset, which combines newly acquired and published measurements, reveals a complex history of human and cattle mobility linked to ecological gradients and sociocultural changes in this part of the continent. During the early Holocene (8,000 to 4,000 BCE), isotopic unanimity in human and cattle remains supports early, correlated mobility of humans and Bos , extending beyond Nile floodplains to adjacent uplands. In the mid-Holocene (4,000 to 1,000 BCE), isotopic data from Wadi Howar suggest bidirectional corridors for mobility of both species linking the Middle Nile and the Western Desert. This pattern correlates with the emergence of the Middle Nile civilizations in which cattle played a central cultural and economic role. From the first millennium BCE onward, a radical change can be observed, correlated with the progressive desertification processes in the Sahel. Although cattle import routes continued to follow wadi systems, they shifted south of the now desiccated Saharan lakes toward Kordofan. The long-term perspective emphasizes the continuous adaptation of societies in the Middle Nile of what is now Sudan and adjacent regions to environmental changes, aimed at maintaining sustained access to cattle, a resource that remained crucial for Middle Nile communities throughout the Holocene.

title: The broad-spectrum RumC1 bacteriocin targets a transient peptidoglycan intermediate of the nascent cell wall
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Ruminoccocin C1 (RumC1) is a structurally unique bacteriocin with broad-spectrum efficacy, including against multidrug-resistant pathogens, yet acting by an undefined mechanism. By integrating genetics, biochemistry, computational modeling, and single-cell fluorescence microscopy, we demonstrate that RumC1 is a distinct cell-wall-targeting toxin. First, all RumC1-resistant mutants isolated through a high-rate, genome-wide mutagenic screening exhibited specific impairments in peptidoglycan homeostasis regulation, pinpointing this pathway as critical for RumC1 activity. Second, RumC1 selectively accumulates within neosynthesized peptidoglycan, leading to cell growth arrest and death in a dose-dependent manner. Third, we characterize the RumI c 1 immunity protein of the RumC1 biosynthetic cluster as a peptidase acting at the cell surface to protect the cells by trimming the stem peptide crucial for cell-wall assembly. As such, RumI c 1 provides cross-protection against vancomycin, while RumC1 is demonstrated to act differently from this glycopeptide antibiotic. Collectively, these findings establish RumC1 as a toxin targeting a key peptidoglycan intermediate of cell wall maturation, which defines a distinct mode of action among the large and highly diverse repertoire of bacteriocins characterized so far.

title: Direct CO 2 splitting using light-based catalysis and an oxygen reservoir
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: As the dominant anthropogenic greenhouse gas, the conversion of CO 2 into value-added products is vital for achieving a circular economy. CO 2 activation typically requires coreactants, high temperatures, or significant electrical input, any of which increases cost or limits scalability. Here we demonstrate a straightforward way to split CO 2 directly into carbon monoxide and oxygen using light. By combining a light-driven antenna-reactor photocatalyst with a material that acts as an oxygen reservoir, CO 2 can be decomposed directly into CO and oxygen with light only. Under illumination, photoexcited carriers induce CO 2 bond dissociation, while cerium oxide adsorbs the released oxygen into vacancy sites, preventing recombination. The oxygen can then be released from the ceria by flowing nitrogen under white light illumination, a process that can be repeated multiple times, restoring full photocatalytic activity. This demonstrates a practical and scalable strategy for efficient CO 2 conversion, shifting the chemical equilibrium of CO 2 dissociation in a controllable manner.

title: Chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 participates in the internalization of arginine-rich dipeptide repeat proteins
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Microsatellite repeat expansion of the 5′ GGGGCC 3′ sequence in the C9orf72 gene is the most common monogenic form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. Dipeptide repeat proteins (DPRs) translated from the mutant allele can be detected in postmortem brains of afflicted individuals. The arginine containing peptides, poly proline-arginine (poly-PR) and poly glycine-arginine (poly-GR), are particularly noxious to cells. Both can undergo cell-to-cell transmission, but underlying mechanisms are not understood. We found rapid internalization and nucleolar localization of bath-applied hemagglutinin (HA) tagged poly-PR with twenty repeats (HA-PR 20 ) in cell lines and neurons. Small molecule and RNAi approaches implicated a temperature-dependent, fluid phase endocytosis mechanism for HA-PR 20 . We sought to identify DPR-related cell surface uptake factors using µMap high-resolution proximity labeling. DPR–iridium conjugates identified candidate cell-surface proteins which were interrogated in a secondary RNAi screen. Focusing on our strongest candidate, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4 (CSPG4), we showed cellular uptake of HA-PR 20 is reduced by inhibition of glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis and knockdown or ablation of CSPG4. Knockdown of CSPG4 protected PR 20 -induced neuronal toxicity. Using a dual reporter system to interrogate in vitro neuron-to-neuron transmission of PR 50, we found PR 50 synthesized by one neuron readily spread to neighboring cells. Transmission was significantly reduced with CSPG4 knockdown. Similarly conditioned media from PR 50 or GR 50 expressing neurons contained transmissible protein that was internalized into neurons in a CSPG4-dependent manner. These results suggest CSPG4 participates in poly-PR/poly-GR internalization and transmission.

title: Gaplinc regulates myeloid metabolic pathways in trans in endotoxic shock
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) Gaplinc is a known regulator of the innate immune response; however, the systemic mechanisms governing its influence on survival during endotoxic shock remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Gaplinc as a dosage-dependent immune and metabolic rheostat. While Gaplinc knockout (KO) mice exhibit elevated baseline immune response genes (IRGs) and resistance to lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced shock, we demonstrate that transgenic Gaplinc overexpression produces the opposite phenotype: suppressed baseline IRGs, diminished nuclear p65, and hypersensitivity to endotoxemia. Analysis of heterozygous and rescue models reveals that Gaplinc functions in trans and is haploinsufficient, requiring strict transcript dosage to maintain wild-type immune homeostasis. To uncover the mechanistic basis of this survival advantage, we performed RNA Antisense Purification (RAP-MS) and identified the mitochondrial enzyme MCCC1 as a primary Gaplinc binding partner. Loss of Gaplinc drives systemic metabolic reprogramming, characterized by reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and a protective lipidome featuring elevated lysophosphatidylcholines and diminished free fatty acids. Finally, while myeloid-specific conditional KOs confer partial protection against LPS-induced hypothermia, tissue-wide expression mapping and sex-dimorphic clinical chemistries suggest a broader, multisystemic role for the lncRNA. Collectively, these data demonstrate that Gaplinc bridges transcriptomic immune regulation with systemic lipid and metabolic output, dictating survival outcomes in systemic inflammation.

title: Vessel noise pollution offsets marine mammal energy budgets
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Shipping is a major global source of underwater noise pollution and is frequently reported to alter the behavior of marine mammals. However, the energetic consequences of these noise-induced behavioral disruptions and their implications for population fitness remain poorly quantified. Using behavioral proxies of energy acquisition and expenditure derived from high-resolution sound and movement tags on 28 wild harbor porpoises, we estimate that porpoises decrease energy acquisition by 20% (range: 1 to 36%) during high-noise vessel exposures, while maintaining constant energy expenditure. With a median of 11 high-noise vessel exposures per day, these disruptions may result in an average daily shortfall of 4.6% of their net energy budget. Sustained over time, such noise-induced energetic deficits have the potential to compromise individual fitness, ultimately affecting the dynamics of harbor porpoise populations in industrialized coastal areas worldwide and reducing their functional carrying capacity. This framework establishes a direct mechanistic link between behavioral disruption and fitness-relevant impacts, providing a biologically grounded metric for predicting population-level outcomes of noise pollution and an objective basis for defining acceptable exposure levels of vessel noise for wild marine mammal populations. Moreover, it is scalable across species and ecosystems and offers a common currency for assessing the cumulative effects of multiple stressors in the Anthropocene oceans. As vessel traffic and its associated noise outputs continue to increase globally, our results offer timely insights for evidence-based management, and support efforts to balance the societal demand for low-cost maritime transport with the responsibility to ensure the sustainable use and conservation of marine biodiversity.

title: Leptin Receptor + cells create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis in the bone marrow by synthesizing CXCL14
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Leptin Receptor-expressing (LepR + ) stromal cells in the bone marrow are a critical source of growth factors for the maintenance of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and most restricted hematopoietic progenitors. An important unresolved question is whether they also regulate terminal differentiation in some hematopoietic cells. We found that bone marrow LepR + cells promote thrombopoiesis by synthesizing the chemokine CXCL14. Cxcl14 -expressing LepR + cells extend fine processes that wrap around perisinusoidal megakaryocytes. Deletion of Cxcl14 from LepR + cells did not significantly alter HSC function or most aspects of bone marrow hematopoiesis, including megakaryocyte generation; however, it significantly reduced the numbers of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes in the bone marrow and platelets in the blood, as well as platelet quality. Megakaryocytes from Lepr-cre; Cxcl14 fl/fl mice expressed lower levels of genes that encode granule proteins as compared to control mice, leading to the release of platelets with fewer α-granules and defective thrombus formation/growth. CXCL14 promoted platelet formation by remodeling lipid metabolism in megakaryocytes, increasing fatty acid transporter expression and enabling megakaryocytes to take up more polyunsaturated fatty acids from circulation. A high fat diet rescued the formation of proplatelet-forming megakaryocytes and platelets, as well as platelet function, in Lepr-cre; Cxcl14 fl/fl mice. CXCL14 protein was sufficient to promote platelet formation by megakaryocytes in vitro and in vivo. LepR + cells thus create a perisinusoidal niche for thrombopoiesis by producing CXCL14, which regulates lipid metabolism and terminal differentiation in megakaryocytes.

title: The evolution and function of eukaryote-to-cyanobacteria horizontal gene transfer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Prokaryote-to-eukaryote horizontal gene transfer (HGT) has emerged as a driver of eukaryotic evolution. In contrast, eukaryote-to-prokaryote HGT remains poorly characterized, limiting insight into how eukaryote-derived genes influence prokaryotic evolution and function. Here, we reconstructed a comprehensive and well-resolved phylogeny of 469 high-quality Cyanobacteria genomes spanning all orders. Leveraging this framework, we identified 204 candidate functionally diverse genes of eukaryotic origin in cyanobacteria, likely representing 59 putative transfer events, including 197 genes not previously documented. All 204 candidates were intronless, consistent with intron loss during their evolutionary history. Transcriptomics reveal that HGT-acquired genes are expressed at significantly higher levels than both genome-wide and functionally matched non-HGT-acquired genes, suggesting functional importance. Notably, 138 genes exhibited functional annotations absent from the host cyanobacteria. We further characterized a granule-bound starch synthase (GBSS) putatively acquired by Crocosphaera from an ancestral archaeplastid lineage, enabling starch synthesis that may facilitate energy storage for nocturnal nitrogen fixation. These findings reveal that eukaryote-to-prokaryote gene transfer is an underappreciated driver of cyanobacterial evolution and function, with broad implications for microbial ecology, functional adaptation, and cross-domain genetic exchange.
